en.anleitungen/ki-assistent-aufgaben.md:
---
key: guide.mcp_tasks
titel: What an AI assistant can do
routen: [/mein-konto/app]
reihe: 51
stichworte:
  [
    AI,
    assistant,
    Claude,
    ChatGPT,
    website,
    draft,
    design,
    menu,
    upload images,
    alternative text,
    chronicle,
    letterhead,
    Instagram,
    Facebook,
  ]
---

Once an AI assistant is connected ([Connect AI assistants to HUBIplan](/hilfe/ki-assistent-verbinden)), it can read the website and edit it as a draft. Publishing happens only in HUBIplan, by a person.

- Design, menu and home page: choose design, colours, fine-tuning, header image and header image for phones, arrange the menu (headings, external links, button) and add, move or hide custom home page sections. This needs the “Manage website” permission and goes into the draft. Switching blocks on or off is only possible in HUBIplan.
- Title image and image carousel: the assistant can set the large image at the top of the home page (image or image carousel of the greeting) and the image at the top of a text page, for example “Use the new photo of the parade as the title image”. This also goes into the draft. If the image has no alternative text, it points this out.
- Sections on text pages: text pages are built from sections like the home page. The assistant can add, change, move or hide tiles, text with image, buttons, contacts and the other section kinds there, for example “Show the four ways to join on the ‘Get involved’ page as tiles”. The right “Edit content” is enough; everything goes into the page draft.
- Introductions of the sections: the assistant can write the introduction above the board, events, sub-units and gallery as well as the box next to the contact form, even if it does not exist yet, for example “Write next to the contact form when we can be reached at the clubhouse”. The new introduction goes into the draft under Website › Texts.
- Upload images: write, for example, “I want to upload photos from the summer festival”. The assistant gives you a link that is valid for 30 minutes and up to 20 images. Open it on your phone or PC and choose the photos; they go straight to HUBIplan, not through the chat, and end up under Website › Images.
- Describe images: the assistant sees the images in a small size and suggests alternative text and caption; it only enters the creator if you name them. For images already on the website it only fills in missing texts; you change existing ones yourself. It does not recognise or name people.
- Images by address: HUBIplan fetches an image itself from servers you approve under [Website › Web address](/webseite/domain) at “Images for AI assistants” (such as the club’s Nextcloud). The source (creator and licence) goes into the “Creator” field. Without an entry this is not possible.
- Appearance: change colours with names and use, further colours, gradients, colour roles and the logo (from an image under Website › Images). This applies immediately to HUBIplan and the website, there is no draft; the assistant asks first. Any change can be taken back in the change log with “Undo”. This is not included by default: when connecting, tick the appearance under “Also allow”. It also needs the permission for the appearance.
- Letterhead: view and change layout, logo and logo size, a logo only for letters (from an image under Website › Images), name next to the logo, fonts, line and table colours, title colour and footer for the Word template and PDF letters, also for sub-units with their own letterhead. This applies immediately to new letters and invoices; the assistant asks first.
- The assistant can only read the texts of the letterhead (name in the letterhead, additional line, salutation, closing); you change them yourself under Settings › Letterhead. That way no slipped-in text (such as false bank details) reaches invoices through the assistant. This is not included by default either: when connecting, tick the letterhead under “Also allow”. It needs the permission to edit the unit.
- Chronicle: view the introduction and the timeline entries, add new entries (also many at once, for example from an anniversary publication), change entries, assign or remove images, e.g. “Add the events from this anniversary booklet to our chronicle”. Everything goes into the draft; publishing happens under [Chronicle](/chronik). This needs the “Chronicle” module and the “Maintain chronicle” permission (or editing website content). The chronicle only names living people if they have not objected; HUBIplan does not check this in the text itself.
- Posts for Instagram or Facebook: the assistant stores text and images as a draft under [Website › Social media](/webseite/beitraege). There you copy the text, save the images and post yourself; HUBIplan publishes nothing on Meta.

New images only become public once they are in a published text or section.
en.anleitungen/ki-assistent-sicher-nutzen.m:
---
key: guide.mcp_safety
titel: Using AI assistants safely
routen: [/mein-konto/app]
reihe: 52
stichworte: [AI, assistant, privacy, provider, confidential, access, limits, decline]
---

A connected AI assistant may never do more than you yourself. What to look out for:

What you write to the assistant and what it reads goes to its provider. Do not put confidential data there. Without signing in, an assistant can only read the HUBIplan help at `/api/mcp/`.

When you grant access, HUBIplan always shows where it goes and since when the assistant is registered here. If the link came by email or message and you did not start the connection yourself, decline, even for well-known assistants. To keep an assistant from running away, limits apply: at most 5 open upload links per person, images from addresses at most 20 per hour and 200 MB per day and unit, very long answers are shortened.

You can disconnect at any time under [My account › App & other instances](/mein-konto/app).
en.anleitungen/ki-assistent-verbinden.md:
---
key: guide.mcp_connect
titel: Connect AI assistants to HUBIplan
routen: [/mein-konto/app]
reihe: 50
stichworte: [AI, Claude, ChatGPT, MCP, assistant, connector, website, draft, write texts]
---

An AI assistant such as Claude or ChatGPT can read your unit's website and edit it as a draft: texts, home page, design and menu. Publishing happens only in HUBIplan, by a person. The assistant may never do more than you yourself; member data, emails and payments are not available through it.

Once beforehand (board or role management):

1. Switch on the “AI assistants” module under [Settings › Modules](/einstellungen/module). It needs the website.
2. Under [Settings › Roles and permissions](/einstellungen/rollen), give the suitable role the extra permission “Connect AI assistants”.
3. Anyone who wants to connect needs two-factor sign-in (My account › Sign-in & security).

Connecting:

1. Open [My account › App & other instances](/mein-konto/app) and copy the address under “AI assistants”, e.g. `https://verein.example.org/api/mcp/verein/`.
2. Enter it in the assistant as a new connection (depending on the assistant “connector”, “integration” or “MCP server”).
3. The assistant opens HUBIplan in the browser. Sign in with password and code, choose the unit and click **Allow**.

Before allowing, check the address under “Access goes to”: that is where your rights go. Anyone can give an assistant any name. If HUBIplan warns that the address does not belong to any known assistant, only allow it if you have just set up the connection yourself. If the link came by email or message, click **Decline**.

Then you can write to the assistant, for example: “Revise the ‘About us’ text on our website and make it friendlier.” The assistant saves the draft and gives you a link to the preview. If you like the result, you publish it in HUBIplan under Website. Every change appears in the change log with “KI-Assistent” and can be undone.

You get an email for every new connection. A connection is valid for at most 30 days and ends after 14 days without use, and also when you change your password or lose the permission. You can disconnect it at any time under [My account › App & other instances](/mein-konto/app) with **Disconnect**.

More: [What an AI assistant can do](/hilfe/ki-assistent-aufgaben) and [Using AI assistants safely](/hilfe/ki-assistent-sicher-nutzen).

key: guide.member_admit
titel: Admit a new member
modul: members
rechte: [members.edit]
routen: [/mitglieder]
reihe: 10
stichworte: [admission, joining, new, join, create, organisation, company, supporting member]
---

Before you start: there is at least one membership type (Members › Setup › Membership types).

1. In the [member list](/mitglieder), click **Admit member**.
2. Enter surname, first name and date of birth and click **Next**. HUBIplan checks whether the
   person already exists, for example from another club. The date of birth is optional; without
   it, HUBIplan only looks for members of your own club with the same name, and age-based fee
   levels, birthdays and ages are left out for this person.
3. If there are **Possible matches**, choose the right person or **None of these – create a new person**.
4. Choose the **Membership type** and the **Joining date**. The membership number is
   optional: if you leave it empty, HUBIplan assigns the next free number (the highest existing
   number in the club plus 1, including former members; numbers with letters do not count).
5. Add contact details and address and click **Admit**. For a person who already exists, the
   existing shared contact details stay as they are; your entries only fill empty fields. You can
   change them afterwards in the member record.

![The “Admit member” form](bild:mitglieder-aufnehmen)

Required fields are marked “(required)”. If something is missing, “Please fill in this field.” appears below the field and the cursor moves to the first empty required field.

If sub-units cannot be loaded, a message offers **Reload**. You can retrieve the choices again without losing names or other details you have already entered.

Admission has two stages: **1. Person** and **2. Membership and contact**. After **Next**, keyboard focus moves to the new heading or **Possible matches**. **change** returns to the retained personal details. Optional sub-units form a named selection group; a group error is described and receives focus there.

![Second stage with membership, sub-units and contact details](bild:mitglieder-aufnehmen-details)

## An organisation as a member

A company, another club, a town or a public body can also be a member. In the first stage, under
**The member is**, choose **an organisation (company, association, public body …)**.
Instead of surname, first name and date of birth, fill in **Name of the organisation**,
optionally a **Name addition** (such as a branch) and the **Legal form (optional)**.
HUBIplan then checks whether an organisation with this name already exists. In the second stage
you can add the register, VAT ID and website; the address is the organisation's address.

Organisations have no age bands for fees: the amount of the membership type applies, for example
a separate type “Supporting member (company)”. Birthdays and the age and gender statistics leave
organisations out, and only a person can hold an office.

key: guide.module_toggle
titel: Enable a module for a unit
modul: platform
rechte: [platform.manage]
routen: [/plattform]
stichworte: [module, enable, website, competitions, titles, member area, template, pass down]
---

The platform administration releases modules. The club switches released modules off and on again itself under [Settings › Modules](/einstellungen/module). Anyone who misses a feature that is not released contacts the platform administration.

1. Open [Platform](/plattform) and choose the unit.
2. In the **Released modules** section, tick what the unit may use, such as website, competitions or entries. The modules are listed by group, each with a short note on what it contains. If a module needs another one (music, meetings and volunteer duties need events, music also the sheet music archive), that one is ticked as well; if you untick it, the dependent modules go too.
3. Save. The change applies immediately to everyone in the unit.

A switched-off module disappears from the menu; its data is kept. Public parts go offline, such as card verification, the public document folder or the social media posts on the website.

Smaller features are modules of their own too, so a small club only sees what it needs: tasks, documents, circulars, membership cards, member area, honours & anniversaries, titles, chronicle, calls, bookings, social media, tax & charitable status (tax areas and reserves), donation receipts, the sheet music archive, which a choir can use without music, and shooting sports (targets, photo evaluation, bird shooting) as part of competitions. The member area matches the switch under Members › Setup › Member area & photos; both stay in step.

When you create a unit, a template (such as marksmen's club, music society / band, choir, sports club, support association, federation) suggests suitable modules and the name for sub-units; everything can be changed freely afterwards. For a federation, the platform administration can allow it to release modules to its clubs itself; it then finds the tick boxes when editing the club under [Sub-units](/untereinheiten).

---
key: guide.passkey
titel: Sign in with a passkey
routen: [/mein-konto/anmeldung]
reihe: 21
stichworte: [passkey, fingerprint, face, PIN, passwordless, WebAuthn, security, 2FA]
---

With a passkey you sign in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN. You need neither a
password nor a code. A passkey counts as two-factor authentication. It is stored on your phone
or computer or in your password manager and only works on the right site, so a fake site cannot
capture it.

## Set up a passkey

1. Open [Sign-in & security](/mein-konto/anmeldung) under **My account**.
2. In the **Passkeys** section, enter a name if you like, e.g. “Phone”.
3. Click **Add passkey** and confirm with your password.
4. Your browser or phone asks for your fingerprint, face or PIN. The passkey is then saved.
5. If this is your first second factor, HUBIplan shows **Recovery codes**. Keep them safe in
   case your device is ever missing.

A passkey only works for the address where you set it up. If you use HUBIplan under several
addresses, set up a separate passkey under each address. The list shows which address a passkey
works for.

## Sign in

On the sign-in page, click **Sign in with passkey**. Many browsers also suggest the passkey
directly in the email address field. If you sign in with your password, you can choose
**Confirm with passkey** instead of entering the code. Under a different address the passkey is
not offered; the sign-in page then names the address it is valid for, and you enter the code.

HUBIplan also asks for the passkey for sensitive actions. With **Enter code** you use a code
from your authenticator app or a recovery code instead.

## Lost your device?

Sign in with your password and a recovery code and remove the old passkey with **Remove**.
Without codes, the board can reset your two-factor authentication. If your passkey is stored
with Google, Apple, Microsoft or in a password manager, it is usually already available on a
new device with the same account.

## In the app

In the HUBIplan app, tap **Sign in with passkey** when connecting and enter your club’s
address. The same passkey as in the browser works if it is stored with Google, Apple or in your
password manager.

- Android: The phone asks for your fingerprint, face or PIN straight away. You can also open
  **Administration** with “Unlock with passkey” instead of your password and code.
- iPhone: The app opens your club’s sign-in page. Sign in there with
  **Sign in with passkey** and tap **Connect**. You unlock **Administration** the same way with
  “Unlock with passkey”: sign in, check that the device is right and tap **Unlock**.

If it does not work, connect the app as before with the QR code under **My account** › App &
other instances.

![Starting point: Sign in with a passkey](bild:konto-passwort)

1. Open the home page.

3. Drag a block to its new place.
4. Hide or show a block with **Show** and choose under **Width** how much room it gets. For tiles such as “Finances at a glance”, “Current registrations” or “Surveys and noticeboard”, choose between **when relevant**, **always** and **never** under **Show**.

The home page in the member area can be customised the same way. There are tiles for open work hours, unanswered surveys, new noticeboard posts, your own registrations, running group orders and, with shooting sports, your own shooting record. titel: Create an event and invite members
modul: events
rechte: [events.manage]
routen: [/termine]
reihe: 10
stichworte: [event, invitation, series, RSVP]
---

1. Open [Events](/termine) and click **New event** (or a day in the calendar).
2. Enter title, date, time and place; for regular meetings choose a repetition. The dialog asks in this order: title, when, where, category and who sees the event. The header and the bar with **Create event** stay in place while you scroll.
3. Choose who is invited and whether acceptances and declines are collected.
4. Click **Create event**.

If the end time is not yet known, enable **Hide end time on the website** under **More settings**.
The website then shows only the start time; the entered end time is kept in the internal calendar.
For a recurring event, the setting applies to all occurrences.

If the event is only for a sub-unit that does not manage its own events (for example a platoon without its own access), choose it under **Event for**.
Then only its members are invited, and you keep managing the event in the unit's calendar.
Sub-units that manage themselves create their own events.

Attach files: Open the saved event. In the **Attachments** row under **For this event**, + **Add file** uploads a file (PDF, JPEG or PNG, at most 15 MB), and **From the document store** attaches an existing document; the event then always shows its newest version.
For a recurring event, the attachments apply to all occurrences.

Invitees receive an email and accept or decline there or in the member area.

key: guide.bank_fetch
titel: Fetch transactions directly from the bank
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.edit]
routen: [/finanzen/kontoauszuege]
reihe: 105
stichworte: [bank, FinTS, HBCI, transactions, fetch, PIN, TAN, bank access, online banking]
---

Instead of downloading a file from online banking, HUBIplan can fetch the transactions from the bank itself. For this the bank connection must be set up on the server and switched on for the club under Settings › Modules.

## Set up once

1. Under Finance › Accounts, enter the IBAN for the bank account.
2. Open [Finance › Bank statements](/finanzen/kontoauszuege) and click **Add bank access**.
3. Enter a name, the bank code (BLZ), the FinTS address of your bank and your login name for online banking. The bank states the FinTS address (also “HBCI with PIN/TAN”) on its website or by phone.
4. Enter your PIN and click **Sign in to the bank**. If the bank offers several approval methods, choose the one you also use in online banking.

HUBIplan then links the accounts whose IBAN the bank lists for this access.

## Fetch transactions

1. Click **Fetch transactions** next to the bank access and enter your PIN.
2. If the bank asks for an approval, type in the TAN or confirm in your bank’s app. With approval in the app, HUBIplan continues by itself.
3. The new transactions then appear as a statement in the list, with suggestions as for an imported file.

HUBIplan fetches from the last fetch onwards, the first time the last 90 days. Transactions that have already been imported, also from a file, are not added twice.

## Your PIN

Your PIN is entered anew for every fetch. HUBIplan does not store it. If the bank rejects the sign-in, HUBIplan asks before the next attempt; after two rejections the access is paused for 24 hours so that the bank does not block it.

---
key: guide.two_factor
titel: Set up two-factor authentication
routen: [/mein-konto/anmeldung]
reihe: 20
stichworte: [2FA, authenticator, phone, code, TOTP, security]
---

You need an authenticator app on your phone, for example FreeOTP, Aegis or Google Authenticator.

1. Open [Sign-in & security](/mein-konto/anmeldung) under **My account**.
2. In the **Two-factor authentication** section, scan the QR code with the app. If you set it up on
   the phone that runs the app, tap **Open in authenticator app** instead or copy the key.
3. Enter the **Code from the app** and **Your password for confirmation**.
4. Click **Activate**.
5. Keep the **Recovery codes** that appear in a safe place, for example printed. Each code
   works once if you don't have your phone. **Copy codes** and **Save as text file** let you
   store them straight away.

You can view the codes again later in the same section with **Show recovery codes**. If they are
used up or have fallen into the wrong hands, create new ones with **Generate new codes**; the
previous ones then stop working.

![The “Two-factor authentication” section with the QR code](bild:konto-zwei-faktor)

Club logo in the app: The QR code contains your club's logo. Some apps such as FreeOTP show it
as the icon. Others, for example Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 2FAS or Aegis, show
the initials instead. In Aegis you can choose your own image for the entry, in 2FAS you can change
the letters and colour. An entry
you already set up only changes when you set up two-factor authentication again.

## Confirming sensitive actions

For some actions HUBIplan asks again for a current code from the app if your last code is
older than 10 minutes: full exports and spin-offs, assigning roles or extending their rights,
resetting another person's two-factor authentication, creating the QR code for the HUBIplan app
and permanent deletion (club, former member, name in the chronicle). A recovery code works too,
and with a passkey set up, the passkey (see “Sign in with a passkey”).
If you have not set up two-factor authentication yet, you confirm with your password during the
transition period.

Platform administration has no transition period: without two-factor authentication its
rights are paused until you set it up here. Anyone else with a permission in a club or
department has 3 days; the deadline is shown at the top of every page. During that time,
circulars, exports and posting in the treasury are already paused, afterwards all permissions.
Your own member area does not need a second factor.

## Trends

Shows how the unit's membership has developed: joiners, leavers and age structure in the selected period.

Under **Cut-off date** it counts the members on one day by age, gender and place of residence, also as PDF, Excel or CSV for a report.

## Entries

Register members of the unit for competitions that are open for entries.

Downloads the unit's data, optionally with files as a ZIP. The export runs in the background; the list below shows when it is ready.
en.seiten/aufgaben-erinnerungen.md:
---
key: page.todo_reminders
titel: Tasks › Personal music reminders
modul: music
rechte: [todos.view]
routen: [/aufgaben/erinnerungen]
stichworte: [Reminder, sheet music return, maintenance, equipment]
---

In Tasks › **Personal music reminders**, enable private tasks for your own sheet music returns and equipment returns and maintenance. Choose zero to 30 days ahead; overdue records are included. Your choice saves itself; tasks are reconciled then and hourly. Equipment still requires inventory read access; department equipment is excluded. Enabling requires task read and edit permission. You cannot select another recipient. Each task links directly to its source record. Notifications use your existing task settings. Unchanged tasks are completed after a recorded return or changed/completed maintenance. Your edits, completions and deletions are preserved; only a new due date creates another task. Disabling completes unchanged automatically created tasks. A review task does not itself record return or maintenance.
en.seiten/aufgaben.md:
---
key: page.aufgaben
titel: Tasks
rechte: [todos.view]
routen: [/aufgaben]
stichworte: [Todo, Tasks]
---

In the overview, tasks appear directly below the status controls and filter. “New task” sits beside the heading. Below the list, notices for tasks without a responsible account and incoming tasks from other installations appear only when there are entries, with a count. Loading errors remain visible with a retry action. Adopting the last entry removes its notice. The export action is below the list. Authorised role managers can also open “Administration” there to configure retention of shared tasks. This section is initially collapsed.

## Own and shared tasks

Create personal tasks with a title and an optional description and due date. Personal tasks are private. After creation, edits are saved automatically. Completed tasks appear under Done. Deleted tasks can be restored from the trash for 30 days. Export personal tasks downloads your private tasks.

Shared tasks are also visible to selected people or current role holders. View permission allows reading; edit permission also allows changes and completion. Only the responsible account can delete or transfer responsibility. Under My account › Notifications, disable email and push notices when tasks are shared. Authorised role managers can take over orphaned shared tasks when the responsible account permanently loses access; personal tasks remain hidden. The outbox stores only a neutral delivery record for task notices.

## Reminders and notifications

Configure email and push under My account › Notifications. For each task with a due date, choose reminder times and channels or disable notices. Responsible participants are reminded; without an assignment, all participants with edit permission are reminded. Date-only deadlines last until the end of the day and reminders arrive at 8 am; timed deadlines use their exact time. Overdue tasks receive exactly one additional notice at 8 am the next day. Highlighting in HUBIplan remains active independently of email and push. Optionally move completed one-off tasks to the trash after twelve months; this is off by default. Recurring task history is excluded. In your profile, personal tasks can still be exported or permanently deleted after a role ends.

## Attachments

Under Attachments, upload multiple files by selecting them or dropping them in the upload area. Each file may be up to 20 MB; the document repository’s file types and safety checks apply. Restore removed attachments from the attachment trash for 30 days. Document links grant no additional repository permissions: without access, only a placeholder appears. The personal export downloads a ZIP file with tasks, settings and authorised files, including your private tasks after a role ends.

## Recurring tasks

Under Repeat, choose daily, weekly, monthly or yearly occurrences with an interval and an optional end date or total count. Completing a task creates exactly one next occurrence. Month-end dates and 29 February retain their original anchor; late completion skips past due dates. Choose whether the interval starts from the previous due date or from completion. Content changes can apply only to this occurrence or to all following ones. Document links and personal reminder rules are inherited; uploaded files are not. Reopening or undoing an occurrence may retract its successor only while it is untouched. End series keeps an existing open occurrence; the series trash deletes and restores the entire history without creating an extra occurrence.

For recurring tasks, Transfer responsibility applies to the entire shared history and future continuation. If earlier private occurrences remain, the transfer is rejected to protect their contents; review their sharing permissions explicitly first.

## Share with other units

Use Target unit to share with allowed neighbouring levels on the same instance. Add same-named roles explicitly for the displayed units; units added later are not included automatically. A shared task is completed once for everyone. With a separate occurrence for each unit, each target unit owns its own copy and, for recurring tasks, an independent sequence. The distribution mode is fixed after sharing. Local editors manage notes, attachments and participants within their unit. Titles, descriptions and due dates remain controlled centrally.

The source receives only progress, including the local occurrence number, due date, completion time and account. Central updates affect open copies while preserving local additions and completed history. Removing a target unit or deleting the source stops future occurrences and access to source attachments; the target unit retains its local data. When it revokes a local share, current permissions also apply to files, undo and reminders. For shared tasks, undo uses the authorised target context.

## Tasks linked to events

Link a task to an event in your own calendar. In the event, the “Tasks” row under “For this event” has two buttons: “+ Create” creates a new task for the event, “Show” opens the filtered task view. The task owner can change or remove the link under “Linked event”. Calendar and task permissions remain independent: linking does not share either object. Without calendar permission, only “Event unavailable” appears. Deleting the event keeps the task and removes its link. Due dates do not move automatically with the event. A recurring event is linked as a whole series, rather than an individual occurrence.

## Member tasks

The responsible account can explicitly select current members under “Share in the member portal” (view only or allowed to complete) or publish an open offer. Current unit members can view an offer; department offers are limited to their members. Exactly one person can claim it, complete it or release an open claim. Every read, change and file download checks current membership, portal access and task publication. Members receive no administration rights and cannot change titles, due dates or participants. Document references grant no additional repository access.

Publication initially applies only to the selected occurrence. Explicitly enabling “Also share following occurrences in the member portal” copies it into future occurrences; offers become available to claim again. Completing and reopening preserve the existing protections for subsequent occurrences. Assigned members allowed to complete, or the member who claimed an offer, receive reminders according to their notification preferences.

Use “My area › Tasks” to view open and completed tasks. Mail and push links select the matching portal access. Revoked access, ended membership or a disabled portal prevents further access.

## Creating tasks

“New task” opens a dialog. “Close” is in a separate dialog header. Enter the title, description, due date and sharing before creating the task. After “Create”, the same dialog stays open for attachments, reminders, recurrence and member access; “Done” closes it. Existing tasks save as usual and unsaved access settings are checked before closing. The description uses a wide, resizable text field. Status and filters share one row on larger screens and wrap on smaller screens.

## Tasks across separate installations

In the task dialog, **Share with another installation** selects a confirmed connection. Enable the task packet in the connection and have the receiving side accept it first. Each task also needs its own explicit grant. New offers appear under **Tasks from other installations** and must be adopted by a responsible local account.

- **Separate copy with independent completion**: Each receiving unit completes independently. The source only sees occurrence, deadline and progress; local notes, additional attachments and account names are not returned. Open copies receive central content changes. Completed copies retain their content. Revocation stops further updates and future occurrences; adopted content stays local. Source attachments still require a current grant.
- **One jointly completed task**: Reading and completion are checked at the source. Completion applies across installations; reload after a version conflict. An unreachable source cannot confirm a new completion state. Revocation, a paused connection or an unconfirmed key change removes access.

After adoption, local task permissions apply. Another board member does not automatically gain access. The source controls whether the receiving side may complete a task. The distribution mode cannot be changed after the first grant. Future occurrences require **Also share future occurrences**. Separate copies then have independent local sequences; jointly completed tasks create successors at the source.

## List and controls

The task list uses table rows for title, deadline and actions. The title is a link; clicking the free area of a row also opens the task. The checkbox only changes completion. The trash icon on the right moves a task to trash; the restore icon returns it from trash. On narrow screens, the deadline appears below the title.

If the music module is switched on, **Personal music reminders** at the top right leads to your reminders for sheet music returns and equipment returns and maintenance. They appear as private tasks.
en.seiten/belegung.md:
---
key: page.bookings
titel: Bookings and booking calendars
rechte: [bookings.view, bookings.edit, infrastructure.view, material.view]
routen: [/belegung]
stichworte: [Booking, Booking calendar, Reservation, Request, Approval, Set-up time, Hall]
---

Equipment & rooms › **Bookings** shows when facilities and material with a booking calendar are in use. The week
view has one row per item. At the top you switch between **Week**, **Month** and **Year** and move
on with the buttons next to it. The month view shows every day of the month side by side (the full
text appears as a tooltip), the year view shows the number of booked days per month; click it to
open that month.

Switch on a booking calendar: On the detail page of a facility or a material item, the
managers switch on booking under **Booking calendar**. There you also decide whether bookings
need approval, how much set-up time stays free before and after, and how far ahead
people may book.

## In detail

Book: Choose **Book**, then the item, the purpose and the time. A booking can repeat
weekly, monthly or yearly. Instead of a time you can choose an event or a competition;
the booking then follows it when it is moved or cancelled. Booking a whole building also books
all of its areas.

## For members and guests

Booking for a member: Under **For a member (optional)** you look up a member (this needs the
permission to view members). You don't enter contact details again; they are in the member record.
The booking shows the name in Bookings, appears in the member record under **Bookings** and in the
member's members area. For guests without membership there is still
**External booking (optional)** with name, email and phone.

Charging rent: In an item's booking calendar you enter a rental price, per booking, per started
day or per hour. On a confirmed one-off booking for a member, **Create invoice** creates a draft
invoice to that member with the rental price as a suggestion. This also works if the member's
fee is otherwise paid through a unit's collective invoice. Finalise and send the draft under
Finance › Invoices like any other invoice; the booking then shows the invoice number. You need
the permission to edit invoices.

If you cancel a booking that has an invoice, the invoice remains; HUBIplan points this out
beforehand and at the booking. Delete a draft under Finance › Invoices, or cancel an issued
invoice there.

## Overlaps and approval

Overlaps: If the item, including set-up time, is already booked, HUBIplan refuses the
booking and shows the booked time. If a linked event later moves onto a booked time, the
booking is marked **check**.

Requests and approval: If an item needs approval, your booking starts as a request and does
not block anything yet. People with the permission “Book for others and approve bookings”, or with edit permission
on the item, see **Open requests** and approve or reject them. You can cancel your own request
or booking yourself.

Visibility: With **Only the managers see the purpose**, other members only see "Booked".
Cancel a single date of a series with **Cancel this date only**.

Lending material: For one-off bookings of material, the managers use **Confirm hand-out** in
the booking and later **Confirm return**. Only if you tick
**Record the item's condition on return** does HUBIplan change the item's condition and note; the change then appears in the
item's history.

Booking from a demand: If a material item with a booking calendar is assigned to an event, its
detail page shows **Book firmly**. This opens a booking for that event; for "This occurrence only"
exactly that date is booked.

On the website: Under **Booking calendar** you choose per item whether the “Bookings” section of the website shows nothing, only booked times or, for public bookings, also the purpose. Switch the section on under Website › Menu and pages.

Requests from the members' area: With **Members may send requests from the members' area** an
item appears in My area on the Bookings tile. Such requests always need approval. Whoever made a
request or booking receives an email when someone else confirms, rejects or cancels it.
en.seiten/bestellungen.md:
---
key: page.orders
titel: Orders
modul: orders
rechte: [orders.view, orders.edit]
routen: [/bestellungen]
stichworte:
  [
    Order,
    Group order,
    Club clothing,
    Commemorative booklet,
    Uniform,
    Sizes,
    Size survey,
    Supplier,
    Hand-out,
  ]
---

Under **Orders** you collect members' orders, for example for club clothing, a commemorative
booklet or uniform items. Members order in the member area or in the app until the deadline and
can change or withdraw their order until then. You see the totals per item and size for the
order with your supplier.

## Creating a group order

With **New group order** you enter a title, a deadline and, if you like, a description. Under
**Who may order?** you choose all members or only one unit. Each item has:

- **Price in euros (optional)**: empty means no price. This turns it into a plain survey, for example of
  sizes for new jackets.
- **Sizes or variants (optional)**, separated by commas, such as “S, M, L, XL”, and a heading for
  them such as “Size”.
- **At most per member (optional)** and **At most in total (optional)**, for example when there are only 50 booklets.

**The club pays** hides the prices from members; then no invoices are created. With **Approve**
members see the group order; a push notification to the apps is optional.

## After the deadline

After the deadline members can no longer order. You can still enter, change or delete orders,
for example from a paper list, with **Enter order**. **Close now** closes early, **Reopen** opens
again as long as the deadline has not passed.

**Totals for the supplier** shows the quantities per item and size. **As Excel** downloads totals
and orders. When handing out, tick **handed out** for each order.

## Invoices (optional)

With a price and the invoicing right, **Create invoices** creates an invoice to the member for
every order without one. Members with a direct debit mandate appear in the next direct debit
run, the others pay by bank transfer. The invoices are under Finance › Invoices and in the member
area. An order with an invoice can only be changed after cancelling the invoice.

## Rights and clean-up

The **Orders** right under Settings › Roles controls viewing and editing. Roles with invoices,
material or registrations have it from the start. The module can be switched on and off under
Settings › Modules. Two years after the deadline HUBIplan deletes the group order and its orders;
invoices stay in the finances.
en.seiten/chronik.md:
---
key: page.chronicle
titel: Chronicle
modul: chronicle
rechte: [chronicle.view, chronicle.edit]
routen: [/chronik]
stichworte: [chronicle, history, timeline, anniversary book, anniversary, chapter]
---

Under **Chronicle** you maintain the history of the club as a timeline: short entries with a
year or period, optionally with pictures, and chapters as subheadings. A short introduction sits
above it.

The chronicle is a module of its own and useful even without a website, for example for an
anniversary book. If the **Website** module is switched on, the published version appears there
under “Chronicle”. It is maintained only here; under Website › Texts the chronicle only shows
its address and menu setting.

HUBIplan saves changes as a draft. **Publish** makes the draft the valid version; earlier
versions can be brought back into the draft below. You can take over many entries at once from
an Excel file.

Anyone with the “Maintain chronicle” right may edit it; anyone with “Read chronicle” may read
it. Roles that edit website content already have both.

A connected AI assistant can also maintain the chronicle in the draft, for example take over
entries from an anniversary publication (see [Connect an AI assistant](/hilfe/ki-assistent-verbinden)).
en.seiten/datenschutz-werkzeuge.md:
---
key: page.dsgvo
titel: Data protection tools
rechte: [privacy.view, privacy.edit]
routen: [/dsgvo, /dsgvo/auftragsverarbeiter, /dsgvo/datenpannen]
stichworte:
  [
    GDPR,
    Data protection,
    Record of processing,
    Record of processing activities,
    Art. 30,
    Processor,
    Data processing agreement,
    DPA,
    Data breach,
    Reporting obligation,
    Supervisory authority,
    TOM,
  ]
---

Under **GDPR** the board keeps the documents the GDPR requires from every club that
holds member data: the record of processing activities, the list of processors and the
log of data breaches. The privacy notices for members and the website remain under
Settings › Data protection.

Record: For every enabled module HUBIplan suggests a processing activity with purpose, legal
basis, data subjects, data, recipients and erasure period. The periods match what HUBIplan
actually erases. Check the details; remove what the club does not use with **Hide**. Add what the
club processes outside HUBIplan, such as car pools or photos in a messenger group, with
**Own activity**. **Record as PDF** creates the record for filing or for the supervisory authority.

## In detail

Controller and measures: Name, address and representatives come from the legal notice. Add the
data protection officer if there is one, and who runs the server. The technical and
organisational measures are prefilled with what HUBIplan itself provides; add what the club does
beyond that.

Processors: This lists all business partners with the role **Processor** and whether a valid
**Data processing agreement** is on file. You maintain partners and agreements under
[Business partners](/geschaeftspartner); an agreement is valid until its end date.

Data breaches: **Record a data breach** documents what happened, which data and persons are
concerned, how high you rate the risk and what you did about it. From the time the breach was
discovered, there are 72 hours to report it to the supervisory authority. Open breaches appear on
the home page under **To do** until the report and closure are entered. Without a risk to the
persons concerned there is no need to report, but the breach is still documented. Closing is
only possible once the report is entered or you explain why it was not reported. **PDF** creates
the log of one breach. Description, data, consequences and measures are stored encrypted.

Permissions: Everyone with “View data protection” may read, everyone with “Edit data protection”
may maintain. Roles that can edit the settings have this permission from the start. The
suggestions are a working aid, not legal advice.
en.seiten/dokumente-papierkorb.md:
---
key: page.documents_trash
titel: Documents › Trash
modul: docs
rechte: []
routen: [/dokumente/papierkorb]
stichworte: [Trash, deleted, restore, delete permanently]

Deleted documents stay in the trash for 30 days. During that time you bring them back to their folder with **Restore**. **Delete permanently** removes a document immediately and cannot be undone. After 30 days HUBIplan deletes by itself.
en.seiten/dokumente.md:
---
key: page.documents
titel: Documents
modul: docs
routen: [/dokumente]
stichworte: [file, storage, folder, statutes, minutes]
---

Document storage keeps the unit's statutes, minutes, forms and other files in folders. For each folder you decide who sees it, for example only the board or all members. Deleted items go to the bin first; the “Bin” link is at the top of the library.

Storage opens in **Tile view** with folder and file type icons. Switch to **List view** for a compact layout. Click a folder to open it, then **Documents** in the folder path to return to the overview.

**Search (folders, title and note)** searches all your visible own and shared folders, even while a folder is open. Results include matching folder names and documents with matching titles or notes. **Clear search** returns to the previous folder.

## In detail

Statutes, fee rules and the founding deed are at the top under “Club documents” as fixed folders with their existing versions and sharing settings. A lock marks board folders. Folders shared by other units are read only. Users with management rights can create folders, change visibility and sharing, upload, edit, move, add versions or delete files. The storage display shows usage and, where available, the club's budget.

If virus scanning is set up on the server, HUBIplan scans newly uploaded files. If the scanner is unreachable right now, the document shows “Being scanned for viruses”: it can only be opened after the scan, usually within a few minutes. “Locked: malware found” means the file stays locked for good; upload a clean version instead.
en.seiten/einstellungen-api.md:
---
key: page.settings_api
titel: Settings › API accesses
modul: api
rechte: [api.manage]
routen: [/einstellungen/api]
stichworte:
  [API, interface, key, federation software, federation, other programs, data exchange, OpenAPI]
---

With an API access another program reads data of your unit, for example your umbrella association's software, a website of your own or a display board. Each access has its own key, may only read what you tick and expires by itself.

These accesses never provide names, addresses or bank details of individual members, and an access cannot change anything. Create a separate access for each program; then one can be deleted without disturbing the others.

The page only exists if the module “API for other programs” is switched on and your role has the additional right “Manage API accesses”. No role receives this right automatically.

## What an access may read

- Unit: name, address, contact, logo and the sub-units.
- Events: events with the visibility “public”, optionally also those for members. Board-only events and replies are never included.
- Member numbers: counts on a reference date by age, gender and sub-unit, no persons.
- Board and offices: roles with their functional address; names only if they appear on your public website.
- Results, posts, documents: only what your website publishes.

An area only appears if its module is switched on. With **Applies to** you restrict an access to one sub-unit; it then only sees that unit's data.

## Key and security

The key is shown on the page exactly once: after creating the access and after **Create new key**. HUBIplan does not store it in readable form. Pass it on securely, not by unencrypted email. For both, HUBIplan asks for a fresh two-factor code.

After **Create new key** the previous key remains valid for seven more days, so the other program can be switched over without an outage. If a key has fallen into the wrong hands, delete the access: it stops working immediately.

Every access expires after one year at the latest; 30 days before, everyone with the right receives an email. Use **Edit** to extend it. If an access is not used for 90 days, HUBIplan switches it off; **Switch on again** puts it back into operation.

Under **Allowed addresses (optional)** you allow requests only from certain IP addresses. **Callable from other websites** is meant for data that is public anyway, because the key is then visible in the website's source code; it is therefore not possible together with member events or member numbers.

Creating, changing, key changes and deleting are recorded in the change log. Each access allows 600 requests per hour.

## For developers

The address of the interface and its description (OpenAPI) are shown at the top of the page. The key is sent as `Authorization: Bearer hpk_…`. Errors are returned as `application/problem+json` with a fixed `code`.
en.seiten/einstellungen-bezeichnungen.md:
---
key: page.settings_terms
titel: Settings › Names and terms
rechte: [org.edit]
routen: [/einstellungen/bezeichnungen]
siehe: [guide.club_setup]
stichworte: [term, platoon, corps, section, sub-unit, article, English]
---

Here you set what your unit and its sub-units are called, for example “club” and “section”, with article and plural and, if you like, in English. HUBIplan uses these words everywhere in the menu, lists and texts; with several levels it counts per level, for example “7 corps · 15 platoons”. Whether sub-units keep their own members and have their own access is also set here. If your club has no sub-units, turn off “Show … in the main menu” here; the menu item then disappears for everyone, existing sub-units are kept, and you can turn it back on at any time. HUBIplan saves changes automatically.
en.seiten/einstellungen-briefbogen.md:
---
key: page.settings_letterhead
titel: Settings › Letterhead
rechte: [org.edit]
routen: [/einstellungen/briefbogen]
# prettier-ignore
stichworte: [letterhead, header, footer, font, line colour, logo size, style guide, word mark, name in the letterhead, line break]
---

The letterhead defines the header, footer, colours and font for all of the unit's letters and PDFs, such as invoices, receipts and circulars.

The defaults match the previous look. For your own corporate design (style guide) you can set:

## Font and logo

- **Body text font** and **Font for name, title and subject**: besides Office fonts such as Arial or Georgia, also the website fonts (Source Sans 3, Crimson Pro, Atkinson Hyperlegible, Open Sans, Roboto, Oswald, blackletter). They are embedded in PDFs. In the Word template their name comes with a fallback font (**Fallback font in Word (text)** or **Fallback font in Word (headings)**) that Word uses if the font is missing on the computer.
- **Logo/crest size**: small, medium or large. Portrait crests become noticeably wider with “large”.
- **Logo for the letterhead**: an image only for letters, such as a landscape word-and-image mark, while HUBIplan, membership cards and certificates keep the coat of arms. Without a logo of its own, the one from the appearance settings applies. Sub-units with their own letterhead can set their own, otherwise they take it over. Wide logos usually fit best with the size “large”.
- **Name as text next to the logo**: switch off if the logo already contains the name. Without a logo, the name is always shown in the header.

## Name, lines and colours

- **Name in the letterhead**: decides how the name breaks in the header, two lines at most, for example “Turn- und Sportverein” and below it “Musterstadt von 1920 e. V.”. With **Second line smaller** the second line looks like a subtitle. If the field is empty, the unit's name appears in the header: a long name is first reduced and, if it still does not fit, spread evenly over two lines, in Word as in the PDF. Following pages and the return address always show the full name.
- **Line colour** from the unit's palette, plus **Line below the header** and **Line above the footer**, each on or off. If the colour barely stands out on white (contrast below 3:1, such as a light yellow), the page points this out.
- **Colour of title and subject**: black or main colour, for example for “Invoice” and the subject of the Word template.
- **Table lines** and **Table stripes** for invoices, cancellation invoices and receipts.

Every sub-unit with its own letterhead sets this separately. A connected AI assistant can also change the letterhead if you explicitly allow it when connecting. It only saves the texts (name in the letterhead, additional line, salutation, closing) as a proposal: it appears at the top of this page with the current and the new text. With **Apply** (fresh confirmation with the second factor) it applies to all new letters, with **Discard** it is gone; after 30 days it expires on its own.
en.seiten/einstellungen-datenschutz.md:
---
key: page.settings_privacy
titel: Settings › Privacy
rechte: [org.edit]
routen: [/einstellungen/datenschutz]
siehe: [guide.privacy_request]
stichworte: [privacy, GDPR, privacy notice, retention periods]
