en.seiten/finanzen-kuenstlersozialabgabe.md:
---
key: page.finance_artist_fees
titel: Finance › Artists’ social security levy
modul: tax
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/steuern/kuenstlersozialabgabe]
siehe: [guide.event_finance]
stichworte: [Artists’ social security levy, KSK, fee, artist, report]
---

The **Artists' social security levy** tab under taxes (Tax & charitable status module) adds up the fees paid to self-employed artists and writers per calendar year, e.g. for a band, choir director, DJ or graphic designer. It counts expenses ticked **Fee paid to artists (artists' social security levy)** in the cash book and all expenses of a category marked as **Artist fees** under Set up › Categories; cancellations do not count. The page shows the total per recipient, the levy at that year's rate (2026: 4.9 %) and the deadline for reporting to the Künstlersozialkasse (31 March of the following year), also as Excel.
en.seiten/finanzen-lastschrift.md:
---
key: page.finance_debits
titel: Finance › Direct debits
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.view]
routen: [/finanzen/lastschrift, /finanzen/lastschrift/mandate]
stichworte: [SEPA, direct debit, collection, mandate, bank]
---

From open invoices with a valid SEPA mandate HUBIplan creates a direct debit file that you upload in online banking. A checklist first checks the creditor ID, deadlines and expiring mandates. HUBIplan does not connect to the bank itself.

For organisation members (and for clubs of an association) you can choose **Business direct debit (B2B)** as the **Scheme** when recording a paper mandate. This needs a signed mandate on the business form, and the payer must register it with their bank. The payer cannot reverse a business direct debit once it has been paid. In a direct debit run, core and business debits sit in separate blocks of the same file. For persons there is only the **Core direct debit**.

If loading fails, **Reload** retrieves proposals and runs again. A failed request is shown as an error rather than an empty selection.
en.seiten/finanzen-mahnstufen.md:
---
key: page.finance_dunning_levels
titel: Finance › Set up › Reminder levels
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.edit]
routen: [/finanzen/einrichtung/mahnstufen]
siehe: [guide.dunning]
stichworte: [reminder level, deadline, reminder fee]
---

Reminder levels define after how many days a reminder is sent and with which text. A friendly first reminder is often enough.
en.seiten/finanzen-mahnungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_dunning
titel: Finance › Reminders
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.edit]
routen: [/finanzen/rechnungen/mahnungen]
stichworte: [reminder, payment reminder, overdue]
---

Here you see overdue invoices and send payment reminders according to your reminder levels. Each reminder is noted on the invoice.
en.seiten/finanzen-mittelverwendung.md:
---
key: page.finance_use_of_funds
titel: Finance › Use of funds
modul: tax
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/steuern/mittelverwendung]
siehe: [guide.reserve, guide.year_closing]
stichworte: [Use of funds, timely use, reserve, charitable status]
---

The **Use of funds** tab under taxes (Tax & charitable status module) is a simplified statement on the use of funds. Non-profit funds must be used for the statutory purposes or placed in permitted reserves by the end of the second financial year after they were received.

The page shows per year the amount carried over, the funds received (income of the non-profit area and surpluses of the other areas), their use (expenses of the non-profit area, losses of purpose-related operations), additions to and releases from reserves, and what is still to be used by year of origin. The oldest funds are used first. If a deadline has passed, a notice appears. From 100,000 € income per year the tax office usually expects such a statement.
en.seiten/finanzen-pauschalen.md:
---
key: page.finance_allowances
titel: Finance › Allowances
modul: tax
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/pauschalen]
siehe: [guide.booking]
stichworte: [Allowance, trainer, volunteer, tax-free amount]
---

The **Allowances** item under “Book” (also part of the Tax & charitable status module) adds up the trainer allowance (§ 3 no. 26 EStG, €3,300 since 2026) and the volunteer allowance (§ 3 no. 26a EStG, €960 since 2026) per person and calendar year. It counts expenses for which **Expense allowance to a person** is selected in the cash book; cancellations do not count. From 80 % there is a note, above the tax-free amount a warning: the payment is then taxable, usually as a mini-job.

## In detail

The tax-free amounts apply across all payers together. Under **PDF** there is a declaration per person to sign, confirming they do not use the amount elsewhere. Once signed, it belongs with the receipts. If a board member receives an allowance, HUBIplan warns as long as **Our statutes allow the board to be paid** is not ticked (§ 27 (3) BGB).

Besides cash book expenses, the following also count:

- waiving the allowance as an expense donation: tick **Waiver of reimbursement of expenses** on the donation and choose the type under **Waiver of an allowance**. The amount uses up the tax-free allowance just like a payment,
- payments from the musician settlement: when an expense is assigned to an approved musician remuneration, HUBIplan sets the trainer allowance (artistic activity) and counts it for the musician,
- payments by sub-units with their own cash book that belong to the club for tax purposes. The same person then appears only once, with all payments in the expandable list below the name. The sub-unit itself only sees its own payments and a note where it is counted.
en.seiten/finanzen-quittungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_receipts
titel: Finance › Receipts
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/quittungen]
stichworte: [receipt, cash payment, voucher]
---

For cash payments you issue a receipt here, with your stored signature if you like. Each receipt gets a sequential number and is booked in the cash book.

The signature on the screen is a simple electronic signature: it shows that someone signed on the spot, but it does not verify who it was. If the app is used offline, date and time come from the phone. For the cash book this is as good a voucher as a paper receipt. If you need more certainty (for example for large amounts), also have the receipt confirmed in writing or by email.

Name searches ignore letter case and normalize Unicode spelling variants; “ß” and “ss” are treated as equal. Other selected filters still apply.

## In detail

The details of a new receipt are saved with **Continue to signature**. If you change details and cancel or leave the page, HUBIplan asks before discarding them. **Continue editing** retains your input. An automatically selected sole cash account does not trigger a warning on its own.

If the receipt list or the account and category choices fail to load, use **Reload**. A failed request for choices does not discard receipt details you have already entered.
en.seiten/finanzen-rechnung.md:
---
key: page.finance_invoice_settings
titel: Finance › Set up › Invoice & payment
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.edit]
routen: [/finanzen/einrichtung/rechnung]
siehe: [guide.invoice_single, guide.invoice_cancel]
stichworte: [invoice, payment term, creditor ID, e-invoice]
---

This holds the details that appear on every invoice: payment term, bank details, creditor ID for direct debits and the number range.

Under **E-invoices for public authorities** you can have invoices to members with a Leitweg-ID (e.g. a town or district as a member) created as XRechnung. Enter the Leitweg-ID in the member’s billing address. When finalising, HUBIplan validates the XRechnung; if something is missing, such as the club’s address, contact, phone or an account with IBAN, the invoice stays a draft and the message names what is missing. Membership fees appear in it as not subject to VAT. The invoice email carries the XRechnung as an attachment.

Cancel bookings with receipts instead of deleting them. Imported bank statements are retained; ignore unwanted transactions. Archive used categories and create a new category for new assignments. Reminders retain their archived version.
en.seiten/finanzen-rechnungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_invoices
titel: Finance › Invoices
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.view]
routen: [/finanzen/rechnungen]
stichworte: [invoice, fee, open, paid, cancellation]
---

This lists all of the unit's invoices, such as membership fees or club clothing costs, with their status: open, paid, reminded or cancelled. You create a single invoice here; a fee run creates many at once.

Name searches ignore letter case and normalize Unicode spelling variants; “ß” and “ss” are treated as equal. Other selected filters still apply.

Enter a search term and choose **Search** or press Enter. Status and other filters apply immediately.

After you change the selection, previous results are hidden until the new request finishes. If loading fails, **Reload** retries the same selection.

## In detail

Final invoices show credited advances and the remaining outstanding amount. A credited
advance invoice is marked “Settled”. Its receipts remain in the cashbook. Cancel the
associated final invoice before removing those payments. A final invoice fully covered
by advances can also be cancelled if it has no additional payments.

Cancelling: in the invoice, choose **Cancel invoice** and give a reason. HUBIplan then creates a separate cancellation invoice, for example R2026-0012-S. It has its own date and reason, refers to the number and date of the invoice and lists all items with negative amounts. The issued invoice stays unchanged. **View cancellation invoice** opens the document and **Send cancellation invoice by email** sends it to the recipient. Members also find it in the member area.

Paid invoices can be cancelled too. The payments then remain on the invoice as a credit. **Refund** reverses the payments in the cash book with today's date; then transfer the amount back. **Offset** moves the payments to an open invoice to the same recipient.

**Cancel and create again** cancels the invoice and opens a copy as a new draft, so you correct a wrong invoice in one step. Invoices from a fee run are recalculated in the fee run instead.
en.seiten/finanzen-rechnungseingang.md:
---
key: page.finance_incoming
titel: Finances › Incoming invoices
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/rechnungen/eingang]
stichworte: [E-invoice, ZUGFeRD, incoming, approval, XML]
---

Import XML invoices or ZUGFeRD/Factur-X PDFs. HUBIplan retains the original even when
validation fails. Importing the identical file again does not create another entry.
Check different files with the same invoice number for duplicates yourself.

**Invoice mailbox**: If an invoice mailbox is set up on the server, the address of your unit is shown at the top, e.g. `rechnung+k7m2q9ab@example.org`. Give it to your suppliers. HUBIplan collects the mailbox every minute and imports XML attachments and ZUGFeRD/Factur-X PDFs just like an import. The entry then shows **By email from** with the sender.

## In detail

If the sender does not match any business partner (email address under Administration › Business partners), **Unknown sender** appears; then check the issuer and bank details with particular care. Emails without an e-invoice, such as an ordinary PDF invoice, spam or malware, are listed under **Notices from the mailbox** until you choose **Done**. **Assign new address** invalidates the previous address, for example if it receives spam.

**Business partners**: HUBIplan suggests a business partner for each invoice, recognised by
VAT ID, IBAN, the email sender (including the contact persons' email addresses) or name.
**Link suggestion** accepts it; **Create as business partner** creates a new supplier from the
name, VAT ID, IBAN and sender. **Unlink business partner** removes the link. When you later
link a cash book entry, it takes over the business partner.

**New IBAN**: If the invoice IBAN differs from the one stored for the business partner,
HUBIplan shows a clear warning. Call the issuer on a number you already know, not the one on
the invoice, and tick **New IBAN confirmed by phone** before approving. HUBIplan stores the
confirmed IBAN with the business partner. This protects you against fake invoices with
someone else's bank account.

## Validation and approval

Technical validation (KoSIT) runs in the background after the import. Until it finishes,
the entry shows **Checking**; this usually takes less than a minute and the page refreshes
by itself. HUBIplan deletes declined entries and files without a readable e-invoice after
90 days if no booking is linked.

Validation covers the XML data. It does not certify PDF/A properties or consistency
between an external PDF view and its embedded XML. Use the **Readable view** of the
structured data for review.

Check the recipient, service, amount and bank details before approval. Enter a review
note and choose **Approve business review** or **Decline**. Approval requires successful
technical validation. Revalidation preserves previous reports in the audit export.

Importing and approving do not send a payment. After actual payment, link a matching
cash book entry. Type, EUR amount and an open financial year are checked; partial
payments cannot be linked here yet. The original also becomes a cash book attachment.
en.seiten/finanzen-ruecklagen.md:
---
key: page.finance_reserves
titel: Finance › Reserves
modul: tax
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/ruecklagen]
stichworte: [reserve, non-profit status, use of funds]
---

Here you keep reserves, for example for the next event or a larger purchase. Non-profit clubs must generally use funds promptly; reserves are only allowed for certain reasons (§ 62 AO).

At the bottom of the page, **Maximum for the free reserve** works out how much may be added to the free reserve in a financial year: one third of the surplus from asset management plus 10 % of the other funds to be used promptly (income of the non-profit area, surpluses from purpose-related and commercial operations). Any amount not used in the two previous years can be carried over. If additions are higher, a notice appears. The calculation uses the tax areas of the categories; entries without an area count as non-profit income.

If there are assets in the asset register, their depreciation for the year is shown as a guide for a replacement reserve. From 100,000 € income per year, the page points out that the tax office usually expects a statement on the use of funds.
en.seiten/finanzen-sammelauszahlungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_payout_runs
titel: Finance › Batch payouts
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/sammelauszahlungen]
siehe: [guide.expense_review]
stichworte: [Batch payout, remuneration, SEPA, transfer, musicians, pain.001]
---

In **Batch payouts** (Finance, Book), select approved outstanding remuneration, a bank account and an execution date. Check each holder, IBAN and optional BIC. Saving a run for review reserves claims and freezes amounts and recipient details. Download the SEPA file (pain.001.001.09, EUR), check it and approve it at your bank. Repeated downloads contain the same instruction; do not submit the file twice.

Export does not execute transfers or mark claims paid. The file requests individual bank entries. Assign each actual expense in the performance settlement; bank account and amount must match. Reversed bookings reopen reconciliation. Cancelling a run releases claims; submitted transfers must also be stopped at the bank. Finance read access permits inspection; edit access is required to prepare, export or cancel.
en.seiten/finanzen-steuern.md:
---
key: page.finance_tax
titel: Finance › Taxes
modul: tax
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/steuern]
siehe: [guide.vat_return, guide.year_closing]
stichworte: [Taxes, exemption limit, charitable status, commercial operation, tax adviser]
---

The **Taxes** item shows the tax report for a financial year. It belongs to the Tax & charitable status module. It also needs categories assigned to tax areas (Set up › Categories). You see:

## In detail

- **Tax-free limit**: income from commercial operations including VAT compared with the tax-free limit (€50,000 since 2026, €45,000 before), plus the two previous years. From 80 % you get a note, above the limit a warning.
- **By tax area**: income, expenses and result per area. Cancellations are offset against the cancelled booking. A loss in the commercial operations shows a note.
- **Included cash books**: sub-units with their own cash book count towards the club unless their settings mark them as "separate for tax purposes". A sub-unit only sees its own figures in its own report.
- **Small-business limit**: turnover from purpose-related and commercial operations in the previous and the current year. If the club shows VAT on its invoices, this part is left out.
- **Tax return**: once the details of the exemption notice are entered, this shows for which years the next return is due.

The report is also available as PDF and Excel, for example for your tax adviser. It is a template, not tax advice.
en.seiten/finanzen-umsatzsteuer.md:
---
key: page.finance_vat
titel: Finance › VAT
modul: tax
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/steuern/umsatzsteuer]
stichworte: [VAT, advance return, input tax, ELSTER]
---

The **VAT** tab under taxes (Tax & charitable status module) is a template for the advance VAT return. For the selected month, quarter or year it shows boxes 81 and 86 (taxable turnover at 19 % and 7 %, with the tax base in whole euros), 48 (tax-exempt turnover), 66 (input VAT) and 83 (amount payable or refund). Bookings with a tax rate are counted. Input VAT only counts for expenses outside the non-profit area, proportionally for mixed use; a cancellation reduces the cancelled booking. Sub-units that belong to the club for tax purposes are included.

## In detail

Under **Settings** you choose whether **The club is liable for VAT (not a small business)**, the **Advance return period** and whether input VAT is calculated as a flat rate under § 23a UStG: 7 % of taxable turnover instead of input VAT from invoices (box 63), only if this turnover did not exceed €50,000 in the previous year; the choice is binding for five years. HUBIplan does not transmit anything to ELSTER. In the DATEV export, bookings with a tax rate get the matching tax key.
en.seiten/finanzen-veranstaltungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_events
titel: Finance › Events
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/veranstaltungen, /finanzen/veranstaltungen/reihen]
stichworte: [festival, event, project, cash report]
---

For a festival or another project you group all related bookings here and produce a cash report at the end. This shows whether an event covered its costs.

Under **Planned income (optional)** and **Planned expenses (optional)** you enter what you expect. The evaluation then shows the plan next to income, expenses and result. The budget for the whole year is under Finance › Evaluate & close › Budget.

## Series

A series groups recurring events, e.g. “Summer party”. Choose the series when editing an event under **Series (optional)**; this lets you compare the years.
en.seiten/finanzen-vermoegen.md:
---
key: page.finance_net_assets
titel: Finance › Net assets
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/auswertung/vermoegen]
siehe: [guide.year_closing]
stichworte: [Net assets, receivables, liabilities, balance]
---

The **Net assets** tab in the evaluation shows what the club owns and owes at the end of a financial year: account balances, open invoices to members and business partners, fixed assets at book value from the asset register (Tax & charitable status module) and open incoming invoices. Anything paid only after the year end counts as open on the reporting date. If reserves are switched on, it also shows how much is set aside and how much is freely available. The overview is also part of the treasurer's report for the general meeting.
en.seiten/finanzen-zuwendungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_donations
titel: Finance › Donation receipts
modul: donations
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/zuwendungen]
stichworte: [donation, donation receipt, tax office]
---

For donations and tax-deductible membership fees you create official donation receipts here, individually or as an annual statement. A checklist first shows missing details such as the tax exemption notice. You enter these details under Finance › Set up › Donations.

An issued donation receipt also protects its source cashbook entry: it cannot be edited, deleted or reverted with Undo. To make a correction, cancel the donation receipt first. You can then correct the entry under the usual cashbook rules; the cancelled receipt copy remains available.

Name searches ignore letter case and normalize Unicode spelling variants; “ß” and “ss” are treated as equal. Other selected filters still apply.

## In detail

For donations up to 300 €, the tax office accepts the bank statement together with a note from the club (simplified donation proof). Once the tax-privileged status details are complete, Finance › Set up › Donations offers this note under **Donations up to 300 €** as a PDF and as text for the website. It names the notice, the purposes, the donation account and whether it also covers membership fees.

A donation taken from the cash book follows its booking: if you change the booking's amount or date, HUBIplan changes the not yet confirmed donation as well. If the booking is deleted or cancelled (also by cancelling a receipt), the unconfirmed donation is removed. Once it is confirmed, the booking and receipt can only be changed, deleted or cancelled after the confirmation has been cancelled. Before issuing, HUBIplan checks that booking and donation match; the checklist names mismatches from older data.

HUBIplan books payments on household and company invoices to the payer, not to the individual members. A donation receipt for them therefore goes to the payer: to the paying member or the company, or for a payer without membership with name and address as on the invoice.
en.seiten/finanzen-zweckbindungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_earmarks
titel: Finance › Earmarked donations
modul: donations
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/zuwendungen/zweckbindungen]
stichworte: [Earmark, earmarked, donation, use of funds]
---

In the **Earmarks** tab you create purposes that people donate to specifically, such as renovating the clubhouse. Assign a donation to a purpose with the **Earmarked for** field, and the expenses for it in the cash book with **Earmarked donation used for**. The overview shows the donations per purpose, how much has been used and the remainder. Only money donations count; cancellations do not. If the first donation was more than two years ago and something is left, a notice reminds you of the prompt use of funds. A purpose with donations or expenses can only be archived, not deleted.
en.seiten/finanzen.md:
---
key: page.finance
titel: Finance › Overview
rechte: [finance.view, billing.view]
routen: [/finanzen]
siehe: [guide.booking, guide.fee_run, guide.year_change]
stichworte: [cash, balance, overview, open items]
---

The overview shows account balances, open invoices and upcoming tasks for the treasurer. On the left, the parts of finance are grouped along the financial year: **Fees & invoices**, **Payments**, **Bookkeeping**, **Evaluate & close** and **Set up**. The group of the page you are on is open; ▸ expands another group for a look. Which groups and entries appear depends on the enabled modules and your rights; a group with only one entry is shown as a plain entry.
en.seiten/fristenkalender.md:
---
key: page.obligations
titel: Deadline calendar for club obligations
modul: obligations
rechte: [obligations.view, obligations.edit]
routen: [/fristenkalender]
stichworte:
  [
    Deadline,
    Obligation,
    Exemption notice,
    Tax return,
    Cash audit,
    Transparency register,
    Register court,
    Register of associations,
    Board election,
    Insurance,
    Reminder,
  ]
---

The **Deadline calendar** collects the obligations a club has to meet regularly, such as the tax
return for the exemption notice, the cash audit before the annual general meeting or the check of
the transparency register. HUBIplan reminds you in time and records when an obligation was
completed.

Adding an obligation: **New obligation** asks for a name, the next deadline, the repetition
(once, every year, every three years …) and how many days before the deadline HUBIplan sends a
reminder. In the note you can record, for example, the legal basis or where the documents are
kept.

## In detail

Responsible: An obligation belongs to a role, not to a person, for example the treasurer. When
the office changes hands, HUBIplan reminds the new holders automatically. Without a role, the
reminders go to everyone who may maintain the deadline calendar.

Suggestions: **Suggestions** lists common obligations of registered, non-profit associations in
Germany. **Apply** creates the obligation; you adjust deadline, repetition and responsibility as
you do so. Suggestions that only concern registered associations appear when “entered in the register” is ticked in the legal notice. The notes are no substitute for legal or tax advice.

Reminder: As soon as the reminder period starts, the responsible people receive one email, and
the obligation appears on the home page under **To do**. Overdue obligations are highlighted
there and in the deadline calendar.

Done: **Done** records the date and a short remark, such as “Notice of 12 March is in the tax
office folder”. A recurring obligation moves on to the next deadline, a one-off one then appears
under **Completed**. The **History** shows who completed which deadline and when. Everyone who
maintains the deadline calendar and the holders of the responsible role may mark it as done.

After a board election: When minutes are approved in [Meetings](/versammlungen) that contain an accepted election to an office that represents the club, HUBIplan creates the task “Report the change of the board to the register court”. It names those elected, is due 14 days after the meeting and is linked to the election in the resolution book. Representing roles are those marked “represents the unit (§ 26 BGB)”; the office in the minutes must have the same name as the role.

If no role is marked, all board roles count. This happens for clubs that are entered in the register according to their legal notice. If you adopt the suggestion, you can change the deadline and the responsible role or switch the task off. If the Tasks module is switched off, a one-off obligation appears in the deadline calendar instead.

You switch the module on under Settings › Modules.
en.seiten/geschaeftspartner.md:
---
key: page.partners
titel: Business partners
rechte: [partners.view, finance.view, billing.view]
routen: [/geschaeftspartner]
stichworte:
  [
    business partner,
    supplier,
    service provider,
    sponsor,
    sponsorship,
    thank-you letter,
    authority,
    contact person,
    customer,
    address book,
  ]
---

This lists all companies, authorities, associations and people outside the member list that you deal with: suppliers, service providers, sponsors, landlords, public offices or the press.

## Create and maintain partners

- **Create business partner** asks for the type (company, authority/office, association/federation, private person, other), address, contact and tax details. Only the name is required. Each entry gets a running number such as “GP-0001”. Changes to an existing partner save themselves.
- Under **Roles** you tick what the partner is for you, several if needed: for example supplier and sponsor. Customer and supplier also apply to invoices and incoming invoices.
- **Add contact** stores people at the partner with function, email and phone. A **Primary contact** is shown first in the list.
- Under **Contact with the club** you record when and how the first contact came about (**First contact on**, **First contact**) and which member looks after the partner (**Looked after by**).
- **Additional fields** creates your own fields for all business partners, such as sponsorship level, delivery time or customer since. The same kinds are available as for the members' additional fields, including repeatable fields with several entries. You enter the values in the partner's record in the **Additional fields** section; they save themselves. Fields without repetition appear as their own column in the Excel export and can be changed through the import. Anyone who may edit business partners may create fields.
- The **Treasury** section (bank account, **Default category**, payment term, artists' social security levy) only appears with cash or fee rights. Below it you see when the bank account was last changed and by whom.

## List, export and import

- You can search the list and filter it by type and role. **Show inactive** brings back partners you no longer need.
- **Export to Excel** puts all details into a spreadsheet, with a second sheet “Contact person”. Bank account, payment term and default category are only included if you have cash or fee rights. Export, serial letter and mailing list require the “Business partners” right; anyone who only manages the cash book or fees sees the partners but cannot take the whole list.
- **Import from Excel** reads such a spreadsheet back in. The easiest way is to export, edit in Excel and import the file. A known number updates the partner; empty cells change nothing. Rows without a number are created, unless the name already exists. HUBIplan finds contact persons by partner number, name and first name. **Check file** shows beforehand what will be added and what will change. “Looked after by” is matched most reliably through the column with the member number.
- **Merge duplicate entry** takes over a second entry of the same company: invoices, bookings, agreements, performances and contact persons move along.

## Letters and mailing lists

- **Serial letter and mailing list** chooses a group by role and type, for example all sponsors. **Copy e-mail addresses** fetches the addresses of the contact persons who receive mail (otherwise the partner's e-mail) for your mail program. **Create serial letter** writes one letter per partner with an address as a PDF on your letterhead.
- **Thank-you letter** creates a letter on your letterhead as a PDF, to the partner's address and the first contact person who receives mail. You can replace the suggestion with amount and in-kind contribution by your own text.

## Turnover and suggestions from the treasury

- **Turnover in the treasury** shows income and expenses with the partner per year and the latest bookings. Cancelled bookings do not count.
- The card “Suggestions from the cash book” lists names that appear several times as payee or payer in the cash book. **Apply** creates a business partner from one and links the bookings with exactly this name. This needs the right to edit the cash book.

## Agreements and contracts

- **Add agreement** records sponsorship and other arrangements: period, amount or in-kind contribution, what you give in return (such as a logo on the website, a perimeter board, a commemorative booklet) and the tax classification. “Mention only” without advertising belongs to the non-profit area or asset management, active advertising to the commercial operations. With an end date, HUBIplan creates a task that reminds you of the renewal in good time (Tasks module); you set how many days before on the agreement.
- For a **Contract** (type of agreement) you enter the **Notice period in days** and whether it renews automatically. The task then reminds you in good time before the last day to give notice, and the list shows “give notice by …”.
- Service providers who process members' data on behalf of the club (such as hosting, email delivery, a printer) get the role **Processor**. Store the contract under Art. 28 GDPR as an agreement of the type **Data processing agreement**. Under [GDPR](/dsgvo/auftragsverarbeiter) you can see where a contract is still missing.

## Documents and website

- Under **Documents** you keep contracts, offers, consents or correspondence on the record. The files count towards the storage of the document library and are checked for viruses as there.
- Under **Website** you record whether the partner may be named on your website as a partner or sponsor. Only these partners are taken over by the website section “Partners and sponsors” with **Take over from business partners**.

## Deleting and duplicates

- You can only delete a partner as long as it is not used anywhere. Otherwise untick **Active**.
- If a partner is also a member, for example a company as a supporting member, please do not create it twice. Only store private persons as far as you need them for a contract.
en.seiten/helferdienste.md:
---
key: page.helpers
titel: Volunteer duties and shift rosters
modul: helpers
rechte: [helpers.view, helpers.edit]
routen: [/helferdienste]
stichworte: [Duty roster, Shift roster, Volunteers, Shift, Bar, Setup, Assignment]
---

Under **Volunteer duties** you plan who takes on which duty at a festival or event, such as the
bar, cash desk, setup or teardown. The overview shows each duty roster with its open places.

## New duty roster

Choose **New duty roster**, enter a title and link the roster to an event if
needed.
From an event in the calendar, **Create duty roster for this event** leads straight here with
the event already selected. In the roster, the event name leads back to the calendar.

## Duties and shifts

Use **Add duty** to create a duty with its place and, if needed, a minimum
age (such as serving alcohol from 18). Below it you create the shifts: day, times and people per
shift. Several shifts can be created at once, such as “14-18, 18-22, 22-02”; a shift past
midnight ends the next day.

## Assigning

**Assign** on a shift adds a member or an external person with name and phone. If the
shift is already full, overlaps with another shift of the same person, or the person is younger
than the minimum age, HUBIplan asks first; **Assign anyway** goes ahead regardless. Phone numbers
are only visible to those who may edit duty rosters.

## Requirement

If the “Qualifications” module is switched on, you choose a qualification under
**Requirement** at a duty, for example first aid for the first-aid service. If the person lacks
it or it expires before the end of the shift, HUBIplan asks when assigning, and a note appears at
the person. Members who sign up themselves see the requirement and cannot sign up without a valid
certificate.

## Printing

**Notice as PDF** creates one page per duty with the shifts and empty lines for
signing up. **List as Excel** contains all shifts with the people assigned.

## Status

**Publish** marks the roster as final, **Close** ends it; after that it cannot be changed
until you reopen it. Only a published roster appears in the member area.

## Roster settings

Under **Roster settings** you choose whether members sign up themselves or only
the administration assigns people, until how many days before a shift members can cancel
themselves, the maximum number of shifts per person and how many days before a shift HUBIplan
sends a reminder email (empty: no reminder). You also choose whether people who signed up see
who else is on their shift, and you can write a note for the helpers. After the cancellation
deadline, only the administration can cancel a shift.

## Units

If a role of a unit (such as the platoon leadership) has the right, it plans its own
duties and only assigns members of that unit.

## Quotas

In a club roster, **Quota** on a shift gives part of the places to a unit, for example
“the rifle platoon provides 4 people for the bar”. The unit's leadership sees its places in its
volunteer duties under **Quotas from the club** and assigns its own members there. Places of a
quota that are still open count as taken in the member area. Setting 0 places removes a quota;
people already assigned stay on the shift.

## Copy roster

**Copy roster** creates a new roster in preparation, for example for next year's
festival. The copy takes over duties, shifts, quotas and settings, but no assignments. If you
enter the first day of the new roster, HUBIplan moves all shifts by the same distance.

## Call-out

If a published roster still has free places, **Call-out as circular** creates a draft
to all members of the unit with the free shifts and the link to sign up. You check and send it
like any circular. You also need the right to send circulars.

## Completed duties

Once a shift has started, tick **done** for each person. **Completed duties**
in the overview shows per year who took on how many shifts and hours, for example for a thank
you or required hours. Required hours with a substitute fee are set up under Finance › Set up ›
Fee rates › **Work hours**; the ticked shifts count there.
en.seiten/infrastruktur.md:
---
key: page.infrastructure
titel: Manage rooms and facilities
modul: infrastructure
rechte: [infrastructure.view]
routen: [/infrastruktur]
siehe: [guide.booking_create, guide.material_add]
stichworte: [Shooting range, Clubhouse, Hall, Room, Area, Key, Shooting lanes]
---

Equipment & rooms › **Rooms and facilities** (Facilities module) lists the fixed premises of your active unit, for example a clubhouse,
a sports ground or a shooting range. Each facility has its own number (INF-…), a type, a short
description and an address.

With editing permission, choose **Create facility**. Optionally enter the capacity,
ownership and use, and an **Access note** such as where the key box is. Only people with
viewing permission for facilities can see the access note.

For the type **Shooting range**, enter the number of lanes per discipline under
**Shooting lanes**, for example ten 10 m air rifle lanes. In the shooting facility settings
the club can choose **Take from facilities**. Target selection in competitions then
recommends targets that suit these lanes.

## In detail

Add parts of a facility on its detail page with **Create area**, for example a hall, kitchen
or individual ranges. An area uses the address of its facility; areas cannot contain further
areas.

The detail page also shows **Equipment stored here** and **Associated equipment**. Equipment
is stored here when its location is **In a facility**. Associated equipment is linked under
**Belongs to** on the equipment item, for example a key kept by a member. Both are only
visible with equipment permission.

Photo, tasks, documents such as house rules or a lease, event links, history and the recycle
bin work as for equipment. A retired facility is hidden and can no longer be chosen as a
location.
en.seiten/material-musik.md:
---
key: page.material_music
titel: Inventory › Instruments and uniforms
modul: music
rechte: [music.view]
routen: [/material/musik]
stichworte: [Instrument, uniform, issue, return, maintenance, loan]
---

When the inventory module and inventory viewing permission are also enabled, the item **Instruments and uniforms** appears under Equipment & rooms. Editing requires both music and inventory editing permissions. **Link inventory item as music equipment** selects an existing inventory item; create items and maintain photos, documents and tasks in inventory management. Inventory number and condition remain shared. Use **Edit equipment details** for type, instrument, size/specification and the next maintenance date.

## Issue and return

**Issue equipment** assigns an item to an active musician with a return deadline and handover note. Issuing equipment to members also requires member viewing permission. The inventory location changes to that member. For guests, the location is marked for review with a reference to the music issue; the guest assignment appears in Music. Items already issued, defective or retired cannot be issued again. Overdue returns are marked.

**Record equipment return** confirms condition and destination: explicitly restore the previous storage location or enter a complete new address. Inaccessible member locations must be replaced with a valid destination. **Record maintenance** saves completed maintenance with date, condition, note and next due date. Schedule planned maintenance in equipment details. The last 100 issues and maintenance entries are displayed; general exports retain all records. Correct issues and returns through these workflows rather than Undo in inventory history. An outstanding issue prevents deletion. The inventory record links back to music equipment when music viewing permission is available.

After an inventory item with closed issues is deleted, the existing 30-day trash period applies; its music links are then removed. Items with an outstanding issue are excluded from permanent cleanup.
en.seiten/material.md:
---
key: page.material
titel: Manage equipment
modul: material
rechte: [material.view]
routen: [/material]
stichworte: [Inventory, Equipment, Location, Photo, Image, Recurring events]
---

Equipment & rooms › **Equipment** lists the items belonging to your active unit. Search by name, description
or address. Use the filters to include retired items or open the recycle bin.

![Equipment list with locations and condition](bild:material-liste)

With editing permission, create an item with a name, short description, purpose or event,
and location. The default location type is **With a member**. Select an accessible member
or enter a complete address. Everyone with
equipment viewing permission in this unit can see manually entered addresses. Save a new item with **Save**. Changes to an existing item save themselves; **Close** returns to the view.

## In detail

The form is divided into basic data, location and condition, with labels above the fields.
To select members, events, tasks or documents, enter at least two characters in **Search choices**.
A result menu opens below the field; choose the matching entry. There is no separate permanent menu.

![Equipment form with grouped input fields](bild:material-formular)

On the detail page, add, replace or remove an **Equipment photo**. JPEG, PNG and WebP
files up to 10 MB are accepted. Image metadata is removed. Viewing the image requires
equipment access.

Link multiple events, recurring series, tasks and documents. For a series, select the
whole series, one occurrence or an exclusion. An occurrence is identified by its original
start, even when rescheduled. If the recurrence rule changes, review and update its links.
Upcoming uses describe demand; they are not binding reservations.

Private tasks and inaccessible documents remain hidden. **Create a task for this item**
opens the task form and links the item when saved. Completing a transport task does not
change the location automatically: confirm the new location using **Edit**.

Under **History**, undo your most recent change if current permissions and linked objects
allow it. History and recycled items are retained for 30 days. Retiring an item preserves
its links; resolve open tasks and future uses first.

If the facilities module is enabled, the location can also be **In a facility**, for example
the clubhouse cellar. Use **Belongs to** to link an item to a facility, for example a key kept
by a member.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-aufgaben.md:
---
key: page.portal_todos
titel: My area › Tasks
rechte: []
routen: [/mein-bereich/aufgaben]
stichworte: [Task, take on, complete, shared]
---

This lists the tasks the club has shared with members, open and completed.

**Claim task** says that you will look after it; the others then see that it is taken. If you cannot do it after all, release it with **Release task**. **Refresh** reloads the list.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-auslagen.md:
---
key: page.portal_expenses
titel: My area › Expenses
modul: expenses
routen: [/mein-bereich/auslagen]
stichworte: [expense, refund, receipt, till receipt, photo, mileage, advance, donation]
---

If you paid for something for the club yourself, claim it here and get exactly that amount refunded. Choose **Claim an expense**, write what you bought and for whom, enter date and amount and add the receipt: with **Take photo** straight from your phone's camera or with **Choose file** as an image, PDF or e-invoice.

For the payout choose **Bank transfer** (account holder and IBAN, prefilled from your direct debit mandate) or **cash**. **Submit** sends the claim to the treasurer and gives it a number; **Save as draft** lets you send it later.

## In detail

If the treasurer has a query, it appears here and on the overview. Answer it, add receipts or change the details; the treasurer then reviews it again. You are notified about approval, rejection and payout by push in the app or by email. Once submitted, receipts can only be added, not deleted.

Depending on the club's settings you can also claim **Travel costs** by kilometres or request an **Advance** before buying. If the club has set a basis for expense donations, you can choose **Waive as a donation** for an approved claim and get a donation receipt instead.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-ausweis.md:
---
key: page.portal_card
titel: My area › Card
routen: [/mein-bereich/ausweis]
stichworte: [card, QR code, membership card]
---

Your membership card with QR code. Show it on your phone or print it. If you lose your phone, the club can block the card and create a new one.

## In detail

If your operator has configured Wallet and your club has switched it on, you can add
the card to Google Wallet or download an Apple Wallet pass (`.pkpass`). The pass shows
name, club, membership type, department and umbrella association in the club's colours
and with its logo, in German or English depending on the phone's language. Google
receives these details, but no photo. Apple passes do not update automatically; download them again
after changes. Scan the QR code to check current validity online. If the club creates
a new QR code, add the new pass to your wallet.

If you are the contact person of an organisation, the card shows the organisation with its logo instead of a photo, and the check page lists it as an organisation member. The card does not show who presents it.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-beitragsnachweise.md:
---
key: page.portal_fee_proofs
titel: My area › Fee proofs
modul: billing
routen: [/mein-bereich/beitragsnachweise]
stichworte: [proof, reduction, studies, certificate of enrolment, reduced fee]
---

If you pay a reduced fee, for example as a student, the club needs a current proof every year. Here you see, per fee year, by when it is due and whether it has been accepted.

Choose **Choose file or photo**, optionally pick the type of proof and click **Submit proof**. PDF files and photos up to 10 MB are allowed. Until the board has reviewed it, the reduction continues to apply. You get an email about the decision or a question.

Instead of here you can also use the link in the reminder, or reply to the reminder email with the certificate attached. If no proof arrives by the deadline, the regular fee applies for that year.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-belegung.md:
---
key: page.portal_bookings
titel: My area › Bookings
routen: [/mein-bereich/belegung]
stichworte: [Booking, Request, Clubhouse, Hall, Room, Equipment, borrow]
---

Here you see when the clubhouse, rooms or equipment that your club has opened for requests
from the members' area is booked. Other people's bookings only appear as "Booked".

Under **Make a request** you choose the item, the purpose and the time and send it with
**Send request**. The managers confirm or reject it; you then receive an email. Under
**My requests and bookings** you see the status and can cancel with **Cancel booking**.
Bookings the managers entered for you appear there too.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-bestellungen.md:
---
key: page.portal_orders
titel: My area › Orders
routen: [/mein-bereich/bestellungen]
stichworte: [Order, Group order, Club clothing, Size, Commemorative booklet]
---

Here you find the group orders of your club and your units, for example for club clothing or a
commemorative booklet. With **Order now** you enter the quantity for each item, per size where
there are sizes, and a comment if you like.

You can change or withdraw your order until the deadline. After that, or once there is an
invoice, the board helps you. If the club pays, you see no prices. You also find any invoice
under **Invoices**.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-daten.md:
---
key: page.portal_data
titel: My area › My data
routen: [/mein-bereich/daten]
stichworte: [address, change, bank details, information]
---

Here you see what the club has stored about you. You send changes, such as a new address, as a notice to the club; they apply once someone there has accepted them.

If your club has switched it on, you can also cancel your membership here. The earliest leaving date follows the notice period in the statutes; the club confirms the leaving date by email.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-firma.md:
---
key: page.portal_company
titel: My area › Employees
routen: [/mein-bereich/firma]
stichworte: [Company, Employee, report, deregister, Company fee, Employer]
---

Contact persons of a company that is a club member and pays the fee for employees see this item. You only see who belongs to the company, since when, and whether the fee is paid via the company. Address, date of birth, events and offices stay with the club.

## In detail

**Report employee**: enter first name, last name and email address and choose **Report**. The person receives an email with the link to the club's online application, completes their details and confirms the application themselves. The link is valid for 30 days. The link is only valid for the email address you entered: the person has to apply with exactly that address. Each address can receive one report per day, and a company can send 20 reports per day. Once the club admits them, they belong to the company with “Fee via the household”. If the club has not enabled an online application, report employees directly to the club.

Deregister: choose **End fee payment** for a person and enter the last day the company pays for. This is not a resignation: the membership continues, afterwards the member pays themselves. The club and the member receive an email.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-helferdienste.md:
---
key: page.portal_helpers
titel: My area › Volunteer duties
routen: [/mein-bereich/helferdienste]
stichworte: [Helper, Duty, Shift, Roster, sign up, cancel, Calendar]
---

Here you see the published duty rosters of your club and your sub-units, for example for the
festival. Each shift shows how many places are still free.

**Sign me up** takes a free shift. HUBIplan checks whether the shift is already full, whether it
overlaps with another of your duties and whether you meet the minimum age. Some rosters allow
only a certain number of shifts per person; in others only the administration assigns people.

**Cancel duty** removes you again while the cancellation deadline is open. After that the shift
shows “Cancellation only via the administration”; please contact the administration then.

**My duties** lists all shifts you are signed up for. **Add to calendar** downloads them as a
calendar file. HUBIplan sends you a reminder email before the duty if your club has set this up.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-musik.md:
---
key: page.portal_music
titel: My area › Music
modul: music
rechte: []
routen: [/mein-bereich/musik]
stichworte: [Performance, rehearsal, sheet music, absence, remuneration, response]
---

As a musician you find your performances, rehearsals, sheet music and absences here.

## Performances and rehearsals

**My performances** lists each date separately, with meeting point, uniform and programme. Respond with **Accept** or **Decline**; your current response is marked. If HUBIplan knows of a conflict with another date, it is shown as text.

## Sheet music

**Sheet music for this rehearsal** shows the files released for your part. There is no sheet music for cancelled rehearsals or after you have declined.

## Absences

Under **My absences** you enter when you are not available. Start and end are enough; you do not need to give a reason.

## Remuneration

Under **My remuneration** you only see your own approved remuneration, with **Partially paid** and **Outstanding remuneration**.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-pinnwand.md:
---
key: page.portal_pinboard
titel: My area › Notice board
routen: [/mein-bereich/pinnwand]
stichworte: [Notice board, News, Short message, Photos, Push]
---

Here you find short news from your club and your units, pinned posts at the top, otherwise the
newest first. Posts added since your last visit are marked **new**; the overview of the member area
and the app show how many new posts there are. Clicking a photo opens it in full size.

You cannot reply here, the notice board is not a chat. If you have questions, contact the person
named below the post.

If you are allowed to write to the notice board in the administration, you also see **New post**
here and can change, pin and delete posts, in the app as well.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-rechnungen.md:
---
key: page.portal_invoices
titel: My area › Invoices
routen: [/mein-bereich/rechnungen]
stichworte: [invoice, fee, paid, open]
---

This lists your invoices from the club, such as the annual fee, with their status. The club's treasurer answers questions about an invoice.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-rundschreiben.md:
---
key: page.portal_circulars
titel: My area › Messages
routen: [/mein-bereich/rundschreiben]
stichworte: [messages, circular, unsubscribe, email]
---

Here you read the messages (circulars) your club has sent you. The app calls them “Messages” too. You can unsubscribe from circulars of the “information” type; you will still receive official notices such as invitations. If your club sends birthday or anniversary greetings, you can also object to them here with **Receive greetings on birthdays and club anniversaries**.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-training.md:
---
key: page.portal_training
titel: My area › Training
routen: [/mein-bereich/training]
stichworte: [training, attendance, check-in, QR code, shooting log, shooting record, report]
---

Here you can see which practice evenings and training sessions you are recorded for and how often
you attended this year and in the last twelve months.

## Checking in

When the session leader has opened check-in, scan the QR code on their screen with the HUBIplan
app or your phone camera. You are recorded straight away. The code changes every 30 seconds;
always scan the current one.

## Shooting log

If your club keeps the shooting log, you see your shooting sessions here and the status under
section 14 of the German Weapons Act (WaffG) for acquisition (last twelve months) and possession
(last 24 months, for handguns and long guns).

Report dates outside training, for example at another club or at a competition, under
**Report a shooting date**. They only count once the club has confirmed them. A report that has not been
confirmed yet can be taken back with **Withdraw**. The board issues the confirmation for the application to the
association.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-umfragen.md:
---
key: page.portal_surveys
titel: My area › Surveys
routen: [/mein-bereich/umfragen]
stichworte: [Survey, Poll, Find a date, Meal choice, answer, anonymous]
---

Here are the surveys of your club and your subunits that ask you, open ones first. The overview
of the member area shows how many are still waiting for your answer.

Answer the questions and choose **Submit**. You can leave optional questions empty. In an open
survey you change your answer until it closes with **Change answer** or take it back with
**Withdraw answer**. An anonymous survey says so beforehand: nobody sees what you answered, not
even the administrators, and the answer cannot be changed afterwards.

Depending on the settings you see the result after answering, always or only after closing. If an
event was created from a date finder and you said “yes”, **Accept the event** accepts it for you.

With the personal link from the email you can also answer without signing in.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-versammlungen.md:
---
key: page.portal_meetings
titel: My area › Meetings
routen: [/mein-bereich/versammlungen]
stichworte: [Meeting, General meeting, Invitation, Agenda, Minutes]
---

**Invitations** lists the meetings of your club and your units to which you are invited as a
member entitled to vote, with time, place and agenda.

If your club accepts motions, the meeting shows the deadline for them. **Submit a motion** lets
you enter a title and a reason, and **Submit motion** sends it. You then see whether it was added
to the agenda or why not. Until a decision has been made, **Withdraw** takes it back.

## In detail

During the meeting: scan the QR code in the room with the app or your phone camera and tap
**I'm here**. If your club allows remote participation, the meeting shows
**To the meeting: take part online and vote**; there you tap **Take part online**. When the chair
starts a vote, choose your answer and tap **Cast vote**, with proxies for each vote. A vote once
cast cannot be changed; you see the result after the end. **I'm leaving** checks you out.

**Minutes** contains the approved minutes of recent years that your club has made available to
everyone entitled to vote. Click a title to download the minutes as a PDF. Minutes of board
meetings do not appear here.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-wettbewerbe.md:
---
key: page.portal_competitions
titel: My area › Competitions
modul: competitions
rechte: []
routen: [/mein-bereich/wettbewerbe, /mein-bereich/gemeldet, /mein-bereich/ergebnisse]
stichworte: [Competition, entry, result, place, title, shooting]
---

Your entries and your results are on one page here.

At the top you see which competitions you are entered for, with the organiser and whether the entry is confirmed. Below, **All starts and awards** lists your results so far with your place, and **Titles and winners** your titles. As long as you have not competed anywhere, the list stays empty.
en.seiten/mein-bereich.md:
---
key: page.portal
titel: My area › Overview
routen: [/mein-bereich]
stichworte: [member, my details, overview]
---

This is your area as a member. Here you find your card, your invoices, messages and the data the club has stored about you. Your club decides which of these appear.

As the contact person of an organisation you see the organisation's data here and report changes for it; first name, date of birth and gender do not apply. If you are also a member yourself, **My account** lists both areas separately, the organisation's with the addition “as contact person”.

## In detail

You can reach your card, events and invoices from any other view too: under **My account** at the top right, the **My area** section lists **My ID card**, **My events** and **My invoices**. If you are a member of several clubs, each club is listed by name. The unit picker at the top only shows the areas you help run.

Under **Competitions** you find your entries (“What am I entered for?”) and your results on one page.

When the music module is enabled, here and, as a musician, under the item **Music** you also find your performances, rehearsals, sheet music and absences also appear here. Individual events are separated; meeting details, uniform and response status are labelled. **Accept** and **Decline** mark your current response. Known availability conflicts are also shown in text.

Under **Messages**, read received circulars with paragraphs, emphasis, lists and links. Attachments are listed by filename with the open circular. A link from the Android app returns to this exact circular and membership access after browser sign-in if needed. **To the overview** closes it; browser Back also works. Retry is available if loading fails.

The information-email setting confirms successful changes. You still receive official notices. If a change fails, the last confirmed setting is retained.

![Received circular with formatted text and an attachment](bild:mitteilungen-lesen)
en.seiten/mein-konto-anmeldung.md:
---
key: page.account_login
titel: My account › Sign-in & security
routen: [/mein-konto/anmeldung]
stichworte: [password, two-factor, 2FA, authenticator, delete account]
---

This is where you change your password and switch **Two-factor authentication** on or off. With it,
signing in needs a code from your phone in addition to your password. Anyone who manages roles,
runs exports, posts in the cash book, may see all members or reads the change log and outbox has
to set it up; for platform administration this applies immediately. Before sensitive actions such
as a full export HUBIplan asks for a code again (guide “Set up two-factor authentication”).

## Email, confirmation and lockout

A new address under **Change sign-in email** only takes effect once you have confirmed it with the link sent to the new
address. If you have no password of your own and only sign in with links, you also have to confirm
the change with the link sent to your previous address. After the change your other browsers are
signed out; the app stays connected.

To confirm, HUBIplan asks for your HUBIplan password, not the password of your email mailbox.
You have five attempts per hour for the sign-in email and ten for the password. After that the
message tells you in how many minutes you can try again. The hour starts with the first attempt.

If someone enters a wrong password for your account several times in a row, signing in with a
password is blocked for a few minutes, but only on unknown devices. On devices you have signed in
with before, and with a passkey, you can still get in. You will receive an email about it.

## Delete account

Under **Delete account** you delete your account yourself, with passkeys, connected devices, authorisations for Nextcloud and AI assistants and your personal tasks. To confirm, enter your login email; as with other sensitive actions, HUBIplan also asks for your passkey, code or password. If you only sign in with links, delete the account within 10 minutes of signing in.

This is not possible while you hold roles: have them ended in the club first. What your club keeps about you as a member remains; you can only leave or request deletion of your member data with the club. A Nextcloud account you sign in to through HUBIplan is deactivated if the club has switched on “Disable accounts automatically”; otherwise the Nextcloud administration removes it.

If your account has had no access for 90 days (no member access, no role), HUBIplan deletes it
automatically. You receive an email two weeks before. If you get access again before then, the
account is kept.

A sign-in in the browser lasts twelve hours. Ten minutes before, HUBIplan asks; **Stay signed in**
lets you keep working without interruption. If the session has already expired, the page stays as
it is with your input: sign in again with **Sign in in a new tab**, come back and choose
**I am signed in again**.

This is where you connect the HUBIplan app on your phone to your account and see which devices are connected. You disconnect a device you no longer use here. Below, you link accounts on other HUBIplan instances so you can sign in there with this account.

Under “AI assistants” you find the address for connecting an AI assistant such as Claude or ChatGPT, and the list of connected assistants. You end a connection with **Disconnect** (see [Connect AI assistants to HUBIplan](/hilfe/ki-assistent-verbinden)).

If your app access or devices cannot be retrieved, the error offers **Reload**. Only a successfully loaded empty device list means that no device is connected.

routen: [/mein-konto/benachrichtigungen]
stichworte: [Tasks, Reminders, Email, Push]
---

Set your task sharing notices and email and push reminders here. These defaults apply to your account across all units. Each task with a due date can have its own channels and reminder times. Due tasks remain highlighted even when messages are disabled.

You can hide task titles in push messages. You can also choose to move completed private one-off tasks to the trash after twelve months. This retention option starts disabled; recurring task history is retained.
en.seiten/mein-konto-briefvorlage.md:

As a board member or with a role in a sub-unit, you create a Word template here with your unit's letterhead, your position and how to reach you. You can also store a signature that HUBIplan puts on receipts, for example.
en.seiten/mein-konto.md:
---
key: page.account
titel: My account › Profile
routen: [/mein-konto]
stichworte: [profile, name, language, appearance, dark mode, quick actions, learning aids]
---

This is where you set everything that only concerns you: your name, the **Display language** and
whether HUBIplan shows you learning aids. The settings apply in every unit you work in.

## In detail

Under **Appearance** you choose **Light**, **Dark** or **Same as device**. Without a choice of your own, HUBIplan is light. This applies to all pages, including administration (such as members or finances). With **Same as device**, HUBIplan follows the setting of your phone or computer. The choice applies on all devices where you are signed in. In the dark, HUBIplan adjusts the club colours so that links and buttons stay easy to read. Below that, **The “?” key opens help for this page** switches the keyboard shortcut off, for example if you work with voice input; this applies to this browser.

Under **Home**, **Show quick actions on the home page** decides whether the home page shows its buttons. You choose which actions appear, and in which order, on the home page under **Customise**. If you made a selection of your own there, **Show the suggestion everywhere** restores your roles' suggestion in all units.

Open the other sections through **My account** at the top right, for example **Sign-in & security**
for your password and two-factor authentication. The same menu shows your email address and lets you **Sign out**.
en.seiten/meldungen.md:
---
key: page.entries
titel: Entries
modul: entries
rechte: [entries.submit, entries.manage]
routen: [/meldungen]
stichworte: [entry, invitation to tender, team, organiser, registration]
---

Under Entries you register teams, people and details with an organiser, for example for a tournament or a competition. You can send the entry as a letter, email or spreadsheet, report changes later and pass a call for entries on to your own sub-units. In the menu, entries are listed under Competitions; if you have no competitions, they are a menu item of their own. If your umbrella association offers events with group registration, they are listed at the top under **Group registrations with the umbrella association**; you register at the event in the calendar.

When creating a call for entries, your input is saved only when you choose **Create**. If you cancel or leave after changing something, HUBIplan asks for confirmation. **Continue editing** retains your input; **Discard** leaves the draft without saving.

## In detail

If results from a linked competition cannot be loaded, **Reload** retries the request. When no competition is linked to a call for entries, the results section remains hidden.

With English selected, submission methods, validation hints, statuses and form actions are also shown in English. Your titles, club details and previously generated correspondence retain their content or the club language.
en.seiten/mitglieder-aemter.md:
---
key: page.members_offices
titel: Members › Offices
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/aemter, /mitglieder/aemter/statistik, /mitglieder/aemter/import]
stichworte: [office, board, position, term]
---

This lists the unit's offices, such as chair, treasurer or secretary, with their holders and terms. Offices are not rights: what someone may do in HUBIplan is set by the roles under Settings.

With **Assign** you give an office to a new person, for example after the annual general meeting. You pick the person from the member list and the date. The dialog says beforehand whether the role has permissions and where an invitation goes. If the office is held, it ends the predecessor’s term on the day before; the box is ticked by default. Afterwards it points to the imprint and letterhead if the role appears there.

## Choose the unit

At the top, pick the club or a sub-unit, such as a platoon, under **Unit**. Offices of a sub-unit are assigned the same way with **Assign**; no account is created and no email is sent. Current holders are ended there with **End**. The sub-unit’s page and its workspace show the same list under “Who has which role?”.

## Statistics

The Statistics tab shows under **People by years in office** who held an office for how long, and per office the holders by years. This helps with honours and the chronicle.

## Import former office holders

**Import former office holders** reads an Excel or CSV file with earlier terms of office, for example from an old board list. The page names the columns the file needs. This does not create any permissions in HUBIplan.
en.seiten/mitglieder-aenderungen.md:
---
key: page.members_changes
titel: Members › Data changes
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/anfragen/aenderungen]
stichworte: [change, address, member area, review]
---

Members report changed details in the member area, such as a new address or bank account. Here you review each notice and apply it to the record or decline it. Nothing changes in the record until you agree.
en.seiten/mitglieder-akte.md:
---
key: page.member_file
titel: Members › Member record
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/:id]
stichworte: [record, master data, periods, leaving, honours]
---

The tabs follow the order of work: **Personal data**, **Membership**, **Fees**, **Roles and account**, **Competitions**, **Music**, **Photo & website**, **Additional fields** and **History**. Tabs for modules that are switched off are hidden. **Photo & website** brings together the photo, photo requests, publication and the membership card. **Music** shows a short musician profile with the instruments; edit it via **Open in music area**.

Issued equipment is listed under **Membership**. On a phone, choose the section from the **Area** list. The header shows the name, photo (otherwise the initials), status, membership number, membership type, units and current offices. **Call** and **Email** appear when a phone number or email address is recorded. **More actions** holds request photo, print membership card, record leaving, and access report and deletion.

![Member record with header, “At a glance” and tabs](bild:mitgliedsakte)

## At a glance

At the top, **At a glance** shows up to four tiles: **Member since** (with duration and next jubilee), **Fees** (open invoices and total, marked red when overdue), **Account** (member area, app, two-factor, last sign-in) and **Equipment** (items issued). A tile only appears if you may see the matching tab and there is something to show; clicking it opens the tab.

## Master data

Next to gender is the **Title**: choose Dr., Dr. Dr., Prof. or Prof. Dr., or enter your own with **other title …** (e.g. Dipl.-Ing.). The title appears in the record header, in the addresses of letters and invoices (“Dr. Max Muster”) and in the formal salutation of circulars (“Sehr geehrter Herr Dr. Muster”); the informal salutation stays without a title. On the website it only appears if “Show titles before names” is switched on there. HUBIplan copies an additional field “Titel” into the fixed field once; the additional field remains.

## Organisations and contacts

For an organisation as a member (company, association, public body …), the master data show the name addition, legal form, register, VAT ID, website and size (e.g. employees or inhabitants) for fees by size instead of first name, date of birth and gender. In the member list, filter with **organisations only** or **persons only**.

In the **Contact persons** section you record who speaks for the organisation. Choose **Select member** if the person is a member themselves; name and contact details then come from their file. Otherwise enter name, function, email address and phone. Exactly one is the **Primary contact**. The settings **receives circulars**, **receives invoices**, **represents at meetings** define who is responsible for what.

You set up a separate member area login for each contact person on the **Roles and account** tab; contacts who have one are marked **Member access**. If the contact person is a member themselves, they choose after signing in whether they act for themselves or for the organisation. Instead of a photo, an organisation has a **Logo**; it needs no consent and also appears on the membership card. When you remove a contact person, their contact details are deleted immediately.

## Guardians, household and company

For members under 18 the section is called **Legal guardians**. There you enter parents or a legal guardian, freely or as a linked member. With **receives circulars** they also get circulars to the child by email. You set up their login on the **Roles and account** tab, as for contact persons; parents with several children choose after signing in whom they act for.

Four weeks before the 18th birthday the guardians get an email (once, even if a day was missed); on the birthday their access and entry end automatically. If only the year of birth is known, 31 December applies. If a member under 16 uploads a photo themselves (link or app), their tick does not count as consent: the photo waits until you record the guardians’ consent and approve it. Through a guardian’s login the consent counts.

If the person belongs to a household or a company, the Master data tab shows a section with its name, their role and the other members. You assign and remove them under [Members › Households and companies](/mitglieder/haushalte).

When you edit existing contact persons, legal guardians and billing details, HUBIplan saves automatically; **Close** ends editing. New entries are added with **Save**.

## Fees and billing address

The **Fees** tab lists the member’s invoices with the outstanding amount and, if SEPA is switched on, their mandates (with the right to view fees and invoices). Open an invoice by its number.

In the **Fees** tab, under **Billing address**, you set where invoices and reminders go if not to the member's address, e.g. a company's accounts department, a town's treasury or a child's parents. It also holds the billing email, purchase order number and Leitweg-ID; the last two are printed on every invoice. Without a separate billing address, an invoice to an organisation is marked “attn.” of the contact person marked “receives invoices”, and the email goes to them.

## Membership and history

The record shows everything about a person: master data, memberships with periods and membership types, honours, offices, contact details, SEPA mandate and photo. Changes are saved shortly after you type; you can undo them at the top right if needed. You record leaving as the end of the membership; the record is kept. Honours are in the **Membership** tab. In the **Roles and account** tab you see the person's roles and enable or block the member area. **Assign role** opens the same dialog as under Members › Offices.

In the **Membership** tab, use **Edit** next to a unit membership to correct its start and end dates, including past memberships. A blank end date means the membership continues. Apply the correction with **Save**. Overlaps with other unit memberships are checked. To add a past membership in one step, pick the unit, enter “from” and “until”, then click **Add**. Without “until”, the membership runs until today. Units that are no longer active are listed too, marked “(inactive)”; for them “until” is required. If HUBIplan reports an overlap, it names the affected membership with its exact dates; the check works by day even when the file shows only years.

## Data protection

Under **Privacy** you can download the access report as a ZIP. For former members, this is also where you delete their data on request. As after the deletion period, only the name, year of birth and membership periods then remain, for the club's history. If the person objects to that too, “Remove name from chronicle and honours” then removes their name from dignities, companions, honours and competition results, including start lists, shoot-offs, entries and prizes. Photos of these dignities are deleted as well. Afterwards the person no longer appears by name on any public page: all objections under **Photo & website** apply and all consents end.
