en.seiten/mitglieder.md:
---
key: page.members
titel: Members
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder]
stichworte: [member list, search, filter, export]
---

The list shows all members of the selected unit. At the top you search by name, email or
number; next to it you filter by status, membership type or gender. Clicking a name opens the
record with all periods, honours and contact details.

## In detail

Each search word must match, but one may occur in the name and another in the email
address or number. Email addresses are found by the full address (`erika@example.org`) or
from the @ onwards (`@example.org` for everyone with that domain); parts without @ only
search names and numbers. Names are searched without regard to case, and `ß` and `ss` are
treated alike. Name sorting places umlauts with their base letter (`ä` with `a`).
Equal names have a fixed order so that moving between pages remains stable.

![The member list with search and filters](bild:mitglieder-liste)

On a phone, search stays visible. The Filters button opens status, membership type and other restrictions; the number indicates how many filters are set. **More actions** contains export and membership cards. For organisations, the Excel export contains type, name suffix, legal form and the primary contact; all contact persons are on the second sheet “Ansprechpartner”.

The separate billing address with billing email, purchase order number and Leitweg-ID can be included as columns of their own. **Per page** lets you choose 10, 20 or 50 results; phones initially show 10. For multiple pages, navigation is available above and below the results. Your selection and page size are retained when you open a record and return. Small screens show name and membership type; open the record for other details.
en.seiten/musik-musiker.md:
---
key: page.music_musicians
titel: Music › Musicians
modul: music
rechte: [music.view]
routen: [/musik/musiker]
stichworte: [Musician, guest, instrument, part, section, skill]
---

Create a musician from an existing member or enter a guest name and contact details. Pick the member via the search: type at least two letters of the name and click a match. The member record shows a short profile with the instruments on its **Music** tab and leads here via **Open in music area**. Record instruments and sections or parts under **Instrumental skills**, marking the main instrument. Deactivate guests when no longer needed.
en.seiten/musik-noten.md:
---
key: page.music_scores
titel: Music › Sheet music library
modul: music
rechte: [music.view]
routen: [/musik/noten]
stichworte: [Sheet music, piece, arrangement, part, import, CSV, repertoire, licence]
---

Open **Music** → **Sheet music library**. Create pieces with composers, then editions/arrangements with arrangers, publishers, duration in seconds, difficulty, instrumentation and licence notes. Archive unused arrangements. Record required musicians, copy counts, storage locations and concert or march book format for each instrument and part. Record full scores separately. Stocks at multiple locations are added together for the same part; the highest player requirement applies.

With **In the repertoire on the website** a piece appears with title and composer in the “Repertoire” section of the club website. Switch the section on under **Website** → **Menu and pages**.

## Digital sheet music

Upload digital files in the existing document library, then link them to an arrangement and optionally a part under **Sheet music documents**. Document viewing permission is also required to link and open files. Access changes and deletions apply immediately. Music permissions do not extend document access. Record licence and usage notes; a stock count or file does not grant copying or performance rights.

## Import a catalogue

Use **Import sheet music catalogue** to select a UTF-8 CSV up to 2 MB with at most 1000 data rows. The **Download CSV template** lists all columns; `title` and `arrangement` are required. Use semicolons or commas as separators. Each row describes an arrangement and optionally stock for an instrumental part. Without an instrument, only the arrangement is created. **Preview import** shows new pieces, arrangements, stock and errors without saving anything.

**Import reviewed sheet music catalogue** explicitly imports the reviewed data together. Identical entries are skipped; conflicting details, changed stock counts or ambiguous existing entries must be resolved first. Existing details and archived arrangements are not overwritten or reactivated. Create a new preview if the file or catalogue changes; previews expire after 30 minutes. Add digital sheet music through the existing document library.
en.seiten/musik-proben.md:
---
key: page.music_rehearsals
titel: Music › Rehearsals and sheet music checkout
modul: music
rechte: [music.view]
routen: [/musik/proben]
stichworte: [Rehearsal, programme, checkout, return, guest]
---

Open **Rehearsals and sheet music checkout** and link events or series from your own calendar. Dates, location, recurrence and cancellations remain in the existing calendar. Rehearsal focus and pieces form the shared series template. Assign musicians and deactivate assignments no longer required. Administrators record guest responses.

## Rehearsal programme

Under **Upcoming rehearsals**, open **Edit rehearsal programme** for an occurrence. **This occurrence only** saves its own focus and pieces, including an empty programme. **Entire series** loads and changes the shared template; occurrences with their own programmes keep their contents. **Use series programme** removes the override and inherits the current template again. Rehearsal planning and rehearsal pieces continue to edit the template. Moved occurrences keep their programmes. After a recurrence rule change, programmes without a matching original start need to be planned again. Programme changes preserve attendance responses.

The overview covers the past 14 days and next 90 days. Each response belongs to the original occurrence start from the calendar rule, including moved occurrences. Changing the series rule requires new responses. Cancelled or started rehearsals cannot be answered. Missing responses are visible.

## What members see

Current members with an active musician profile see their own rehearsals and performances with their effective programmes and focus under **My area**. **Sheet music for this rehearsal** shows matching permitted files. Downloads still require the document library’s member permissions and a matching part or skill. Removed pieces no longer grant access unless another own event needs them. Rehearsals use the displayed past 14 and next 90 days; cancelled rehearsals and declined invitations grant no sheet music access. Restricted, deleted and unrelated files remain inaccessible.

## Sheet music checkout

Record musician, part, quantity and return date for checkouts. Each checkout reduces available stock. Partial returns are recorded with timestamps. Outstanding checkouts prevent reducing or repurposing stock. Overdue returns are highlighted; members see their own outstanding quantities. Preparation distinguishes available copies from copies already held by assigned musicians.

## Notices and reminders

New rehearsal assignments and upcoming pending responses generate neutral notices through the existing outbox. The hourly job reminds once per occurrence within the configured number of days; 0 disables reminders. Notices link to the member area and contain no sheet music attachments or confidential event details. Guests without member access do not receive these notices. Preparation tasks and other calendar communication remain in the existing task/calendar workspace.

## Rehearsal guests

In the rehearsal overview, **Guest invitation** creates a personal link for exactly one occurrence. Series occurrences can have separate links. Share links confidentially. Guests can only accept or decline their own assigned occurrence. Links can be rotated or revoked and expire within 180 days. Changing a guest email revokes rehearsal and performance links. Document managers with edit rights may explicitly share matching sheet music from the current programme.

Check usage rights first. A grant covers the selected file version; later uploads are not shared automatically. Downloads stop when the guest declines, the event is cancelled, the piece leaves the programme, the document is deleted or moved, or the grantor loses permission. Performance invitations support the same sharing. Department documents and documents from other organisations cannot be shared this way.

General exports include rehearsal, response and checkout data.
en.seiten/musik-uebersicht.md:
---
key: page.music_overview
titel: Music › Overview
modul: music
rechte: [music.view]
routen: [/musik/uebersicht]
stichworte: [Performance overview, responses, conflicts, preparation]
---

**Performance overview** combines staffing, pending responses, known conflicts, sheet music requirements and permitted settlement issues. Select a period and choose **Update overview** when needed. Each issue links to staffing, the programme or the performance settlement. “Prepared” refers only to information you can access; it does not confirm attendance. Missing planning details remain open. Finance issues require cashbook read access. Cancelled performances are marked separately. Each page shows twelve performances.
en.seiten/musik-verfuegbarkeit.md:
---
key: page.music_availability
titel: Music › Availability
modul: music
rechte: [music.view]
routen: [/musik/verfuegbarkeit]
stichworte: [Absence, holiday, conflict, overlap]
---

Under **Availability**, manage absences for active members and guests. Members can manage **My absences** in their own area. Only start and end are recorded, without reasons. Adjacent periods do not overlap. Other known performances including meeting and setup time, rehearsal series and accepted calendar events in the same association are considered. Individual declines and moved occurrences take effect immediately. Other associations and private calendars without an association response are not checked; plan travel and buffer time yourself.

Planning shows **Absent**, **Scheduling conflict**, **Declined this event** or **No known conflict**, without revealing private calendar content. Assignment and acceptance check again before saving. No known conflict does not constitute acceptance. Later changes highlight conflicts for existing assignments without automatically changing responses or remuneration. Decline the assignment separately if needed.
en.seiten/musik-vorlagen.md:
---
key: page.music_templates
titel: Music › Instrumentation templates
modul: music
rechte: [music.view]
routen: [/musik/vorlagen]
stichworte: [Instrumentation, template, staffing, part]
---

Under **Instrumentation templates**, use **Create template** to store instruments, parts and required player counts. Each part may appear only once. Clear **Active** to archive a template. Editing requires music editing permission; read-only users can view templates.

How to apply a template to a performance is described in the help for Music › Performances under “Staffing and assignments”.
en.seiten/musik.md:
---
key: page.music
titel: Music › Performances
modul: music
rechte: [music.view]
routen: [/musik]
stichworte: [Music, performance, staffing, guest, fee, settlement, programme]
---

Plan performances here: staffing, programme, guests and settlement. The other music items are in the sidebar: Overview, Availability, Musicians, Rehearsals and sheet music checkout, Sheet music library and Instrumentation templates. Changes to existing entries save automatically; create new entries with **Save**.

## Create a performance

Create an individual event in your own calendar, then select it under **Performances**. Add customer, meeting time and place, setup, uniform, formation and notes. Performance times and location remain in the calendar. Use individual events for recurring performances. Open **Performance tasks** to manage tasks through the existing task workspace.

The search field is named after the view, for example **Search performances** or **Search musicians**, and filters it, for example by name, instrument or performance. Add new items with the matching button, such as **New performance**; an empty view explains what belongs there and offers the same button. **Search sheet music** filters the current library view. Empty lists and searches without matches show a message. Performance cards group programme, instrumentation, settlement, tasks and calendar links; detail pages show the associated performance above the heading. Totals and programme durations appear in labelled summaries. Responses and availability conflicts use consistent text badges, including in the member area.

## Staffing and assignments

Record required player counts per instrument and part, then assign musicians with matching skills. Each musician can be assigned once per performance. The overview counts accepted and missing players per position.

Open **Plan instrumentation** for a performance, select an active template and review its positions. **Apply template** adds missing parts and increases required counts if needed. Other positions and existing assignments and responses are preserved. Resolve ambiguous duplicate positions first. **Save performance instrumentation as template** copies the required positions into a new template without musicians or responses. Template changes affect performances only when applied again.

Under **Batch assignment**, select multiple matching active members or guests. Choose one position for multi-instrumentalists; each musician profile is assigned only once. Pending and accepted assignments reserve places. Already assigned musicians and existing declines are not offered again; edit their existing assignment individually.

**Request selected musicians** creates pending assignments. If the selection exceeds available places, contains invalid references, lacks skills or has known availability conflicts, nothing from the request is saved. Retries create no duplicate assignments. Existing calendar permissions apply to performances. General exports include templates.

## Replacements

For a declined assignment, open **Find replacement** under **Plan instrumentation**. Conflict-free musicians with matching parts are offered, with matching primary instruments first. Select and request a replacement; the earlier decline remains. **Show all candidates** exits the filter; **Reset selection** discards an unsaved selection. General exports include absences.

## Responses and reminders

Members can accept or decline their assignments under **My area**. Calendar cancellations remain visible. Calendar access restrictions also apply to performance administration.

Active members with enabled member access receive neutral outbox notices for new performance assignments, changes to dates, meeting details, instrumentation positions or programmes, and cancellations. The background service checks every five minutes and combines intermediate changes. Messages contain only the member-area link. Existing assignments do not generate another initial invitation when the feature is introduced. Guests receive automatic notices only after an explicit guest invitation is sent.

For each performance, **Reminder days before (0 = off)** sets the reminder window for pending responses (0 to 30 days, default 3). It uses the earliest meeting, setup or performance time. Each current information version receives at most one reminder, no earlier than one day after an invitation or change. Accepted or declined assignments and past or cancelled performances are not reminded. Failed deliveries are retried; failed attempts remain visible in the outbox.

## Invite guests

For guests, open **Plan instrumentation** → **Manage guest invitation**, create a personal link and share it confidentially. Guests need no account and see only their own assignment, meeting details, setup, uniform, formation and programme. They can accept or decline; known conflicts prevent acceptance. Other musicians, contact information and settlements remain hidden. Links expire seven days after the performance, with a maximum lifetime of 180 days. **Revoke invitation link** blocks access immediately; **Create new invitation link** replaces the previous link. Changing the guest email address revokes existing links.

To send an invitation, enter the musician's **Email address for guest invitations** and explicitly choose **Send guest invitation**. This also enables change notices and reminders while access remains active. Creating or copying a link alone does not enable automatic email. Personal links are redacted in the outbox; reopen guest management to share them again. If delivery fails, retry or share the link confidentially.

## Musical programme

Open **Musical programme** on a performance. Add pieces and encores with an arrangement, and breaks with their own duration. A blank duration uses the arrangement duration; an explicit value overrides it. Edit, remove and move items up/down. Regular duration includes breaks; encore and total durations are shown separately. Zero indicates an unknown duration and is highlighted.

Preparation compares required instruments and parts against planned instrumentation and active musicians who accepted assignments. Names are compared without case sensitivity or surrounding whitespace; different instrument names remain distinct. Missing musicians, planned counts and missing copies in the chosen format are visible. Copies in the other format do not count. Repeated pieces need one set per format. Missing instrumentation is highlighted. Changes to stock and arrangement duration affect existing programmes.

For each performance, **Programme list as PDF** and **Parts list as PDF** complement the existing CSV exports. Printouts include performance, location, creation timestamp and page numbers. The programme lists order, breaks, encores and durations; the parts list shows format, available and missing copies, copies held by assigned musicians, missing musicians, storage locations and licence notes. Check current stock and usage rights before printing.

Download programme and part lists as CSV. Use **Sheet music preparation tasks** to create preparation tasks linked to the event in the existing task workspace. Programmes require music and calendar viewing permissions; editing requires music editing permission. General exports include the catalogue and programmes. Digital files remain in the existing document export.

## Performance settlement

Open **Performance settlement** from the performance. Music and calendar viewing permissions and the enabled cash book with finance viewing permission are required. Editing requires finance editing permission. Record the agreed fee, travel costs and additional services as gross amounts in EUR. With invoice editing permission, create a draft in the existing e-invoice editor. The customer and total gross amount must match the agreement. Enter net amounts, tax categories and invoice details explicitly, then validate, issue, send and manage receipts using the invoice workspace. Each performance links one customer invoice.

Record fees, allowances and documented expenses per assignment. Confirm attendance after the performance, then approve remuneration. Approved amounts are locked. Before payment, void approval and reopen the draft for corrections. Members see only their own approved remuneration in their personal area. Finance administrators handle guest remuneration.

Record payments with receipts as expenses in the cash book first. Search the booking text and link each matching booking in full. Each remuneration permits multiple partial payments up to the outstanding balance. Link other performance expenses in the same way. Each booking can be used once. Linking does not initiate a bank transfer.

Reverse incorrect payments in the cash book. The original link remains visible, while the outstanding balance increases and can be linked to a corrected payment. The overview distinguishes agreed and invoiced amounts, actual income and expenses and their cash result. Approved remuneration is shown separately and does not indicate a completed payment.

Use **Replace cancelled invoice** after fully cancelling the customer invoice. Then correct the agreement and create a replacement invoice. Previous invoices remain linked and traceable in the audit export.

General exports and financial audit exports include agreements, remuneration and booking links. Financial retention and anonymization include settlement notes.

## Fee templates and partial payouts

Under **Performance settlement** → **Musician remuneration**, finance editors can **Manage fee templates**. Templates contain fee and allowance amounts in EUR. Archiving prevents new use; existing remuneration retains its copied amounts.

For a batch settlement, select an active template and assignments without existing remuneration. **Select all without remuneration** selects assignments without confirming attendance. Confirm attendance separately for each musician. **Create remuneration drafts** creates drafts with expenses set to zero. Add actual expenses and check attendance individually, then approve after the performance as usual. Invalid selections are rejected together. Existing remuneration is never overwritten.

You can assign multiple recorded payouts from Finance to an approved remuneration claim. Each booking is used fully and only once and must not exceed the outstanding amount. **Partially paid**, **Paid** and **Outstanding remuneration** also show the current balance in the member's own area. An active partial payment prevents approval reversal. Reversing the booking in Finance increases the outstanding amount again. Assigning a booking does not initiate a bank transfer.

## Offers and confirmations

Open **Offers and confirmations** from a performance settlement. First complete the customer address and gross amounts. Check expiry date and agreements before issuing the offer PDF. Issued PDFs and checksums preserve their original content. A new offer supersedes a pending offer. Invoice numbering is separate. Issuing does not send mail. Record the customer's actual acceptance with evidence, then issue an order confirmation.

Repeated issuance returns the same confirmation. Firm confirmation locks agreed amounts and performance details. Record cancellation with a reason before making changes and issuing a new offer. Original PDFs remain as evidence after cancellation. Calendar changes do not alter archived documents. These documents are not invoices. Finance readers can inspect documents; issuance and status changes require finance and music edit rights. PDFs use the existing letterhead.

## Who may do what?

The platform enables Music per organization. Roles need music viewing or editing permission. Performances also require calendar viewing permission.
en.seiten/noten.md:
---
key: page.scores
titel: Sheet music
modul: scores
rechte: [scores.view]
routen: [/noten]
stichworte: [Noten, Notenarchiv, Notenbestand, Chor, Arrangement, Stimme]
---

# Sheet music

The sheet music archive manages pieces, arrangements, parts and digital scores. Without the Music module, for example in a choir without performance planning, it appears as its own **Sheet music** entry in the sidebar; with Music you find it under Music › Sheet music library.

Anyone with the right “Maintain sheet music library” may edit it. Roles with music rights can read the inventory so that programmes and rehearsals can pick arrangements.

**Import sheet music catalogue** takes over an existing catalogue from a CSV file. Upload digital scores in the document storage and link them to an arrangement under **Sheet music documents**.

## Music folders for the app

Under **Music folders** you create fixed folders such as a **March book** or the **Repertoire**. Each folder holds arrangements in a fixed order, optionally with a number (“No. 27”). Use ↑ and ↓ to change the order.

Musicians find the folders in the “HUBIplan” app under **Sheet music** and can search by title, composer or number there. Everyone only sees the parts for their own voice, and only files that the document storage shares with members. Without a selection under **Visible to**, all musicians see the folder; otherwise only members of the chosen sub-units.

If a piece has several files for one voice (for example page 1 and 2 as images), **Order when there are several files** under **Sheet music documents** sets the order in which they are shown.

## Music files: PDF, images, MusicXML and MIDI

Upload sheet music in the document storage. Besides PDF, JPEG and PNG, HUBIplan understands MusicXML (`.musicxml`, `.mxl`, `.xml`) and the open formats MEI and ABC. MuseScore, Capella, Sibelius and Finale export MusicXML (usually under “Export” or “Save as”).

- From a MusicXML score, each musician only gets their own part. HUBIplan picks the part by the instrument and register of the link. If that is not unambiguous, enter the part’s name as it appears in the file under **Sheet music documents** in **Part in the MusicXML score (empty: by instrument)**.
- In the browser, MusicXML music opens as a PDF. In the app it is engraved to fit the screen and can be transposed.
- Link MIDI files (`.mid`) as listening examples. For MusicXML music, HUBIplan creates the listening example itself.

## Leading in the app

The conductor, bandleader or drum major can send the next piece to all musicians in the app; the devices then jump to each musician’s own part. Anyone allowed to edit music can do this, as well as anyone entered under **Leading in the app**: for a music folder (under **Show pieces**), for a performance under **Plan instrumentation**, or for a rehearsal.
en.seiten/pinnwand.md:
---
key: page.pinboard
titel: Notice board
modul: pinboard
rechte: [pinboard.view, pinboard.edit]
routen: [/pinnwand]
stichworte: [Notice board, News, Short message, Message, Messenger group, Push, Photo, Party photos]
---

The notice board is for short news to members, such as “The bus leaves 10 minutes later today”
or photos from the party. It sits between the formal circular and a messenger group: members see
the posts in the member area and in the app but cannot reply. There is no chat and there are no
comments.

## Writing a post

Under **New post** you write a text of up to 2,000 characters and attach up to six photos if you
like (JPEG, PNG or WebP, at most 10 MB each). **Publish** shows the post to the members right away.

- **Pin to the top** keeps important posts above all others until you remove them with **Unpin**.
- **Show until (optional)** hides the post from members after that day.
- **Send a push notification to the app** sends a short notification to all members with the app
  and notifications switched on. No email is ever sent; use circulars for that.

Changing the text, pinning and deleting is available below each post. Anyone allowed to write can
also do so in the member area and in the app under **Notice board**, so on the go from a phone.

## Who sees what

Posts of the club are seen by all current members. Posts of a unit (such as a platoon) are seen
only by its members, including those of the units below it. Each post shows who wrote it.

Writing requires the **Notice board** right for editing. Roles that edit circulars or events have
it from the start; you can change it under Settings › Roles. The notice board is a module and can
be switched on and off under Settings › Modules.

## Clean-up

You still see expired posts here for 30 days, then HUBIplan deletes them together with their
photos. Posts without “Show until” disappear after a year, pinned ones only once you unpin them.
en.seiten/plattform.md:
---
key: page.platform
titel: Platform
modul: platform
rechte: [platform.manage]
routen: [/plattform]
stichworte: [platform, create club, umbrella association, enable modules, self-update]
---

Platform administration creates clubs and umbrella associations on this HUBIplan instance and enables modules. When creating one, a person receives the “board” role with all rights and then manages roles and users themselves.

In the list of units, each unit shows the number of enabled modules (“12 modules”); click it to see them one by one.

Under settings you set the deletion period after leaving. A shorter period only applies 30 days after the change. Until then, data is still deleted after the longer one, so that a typo does not immediately delete the data of former members.

## Deactivating or deleting units

Under **Units** → **Edit**, clear “is active” and save to deactivate a unit. Its data is retained and the unit can be activated again later.

Deletion happens in two stages:

1. **Deactivate and schedule deletion**: in the edit form, enter the full name under “Delete unit”. The unit and all subunits below it are deactivated immediately; nobody can access them any more and the data is retained. While deletion is scheduled the unit cannot be activated again; **Withdraw scheduling** cancels it.
2. **Delete permanently**: at the earliest 30 days after scheduling (an empty unit that never had members or financial data straight away) and only once the statutory retention periods for books and vouchers of all financial years have expired (§ 147 AO: vouchers 8, books 10 years). The form shows until when the periods run. A deletion hold on a financial year prevents deletion. To confirm, enter the name; HUBIplan also asks for a current two-factor code. If the unit has financial data, state who confirmed the retention periods (e.g. auditor or tax advisor).

Permanent deletion removes the members, roles, financial records and stored files of the unit and its subunits. User accounts are retained. Clubs belonging to a federation must be deleted or moved first. If references from other units prevent deletion, an error is shown and the data is retained. The deletion is recorded in the platform audit log and on the deletion list: if an older backup is restored later, HUBIplan deletes the unit again.

## New versions

Once a day HUBIplan asks GitHub whether a newer release is available. If so, you see the notice “A newer version of HUBIplan is available” at the top, with a link to the changes. None of your data goes to GitHub; GitHub only sees the server's IP address, and the platform's privacy policy mentions this. Whoever runs the server can switch the check off with `HUBIPLAN_UPDATE_CHECK=0` in the `.env`. Once the new release is running, the changes are listed under [News](/hilfe/neuigkeiten).

## Updating from HUBIplan (self-update)

Platform › Version shows which version is running and whether a newer release is available. If the operator has turned on self-update (`HUBIPLAN_SELBSTUPDATE=1`, see `docs/betrieb.md`), you can install the new release there with “Update to …”. This needs two-factor sign-in, and you enter your password again.

HUBIplan only leaves an order. A service on the server first backs up the database, checks the release signature and that it is newer than the running version, and then installs it. HUBIplan is unavailable for a few minutes meanwhile; the page checks back on its own and then shows the result. If anything fails, the previous version keeps running. Every order is recorded in the change log, and the operator receives a security email.

## Virus scanning

If no virus scanning is set up on the server, or it is switched off for sharing, a notice appears there: circular attachments and public documents then go out unscanned. With virus scanning (ClamAV) set up, HUBIplan shares such files only after scanning them.

If the virus scanner is briefly unreachable, HUBIplan still accepts uploaded documents, attachments and receipts, but locks them until the scanner has checked them (quarantine). Platform › Version shows how many files are waiting and whether malware was found in any of them; such files stay locked for good.

## Addresses per unit

In the **Addresses per unit** section of the platform settings you assign further addresses to a unit, for example `mitglieder.sv-musterstadt.example` to Schützenverein Musterstadt. Anyone opening HUBIplan via that address sees the unit's name, colours, coat of arms and icon on the sign-in page; after signing in, the unit is preselected. Unknown addresses and the main address show the instance. Links in the unit's emails (invitation, sign-in link, events, volunteer shifts, tasks, membership card, photo link, circulars) lead to its address, otherwise to that of the next higher unit with its own address; “Forgot password” sends the link for the address on which it was requested.

The unit uploads its own icon under Settings › Appearance; without one, HUBIplan uses its coat of arms. Sign-in applies per address. The address must point to the server via DNS. If the server has `HUBIPLAN_ADRESSEN_AUS_LISTE=1` set, it accepts listed addresses without further configuration and obtains the certificate on first access; otherwise the operator must allow them (`DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, certificate). Nextcloud, the app connection and federation stay on the main address.

## Feedback on the help

Below every guide and page help you find “Did this help?”. The **Help** tab shows the answers per help text, most “No” first, with the sentence about what was missing. Only the help text, language, version, answer, sentence and day are stored, no person and no club. If a sentence does name someone, take it out with **Remove**; the answer still counts.

Below that, **Searches without results** lists what people searched for in the help without finding anything, with a counter. Entries with digits or email addresses are not stored.
en.seiten/rundschreiben-glueckwuensche.md:
---
key: page.circulars_greetings
titel: Circulars › Greetings
modul: circulars
rechte: [circulars.send]
routen: [/rundschreiben/glueckwuensche]
stichworte: [birthday, anniversary, congratulations, birthday greeting, greeting]
---

HUBIplan congratulates your members on their birthday and club anniversary, by app or email, and by letter for members without an email address. Under **Settings** you choose which birthdays to congratulate on, whether to include anniversaries, and write the texts. Then **Save**.

## How it works

A few days in advance (seven by default) a draft is created for each day. Under **Upcoming greetings** you see who receives it and how. Print letters there in good time using the print button (PDF). On the day the greeting is sent automatically from the hour you set, or with **only after approval by the board** only when you click **Send now**. **Skip** drops a day; **Schedule again** brings it back. Sent greetings are listed under **History (30 days)** with their delivery log; they do not appear in the list of circulars.

## Texts and placeholders

The placeholders {Alter} and {Jubiläumsjahre} insert the age on the birthday and the years in the club, {Anrede Du} the greeting with the first name. **Use default text** restores the supplied text.

## Objection

Members can object to greetings in the members' area under **Messages**. If someone tells the board, untick **Wants birthday and anniversary greetings** in the member file under **Communication & delivery**. Anyone who has objected is shown in the preview with “does not want greetings” and receives nothing.
en.seiten/rundschreiben.md:
---
key: page.circulars
titel: Circulars
modul: circulars
routen: [/rundschreiben, /rundschreiben/brief, /rundschreiben/empfangen]
stichworte: [mailing, letter, newsletter, distribution list, invitation]
---

Circulars go by email, letter or to the app to members, boards or holders of certain roles. You choose the type: everyone receives official notices such as invitations, while members can unsubscribe from “information”. Sent circulars remain available to read.

## Organisations and households

For organisations as members, the circular goes to every contact person marked “receives circulars”. Without such an address it goes to the organisation's email address or as a letter marked “attn.” of the primary contact. The placeholder {Organisation} inserts the organisation's name; the salutation addresses the contact person.

If members belong to a household at the same address, they get one joint letter, and emails to the same address become one email. The preview shows the others as “im gemeinsamen Schreiben an den Haushalt” (in the joint letter to the household). Under **Recipient** you switch this off with **Combine letters per household**. The placeholder {Haushalt} inserts the household name. You create households under [Members › Households and companies](/mitglieder/haushalte).

## Letter

For a single letter, Circulars › Letter creates a Word template with the club letterhead and your sender details. The board designs the letterhead under Settings › Letterhead; you store your signature under My account.

## Mailing lists

A mailing list turns a mail sent to a club address into a circular. Anyone may write to an open mailing list. So that outsiders cannot reach many members unchecked, their mails go out directly only up to an adjustable number of recipients (50 by default) and up to a number per day. Anything beyond that is kept as a draft. Those allowed to write to the list are notified and release or delete the mail.

## Events from your email program

If someone with the events permission invites a mailing list to an event in their email program, for example `vorstand@…` in Outlook, Thunderbird, the Nextcloud calendar or on a phone, HUBIplan creates an event from it. As with circulars, a confirmation link comes first; only **Take over and inform** creates the event and sends the list's recipients an invitation with time, place and video link. The sender's calendar then shows the list as “accepted”.

For lists to role holders the event is “board only”, otherwise visible to members, never public. Replies exist only for member events. A video link in the invitation (Talk, Teams, Zoom, Jitsi) is taken over; if there is none and **Create a video room if the invitation has no video link** is on, HUBIplan creates a new room in Nextcloud Talk. Changes and cancellations from the email program arrive the same way. General meetings with a formal notice are still created in HUBIplan.

## Lists

Name lists use a fixed alphabetical order: accented letters are placed with their base letter. Identical names keep their relative order when paging through the list.

## Circular for an event

You create a circular about an event in the open event with **Write a circular about it** in the button bar; it is then listed there under **For this event**. It goes to those invited to the event, optionally only to those with a certain reply. For an event with registrations, an information letter goes to the registrants, including guests (see Events).

## Received

If the club belongs to an umbrella association, the **Received** tab shows its circulars to the boards. Without an umbrella association this tab does not exist.

Received circulars and their attachments are also available in the member area under **Circulars**. The Android app calls this shared inbox “Messages”. Changes to information emails are confirmed and keyboard focus is kept while saving. Further changes are blocked during the request; official notices are unaffected.
en.seiten/start.md:
---
key: page.start
titel: Home page
routen: [/]
stichworte:
  [
    quick search,
    area bar,
    area menu,
    new,
    search,
    tasks,
    quick actions,
    notices,
    anniversaries,
    birthdays,
    accept,
    customise,
    layout,
    drag,
  ]
---

The home page is your workplace in the selected unit. Without a layout of your own it has the same order for every role: **To do**, **Quick actions**, **Upcoming events**, **Anniversaries**, **Birthdays** and **Notices**. What you see depends on your rights; anything you may not do is simply left out. At the top right you switch units if you work in more than one.

## Areas and menu

On the left, the area bar in your club's colour shows up to seven areas: **Home**, **Members**, **Planning**, **Communication**, **Club life**, **Finances** and **Club**. You only see the areas in which you have rights. A click opens the area; next to it, the light area menu shows only the pages of that area, for example Events, Meetings, Volunteer duties and Tasks under Planning. **Menu** at the bottom of the area bar collapses the area menu when a list needs more room, and opens it again; **Help** is below it. On a phone, “More” opens the whole menu, grouped by area.

**New** in the header creates something from any page, depending on your rights for example an event, a member, a booking or a circular. These are the same actions as the quick actions on the home page.

## Help and quick search

At the top, **Help on this page** opens help for the current page; on narrow screens only the “?” sign is shown. **Help** at the bottom of the area bar opens the overview of all guides. **My account** contains your email address, personal settings and **Sign out**.

**Quick search** at the top centre (or Ctrl+K, on a Mac ⌘K) jumps straight to a page: type a few letters, such as “remind” for Finance › Reminders, choose with the arrow keys and open with Enter. If you may see the club's members, you also find members there by name or membership number and land in the member record. Only what you can reach in the menu is found. On a phone, quick search is at the top of the menu (“More”).

The bar at the bottom of a phone shows Start and two areas that suit your role, such as Finance for the treasurer or Meetings for the secretary; everything else is under “More”. Events from the calendar are found there by their title too, such as “meeting” for the general meeting; upcoming ones come first. With ↶ and ↷ at the top you undo or redo your latest changes; the arrow ▾ next to them shows your steps in this browser window. Older changes are listed under Settings › Log.

Buttons have their own opaque background, including subtle actions, disabled buttons and file pickers. Selected views also use a distinct fill. Very light club colours are darkened for action buttons to keep them recognisable; the club logo and the remaining brand colour are preserved.

## To do

The **To do** tile comes first and collects tasks, approvals, requests, overdue invoices, open booking requests, held contact form messages, your own circular drafts untouched for a week, meeting invitations from two weeks before the invitation deadline, received motions and open minutes, open helper places in the next two weeks, queries and close entry deadlines, received invoices to review, invoice drafts, due reminders and direct debits, expired account invitations, bookings without a receipt in the current financial year, bank accounts whose statement for the previous month is still missing from the 5th, and missing required items of the [setup](/einstellungen/einrichtung); each entry only appears with the matching permission.

Finance › Overview shows the same entries where they concern finance. The count is shown beside its heading. **New task** at the bottom of the tile opens the task dialog. **All tasks** beside it opens the overview. Each row separates its type, title and details; tasks that are due also show a due-date notice. Use the checkbox to complete a task if you have permission. Its title opens the details.

## Quick actions

**Quick actions** are buttons for what you do most often; the first one is highlighted. Without a selection of your own, HUBIplan suggests at most four actions for your role: the treasurer gets **Record a booking**, **Import bank statement**, **Issue receipt** and **Prepare reminders**, the board **New event**, **Admit member** and **Write a circular**, the secretary **Create a meeting** and **Write minutes**. The treasurer's actions are only suggested if you hold a treasurer role (a role with finance rights that may not assign roles); if you have several roles, they come first.

Under **Customise** you choose up to six actions yourself from everything your rights allow, grouped by area: finance (such as **Record income**, **Write invoice**, **Prepare fee run**), events and planning (**Create task**, **Create helper shift**, **Enter booking**), members, club (**Add to chronicle**, **Create competition**, **Enter results**, **Upload sheet music**) and writing and filing (**File a document**, **Edit website**, **Write a letter**). You set the order by grabbing an action anywhere and dragging it; with the keyboard, use the handle and the arrow keys.

The selection applies to each unit and sub-unit separately; **Restore suggestion** goes back to the suggestion. In the workspace of a sub-unit you can choose **Event for the unit**, **View members**, **Letterhead** and, if allowed, **Create task**. **Hide quick actions completely** removes the whole block; you can turn it back on under My account › Profile › Home.

## Events, anniversaries and notices

In **Upcoming events**, **New event** opens the event dialog when you have permission to create events, and **Calendar** opens the overview.

The **Anniversaries** card shows the anniversaries of the current year, from October also those of the next year, each under its own heading such as “Anniversaries 2026”. Anniversaries count for a calendar year; a date is only shown if the club counts to the day or month. **All anniversaries** leads to the full list. The **Birthdays** card shows the birthdays in the next 30 days. Names lead to the member record.

The **Notices** card collects what is not urgent: missing details in the legal notice and letter template notices (with **Later**). The number next to the heading is the number of these notices. Without a notice there is no card.

## Customise the home page

**Customise home page** at the top right lets you put the home page together the way you like. Each block then gets a dashed frame and a bar with **Show**, **Width** and **Height to fit content**. Grab a block anywhere and drag it to its new place; with the keyboard, use the handle and the arrow keys. Drag the corner at the bottom right to change width and height; with the keyboard, the left and right arrow keys there change the width and up and down the height.

The home page uses a grid of twelve columns and fine rows: a block moves up into the next gap that is wide enough, including below a shorter block next to it. You choose the width as ¼, ⅓, ½, ⅔, ¾ or full, and at the corner also in twelfths. If a block has a fixed height, its content scrolls inside the card; **Height to fit content** makes it as tall as needed again. Hidden blocks stay faintly visible while customising so you can switch them back on.

A block without content, such as birthdays when there are none in the next 30 days, does not appear on the home page. Every change is saved straight away; **Done** ends customising. The layout is yours alone and kept separately for each unit and sub-unit; **Restore default** returns to the order above, and under My account › Profile › Home page you can do this for all areas at once. On narrow screens all blocks are stacked; on a phone the page scrolls over the content, and you drag by the bar with the name.

![Board home page with To do, quick actions, anniversaries and notices](bild:startseite-vorstand)

## As a member

As a member the next event is at the very top, on a phone too. If a response is possible, you accept or decline right there with **Accept** or **Decline**; the following events come below. Under **My area** at most four tiles are shown, **Show ID card** first; **Everything in My area** leads to the rest.

![Member home page with the next event at the top](bild:startseite-mitglied)

## Two-factor notice

If two-factor sign-in is required for your permissions, every page shows the same short notice with **Set up now**; **Learn more** shows which permissions are affected. If the connection drops, the “No connection” band appears straight away. Automatically saved changes are sent as soon as the connection is back; after about ten seconds at the latest the form shows that nothing has been saved yet.
en.seiten/termine-abo.md:
---
key: page.events_feed
titel: Events › Calendar subscription
modul: events
rechte: []
routen: [/termine/abo]
stichworte: [Calendar subscription, subscribe, iCal, phone calendar]
---

Create a personal calendar-subscription link for your own calendar app. Keep it private. Creating a new link invalidates the previous link. A status confirms when your link is ready.

With a board role you also see the **Board subscription** below: a separate link with only the “board only” events of your unit. This lets you show or hide the board calendar in your calendar app on its own. The link only works while you hold a board office; when it ends, the link no longer returns events. Do not pass it on, not even into a shared calendar.

![Create a personal calendar subscription](bild:kalender-abo)
en.seiten/termine-einrichtung.md:
---
key: page.events_setup
titel: Events › Setup
modul: events
rechte: [events.manage]
routen:
  [
    /termine/einrichtung,
    /termine/einrichtung/kategorien,
    /termine/einrichtung/weitergabe,
    /termine/einrichtung/link,
  ]
stichworte: [Category, colour, sharing, public link, federation, unit]
---

Here you set how the unit's calendar works. The items are tabs next to each other.

## Categories

Categories organise events, such as “Training”, “Festival” or “Meeting”. Each category has a colour and an abbreviation by which you recognise it in the calendar. A category that still has events cannot be deleted. Deleting happens without a confirmation; “Undo” in the top bar brings the category back.

## External calendars

Shows events from other calendars in your own, for example those of a neighbouring club. There is a separate page help for this.

## Sharing

For each category you choose whether its events also appear elsewhere: **Pass on upwards (in the calendar of the higher unit)** or **Pass on downwards (to the sub-units and their members)**. This way the summer party also appears in every sub-unit's calendar, but the board meeting does not.

## Public link

With **Public events retrievable via a link** there is an address through which other programs read your public events, for example another website. **Create new link** invalidates the old one.
en.seiten/termine.md:
---
key: page.events
titel: Events
modul: events
routen: [/termine]
stichworte: [calendar, event, accept, decline, subscription]
---

The calendar shows the unit's events. With the right to do so, you create events, including recurring ones, and invite members who accept or decline. With the calendar subscription the events appear in your own calendar on phone or PC. Under Events › Setup you manage categories, external calendars, sharing with other units and the website link. Under “External calendars” the calendar imports other calendars’ events every hour, e.g. the federation’s from Vereinsplaner.

## Reading the calendar

Each entry names its unit and, where applicable, its external calendar, so you can distinguish events with the same title before opening them. In the month view, a multi-day event starts with its start time; subsequent days show “Continued”, and the last day shows, for example, “Continued until 01:05”. An end exactly at midnight is shown on the preceding day as 24:00, without an extra entry on the new day. All-day events remain labelled as such. The list and accessible names include the complete date and time range; the list is the default view on small screens.

You can tell an event’s category not only by its colour: every event has a light background and a stripe on the left in its category colour, and the category name appears below the title. On small screens the month view shows a short code instead of the name (e.g. “Mee” for Meeting). The legend above the month explains the colours and codes of all categories in that month. Screen readers announce the category too.

![Calendar with units and continuation past midnight](bild:kalender-kontext)

## The open event

An open event is laid out like this: at the top are when, where and the calendar, below them a bar with the buttons **Edit**, **Write a circular about it**, **Reminder to everyone without a reply** and **Add to my calendar** (.ics). The **Responses** card shows the number of acceptances, refusals and open replies, Excel and PDF for the participant list and, to expand, everyone who has not replied yet.

The **For this event** card shows one row for each thing that belongs to the event: circulars, meeting, volunteer duty roster, booked rooms and equipment, tasks, the music performance, equipment, the statement in the event finances and the attachments. The area is on the left, its state in the middle and the buttons on the right, for example **Open**, **Show** or + **Create**. **Delete** stands on its own at the very bottom. You only see areas whose module is switched on and for which you have the right. Events, meetings, volunteer duties and tasks are grouped together in the sidebar under “Planning”.

## Attachments

In the **Attachments** row you attach files: + **Add file** uploads a file (PDF, JPEG or PNG, at most 15 MB), and **From the document store** picks a document from your unit's document store. A linked document always shows its newest version; if you upload a new version in the document store, it applies to the event right away. Everyone who may see the event also sees its attachments, in the member area and in the app, even if the folder in the document store has narrower visibility; the dialog points this out before linking.

To link, you need the right to edit the event and to see the document store. If the document is in the trash, it disappears from the event and comes back when restored. **remove** only removes the link; the document stays in the document store. For recurring events, the attachments apply to all occurrences. For public events, each attachment has **show on the website**: only ticked attachments appear on the website in the event window; all others stay internal. If the event later becomes internal, they disappear there again.

## Video room

If your unit has switched on **Video room for events** under Settings › Nextcloud, **Create video room** creates a Talk conversation. Link and password then appear in the **Video room** row, in the member area, in the apps and in the invitation and reminder; **Copy link** takes both. **Remove video room** deletes the room at once, otherwise it goes by itself a few days after the event.

## Circular for the event

**Write a circular about it** in the button bar creates a draft to those invited. It contains title, time, place, description and the reply deadline, and the event's PDF attachments go along as attachments. In the circular you can pick only those invited with **no reply yet**, **accepted** or **declined**, for example for a reminder. All circulars for the event are then listed in the **Circulars** row. **Reminder to everyone without a reply** creates such a draft right away to everyone who has not replied yet (and, if “Maybe” is allowed, to those as well). You see the replies in the event's participant list.

## Create and edit an event

The event dialog first asks for title, time and place, then category and **Who sees the event?**. Rarely used options are folded under **More settings**: **Pass on upwards**, **Pass on downwards** and **Hide end time on the website**. If one of them is set, the section is open. The header and the save bar stay in place while you scroll in the dialog.

When editing, the dialog saves every change straight away: **Done** at the bottom takes you back to the event view, **Close** at the top closes the dialog. In the **Place** field, typing, a click or the down arrow opens the list of saved places; choose with the arrow keys and Enter, Esc closes only the list. “public” means visible on the website and without signing in. Inside HUBIplan the members of the level that creates the event see it; other units only see it if it is passed on upwards or downwards.

“board only” events are seen by members with a board role in the unit: in the administration, under **My events** and in the app. They are not included in the personal calendar subscription; for them there is the separate **Board subscription** under Events › Calendar subscription.

Under **Directions** you enter notes such as parking or the entrance. Without further details the links **Route in OpenStreetMap** and **Route in Google Maps** lead to the address. If the address is not enough (meadow, hut in the woods), enter **Latitude** and **Longitude** or paste a link from OpenStreetMap or Google Maps under **Take point from map link**. Directions and route links appear in the event, in the emails, on the reply page and in the calendar subscription; no map is embedded. If you pick a saved place, the event copies its address, directions and point.

When creating or editing an event, enable **Hide end time on the website** to show only the start time publicly. The internal calendar and calendar subscription keep the end time. For recurring events, the setting applies to all occurrences.

## Accepting and declining

After successfully accepting, declining or withdrawing your response, a confirmation is provided as a status message for screen readers. Focus stays at the action when accepting or declining; after withdrawal it moves to **Accept**. An error produces no success confirmation; you can retry your response.

For replies to an event you can switch on **Allow “Maybe” as an answer**. “Maybe” does not count against the maximum number, but the reminder before the event also goes to these members. **Allow a comment** is on by default; with **Own question for the comment (optional)** (e.g. “Meal preference?”) it appears above the field instead of “Comment”. The participant list and the export show “Maybe” and the comments.

Every email about the event (invitation, reminder, circular about the event) contains a personal link “Accept or decline (without login)” for each member. It opens a page with time, place, description and attachments; there the member chooses “I am coming”, “Maybe” or “I am not coming” and saves. Just opening the link saves nothing. The same link lets them change the answer until the deadline, as do the member area and the app. The invitation carries the event's attachments directly as email attachments (up to 5 files, 10 MB each); larger ones are on the page behind the link.

The invitation also carries a calendar entry: Outlook, Thunderbird and phones then show “Accept”, “Tentative” and “Decline”. The answer arrives as a reply (“entered by: email program”). Members with their own calendar subscription get no calendar entry in the mail, so the event does not appear twice in their calendar.

## Binding registration with participation fee

With the Registrations module (under Settings › Modules, needs events and invoices) an event gets binding registration instead of accepting and declining. An event has one or the other. In the open event you set it up with **Set up binding registration**: registration opens (optional), registration deadline (until then members can also cancel themselves), places, people per registration, whether members may register guests too, payment term, category in the accounts and terms of participation.

Every rate (e.g. members, guests, children aged 6 to 13) has one price or several price tiers that apply one after another, such as “early bird” until a date or for the first 50 people; the last tier applies until the registration deadline. Whoever has registered keeps their price. Prices are set by whoever may edit invoices; without that permission only free rates are possible. On first saving, an event is created under Finance to which the income is assigned.

Members register for the event in the members' area, if they like together with their family and with guests. For age-based rates HUBIplan asks for the date of birth. After **Register with obligation to pay** a registration confirmation arrives by email with the invoice as a PDF and the event for their own calendar. When the payment arrives (also via the bank statement), a payment confirmation follows. Anyone who cancels or is cancelled receives a confirmation with a cancellation invoice; the club refunds anything already paid.

The board sees all registrations with their payment status, uses **Add registration** to record registrations by phone or on paper (for members or guests with an address) and downloads the **List of participants (Excel)**. Guest data is anonymised six months after the event. An event with registrations cannot be deleted, only cancelled.

## Waiting list and cancellation fees

Under **Waiting list and cancellation** in the registration settings there are further rules. With **Waiting list when all places are taken**, new registrations go on the waiting list once the event is full (in the members' area the button then reads **Join the waiting list**). When a place becomes free, the next registration that fits moves up automatically, becomes binding and receives the invoice by email; it can then cancel free of charge for 48 hours.

The waiting list ends when the event starts, and anyone still waiting is told. Cancellation fees follow tiers such as “less than 14 days before: 50 %”, optionally with a fixed handling fee. Before cancelling, HUBIplan shows the fee; it comes as a separate invoice, and anything already paid is offset against it where it fits. If someone moves up from the waiting list instead, there is no fee; the board can waive it in individual cases with a reason (**Waive cancellation fee**).

With several people, individual people can be cancelled too; the invoice is then cancelled and reissued for the rest. With **Substitute**, someone else takes the place at the same rate and price, and the invoice stays. If the event is cancelled, HUBIplan cancels all registrations and the waiting list without a fee and writes to everyone. Optionally, unpaid registrations expire a few days before the start; the place then goes to the waiting list.

## Schedule and information letters

The “Schedule or programme” field says what happens when. The programme appears in the event and is included in circulars about the event. For an event with registrations the button in the button bar reads **Information letter to registrants**: the circular then goes to the people who registered, including guests without a membership, optionally only to binding registrations, the waiting list, paid or unpaid ones. HUBIplan fills placeholders such as registration number, people and amount outstanding for each registration. With **Send the letter to later registrations too**, anyone who registers later or moves up from the waiting list also receives the information letters already sent.

## Extras and questions

Under **Extras and questions** in the registration settings you can offer extras such as a coach trip or a menu, per person or per registration, with a surcharge and a place limit. They appear as a separate item on the invoice and as a column in the list of participants; the count (say, 32 schnitzels) is shown with the extra. Additional questions without a price (text, yes/no or a choice) apply per person or per registration and can be required.

You may only ask about allergies and intolerances if there is food (**with catering** or an extra of the type food). The answer is voluntary and needs consent; only the administration sees it, it appears only in the **List with allergies (Excel)** and is deleted 14 days after the event. If the catering is removed, information already collected is deleted. With **Minors can take part** the registration always asks for the date of birth; for participants under 18, the name, phone number and email of a parent or guardian are required, and a second person can be added.

## Public registration for non-members

For events with the visibility “public”, **Public registration** › **Non-members can register too (form with link)** lets people without a membership register as well. After saving, the link to the form appears with the registrations, with **Copy link** for passing it on, for example on the website, in an invitation or on a poster. The form shows the event, the programme, the rates for guests, free places, the cancellation rule and the terms of participation.

Whoever submits it first receives an email with a confirmation link that is valid for 24 hours; only then is the registration binding, the place taken and the invoice on its way. HUBIplan deletes unconfirmed registrations after 24 hours. The confirmation contains a link with which the person can view their registration and cancel according to the event's rules. A puzzle solved in the background and a limit per hour keep spam out. As with guests, the details are anonymised six months after the event.

## Registration on the club website

On the club website such an event shows, in the event window, the state of registration, the current prices with the deadline of the price tier, places left and the “Register now” button. The event gets a page of its own under “For this event” › **Website** › **Create**: this creates an event page as a draft under Website › Texts.

Date, place, directions, programme, prices, cancellation rule, terms of participation and documents come from the event; you maintain the text and further sections there like on any text page. With **Publish** the page appears at `/veranstaltung/<address>/` with a menu item that you can move under Website › Menu and pages, for example below “Events”. On the day after the end the menu item disappears by itself; the page stays as a look back unless you tick **Remove from the website after the event has ended** there.

## Tickets and admission

Every binding registration has **Tickets** as a PDF, one ticket per person with a QR code. The code contains no names, only a verified identifier. For free events the tickets come with the registration confirmation, otherwise with the payment confirmation; they are also in the members' area, behind the “view registration” link and, for the administration, with each registration under **Tickets**.

Anyone who was registered by someone else sees only their own line and their own ticket in the members' area and the app (parents also those of their children); the whole registration with the invoice is visible to whoever made it. On site, **Admission** opens the list of everyone registered with their payment status. With a hand scanner you scan the ticket into the **Ticket code** field; on a phone, tablet or laptop, **Scan with the camera** works too.

Without a ticket, tick the person off in the list with **Admit**. HUBIplan tells you if someone has already been admitted, the ticket belongs to another event, the person has cancelled or has not paid yet. **Undo** reverses an admission. Whoever may edit invoices sees **Take cash** for unpaid registrations: it opens the invoice, where you book the cash payment, with a signed receipt if you like (box office). In the HUBIplan app, admission is under Administration › Events with a camera scanner and box office; the list stays readable without a network.

The admission list reloads every 10 seconds, so you see live who has been scanned, through which scan link and when extras such as meals were redeemed.

## Scan links and cash desk on site

For scanning staff without an account, create one or more links under **Scan links for staff**, each with a **Label** (e.g. “North entrance”) and a **Station**: **Admission** ticks the person off, an extra (e.g. lunch) is redeemed. Pass the link on with **Copy link** or let someone scan the QR code. On the phone or tablet there is then only the ticket scanner: it shows whether the ticket is valid, the name and date of birth to compare with an ID, the tariff, booked extras with the time they were redeemed and whether the ticket has already been scanned. Staff do not see a participant list.

The link is valid until the day after the event at the latest; **Block** ends it at once.

A scan link also expires when the person who created it loses their role or account; create a new link in that case. The camera works in all common browsers, including Safari on the iPhone; alternatively, enter the code with a hand scanner or by hand. With **Allow name search**, staff can book in registered people without a ticket: they search by name from three letters on, see only the matches with their date of birth and book them in after checking their ID.

Cashiers also work via a link: whoever may edit invoices chooses a cash box under **Accept cash payment** when creating the link and enters the **Cashier**. When scanning or after a name search, staff then see the open amount and book the cash payment onto the invoice with one tap, into the chosen cash box. Free registrations have nothing open. In the list of scan links, each cash link shows the number of payments and the total as its cash closing, to compare with the cash.

## Name badges, labels and equipment

For on site and afterwards: **Name badges and labels** prints name badges in business card format (85 × 54 mm, ten per A4 page) or labels (70 × 37 mm, 24 per sheet, or 105 × 74 mm, eight per sheet) from the registration list. Under **Details** you choose what goes on them: event, name, club, tariff, extras, registration number, ticket QR code and answers to additional questions; to print a company name, ask for it as an additional question per person. Under **Equipment** you create what is handed out on site, such as a name badge, bag or loan device, optionally **to be returned**.

The list shows for each person what was handed out and returned when, and reloads every 10 seconds; **Hand out**, **Take back** and **Undo** tick things off by hand. Staff can do the same through a scan link with the station “Hand-out” or “Return”. **Certificates of attendance (PDF)** creates one page per person on your letterhead. Participants are those checked in at the entrance; if you did not use check-in, everyone registered counts. With the Qualifications module switched on, **Record qualification** adds the chosen record to all participating members after a course, dated the last day of the event and with the usual validity. Guests without membership are skipped and duplicates avoided.

## Group registration with the umbrella association

Group registration with the umbrella association: When an umbrella association sets up registration, it can switch on under **Group registration** that clubs register their members as a group. The clubs see the event in their calendar; whoever in the club may edit registrations and see members finds **Club group registration** there, picks members and tariff and registers them (binding).

The invoice goes to the club, not to the individual members. The club only sees its own registrations and can cancel people until the registration deadline. The club needs the Registrations module for this. Under Entries, **Group registrations with the umbrella association** lists all upcoming events of the umbrella association with group registration and how many members the club has registered for each.
en.seiten/training.md:
---
key: page.training
titel: Training
modul: training
rechte: [training.view, training.edit]
routen: [/training]
stichworte: [
    training,
    practice evening,
    attendance,
    attendance list,
    check-in,
    QR code,
    coach,
    coach
    expenses,
    grant,
    shooting log,
    shooting record,
    firearms licence,
    WaffG,
  ]
---

Under **Training** you record who attended practice evenings and training sessions. A list belongs
to the club or to a sub-unit such as the youth section or a division; the attendance list then
only shows that sub-unit's members.

## Creating a session

**New training session** creates a practice evening or training session with date, time, place and leader.
If a matching event is in the calendar, **Take over from the calendar** copies its details with
one click. HUBIplan calculates the hours from start and end, for example for coach expenses.

## Recording attendance

In a session you tick off who is there. It is quicker with **Open check-in**: the page then shows
a QR code that members scan with the HUBIplan app or their phone camera. The code changes every 30
seconds, so a photo of it is no use to anyone who is not there. Check-in works on the day of the
session and on the day before or after. **Show code full screen** fills the screen, for example for a
TV in the clubhouse.

## Evaluation

**Evaluation** counts who attended how often in a period and shows the total hours. **Download as Excel** gives the attendance per member and the list of sessions, for example for grant
applications.

## Shooting log and shooting record

If the Shooting module is also switched on, there is the **Shooting log**. For the firearms
licence requirement (section 14 of the German Weapons Act, WaffG), sport shooters must prove that
they shoot regularly:

- Acquisition (para. 3): member for twelve months and, in the last twelve months, shot in
  every month or 18 times in total.
- Possession (para. 4): in the last 24 months once per quarter or six times in each
  twelve-month period, separately for handguns and long guns. After ten years, membership is
  enough.

Entries come about in three ways: a session marked as a shooting date records everyone
present with discipline and firearm. The board adds entries to a member's shooting log by hand.
Members report sessions outside training in the member area; the board confirms or rejects them
under **Reported shooting dates**.

Only confirmed sessions with firearms that need a licence count; air guns do not count. At most
one session per discipline counts per day. HUBIplan also points out breaks of more than four
months and more sessions in other clubs than in your own, as for example the BSSB guideline
expects.

**Create PDF** produces the confirmation of shooting dates for the last 24 months with the
status under section 14 WaffG. The board member authorised to represent the club signs and stamps
it; it is the attachment to the application to the association. The association's application
form is still needed. The association decides what it accepts.

## Rights and retention

Anyone with edit rights for “Training and attendance” can record attendance; roles that edit
events have it from the start. The module can be switched on and off under Settings › Modules.
HUBIplan deletes attendance and shooting log entries after ten years, and immediately when the
member's data is deleted.
en.seiten/umfragen.md:
---
key: page.surveys
titel: Surveys and polls
modul: surveys
rechte: [surveys.view, surveys.edit]
routen: [/umfragen]
stichworte: [Survey, Poll, Date finder, Find a date, Meal choice, anonymous, Doodle]
---

Under **Surveys** you quickly ask members something: find a date, ask for meal choices for the
festive dinner, who is taking the bus, or get an opinion poll. Surveys are polls, not
resolutions; formal votes belong in meetings.

## Creating

New survey: **New survey** offers templates: **Find a date**, **Meal choice**,
**Who is coming along?**, **Opinion poll (yes/no/abstain)** and **Free survey**. A survey has up
to 10 questions. Question types are single and multiple choice, yes / no / abstain, date finder
(yes, no and optionally maybe per option), quantities (such as 2× schnitzel, 1× vegetarian) and
free text up to 500 characters. Answers can have a number of places; once it is reached, nobody
can choose that answer any more.

Who is asked: all members of the club or subunit, limited by subunits, membership types or the
board only, or selected people. A survey for an event asks everyone invited or only those who
accepted. For a meal choice at an event, guests count too: anyone coming with one guest chooses
up to two meals. If someone declines the event, their answer is removed from the survey.
**How many are asked?** shows the number before starting.

## Names and result

Names and result: **open** (everyone asked sees names), **only the administrators see names** or
**anonymous**. Anonymous means nobody sees who answered what, not even the administrators.
HUBIplan only stores that someone took part, separately from the answer. Anonymous answers cannot
be changed, and the result only appears from five answers on and only after the end, also for
the administrators. After starting, names and result can only become stricter, never more open.
People asked see the result after answering, always, only after closing or not at all
(administrators only); for anonymous surveys only “only after the end” or “administrators only”.

## Start, evaluate, keep

Start and close: **Start** notifies everyone asked, by app or by email with a personal link they
can use to answer without signing in. Questions and audience can no longer be changed afterwards;
**Change closing time** still works. Optionally HUBIplan reminds everyone who has not answered a
few days before closing. The survey closes by itself at the end; **Close now** closes it at once.

Results: The survey shows bars per answer, with names for open surveys, and who has not answered
yet. For a date finder, the best date is highlighted; the button “Create event on …” turns it
into an event with RSVPs. Everyone who said “yes” accepts it there with one tap. **PDF** and
**Excel** contain the result, for example as an order list for the kitchen.
**Enter for a member** records an answer given by phone or on paper (not for anonymous surveys).

Retention: HUBIplan deletes answers with names the set number of months after closing (default
12). The totals remain. **Copy** creates the survey again for next year.

Subunits: If a subunit role has the right to do so, it asks its own members.

key: page.dept_expenses
