If the club has set your department to confirm expense claims first, you see the claims for your department here. The leaders check that the expense was for you and choose **Confirm** or **Send a query**. Then the treasurer reviews, approves and pays. Your own claim is confirmed by someone else. To confirm, the role needs the right "Review expense claims" in the department.
en.seiten/untereinheiten.md:
---
key: page.units
titel: Sub-units
routen: [/untereinheiten]
stichworte: [platoon, department, sub-unit, manager]
---

This lists the sub-units of your unit, which can be nested freely. A club without sub-units hides this menu item under Settings › Names and terms. Each sub-unit can have its own roles, its own cash book, events and a website. With “Assign head” a person from the sub-unit gets an account with all permissions for their area.

For each sub-unit you upload a coat of arms or logo and, if you like, a second one for dark mode. Without a dark one, the normal one is used in the dark.

## In detail

Unit settings and roles have separate rights. Settings “read” shows administrative data; role “read” shows roles. Without settings read access, a limited sub-unit selection remains available for this purpose. Changing and assigning roles requires role “edit”; “Assign head” additionally requires settings edit access.

“Who has which role?” lists the current holders per role. With **Assign** you give a role to a member, without an account and without email; the predecessor’s term can end in the same step. Earlier terms are under Members › Offices with the Unit filter.

With its own workspace you choose under “Modules for this unit” which of the club’s modules the sub-unit also uses there, such as tax & charitable status for its own cash book or social media for its own website. By default: all.
en.seiten/versammlungen.md:
---
key: page.meetings
titel: Meetings
modul: meetings
rechte: [meetings.view, meetings.edit]
routen: [/versammlungen]
stichworte: [AGM, General meeting, Board meeting, Agenda, Item, Notice period, Minutes]
---

Under **Meetings** you prepare general meetings, board meetings and meetings of a unit. The
overview shows upcoming and past meetings with their status.

## New meeting

Choose **New meeting**, then the type, start, end and place. HUBIplan creates an
event in the calendar for it. All members see general meetings in the calendar; only the board
sees board meetings. If **Copy the agenda of the last meeting of this type** is ticked, HUBIplan
copies its items; for the first meeting of a type it suggests a typical agenda.
**Event in the calendar** in the meeting leads to its event; there the block “For this event”
shows duty rosters and bookings for the meeting.

## Agenda

Each agenda item has a title, a type (report, resolution, election or other) and an
explanation. Use the arrows to change the order; the numbers follow from it. The agenda saves
itself shortly after each change, as soon as every item has a title. Removing a saved item asks first.
The meeting details (location, chair, minute taker, note …) also save themselves; the top of the box shows whether everything is saved.

## Sub-items

**Add sub-item** gives an item sub-items, for example 8.1 and 8.2 under “Elections”. To put an existing item under another one, drag it onto that item or pick the item under **Belongs to**; “Own item (top level)” makes it an item of its own again. You can drag by the handle or any empty spot of the item (on a phone only by the handle): dropped between two items it changes the order; dropped onto an item it becomes a sub-item of that item.

An item always takes its sub-items along. The arrow keys work on the handle too: ↑ and ↓ move, → makes the item a sub-item of the item above, ← makes it an item of its own again. There is one level of sub-items. The numbers appear the same way in the invitation, the minutes, the member area and online voting.

## Notice period

Below the heading you see the date by which the invitation has to go out. Once
that day has passed, HUBIplan points it out. Set the notice period for each type under **Types and notice periods**, in line with your statutes.

## Cancelling and deleting

**Cancel** keeps the event in the calendar and shows it as cancelled.
You can only delete a meeting before invitations have gone out. The event of a meeting cannot
be deleted in the calendar, only here.

## Types and notice periods

HUBIplan starts with the usual types, such as the annual general
meeting and the board meeting. You can rename them, add more or switch them off. For each type
you set the notice period, how invitations are sent, the quorum and who will see the minutes. Changes to an existing type save themselves.

## Invitation

**Prepare invitation** creates a draft circular with the agenda. For general meetings it goes to the members entitled to vote under the type (member types and minimum age), for board meetings to the board, and for leadership meetings of a unit to its role holders. Use **Open circular** to check the recipients and text and to send the invitation. After that the meeting counts as invited; if it went out after the last day of the notice period, HUBIplan points this out.

You also need the right to send circulars. If the agenda changes after the draft has been created, adjust the text in the circular. Until the invitation has gone out, the **Before the invitation** checklist shows whether the notice period can still be met, whether the agenda has items and whether every resolution and election item has an explanation. It never blocks anything.

## Attendance

If you also have read access to members, **Attendance** lists everyone entitled to vote at the meeting. For each person choose **Present**, **Excused** or, if the type allows proxies, **Represented** and then who holds the proxy. Only a present member with voting rights can act as proxy. Enter guests under **Guest without a vote**. The figures at the top show whether the meeting has a quorum under the rule of its type.

Organisations as members have one vote and attend **By representative**: choose a contact person marked “represents at meetings” or enter a name. This is not a proxy and also works if the type does not allow proxies. The minimum age of the type does not apply to organisations. If the representative is a member themselves, they keep their own vote; the list then shows “also represents”. The minutes name the organisation and its representative.

## Check-in via app and online voting

**Open check-in via app** shows a QR code that changes every 30 seconds; **Show code full screen** displays it full screen for the projector. Members scan it with the HUBIplan app or their phone camera and tap **I'm here**; **I'm leaving** checks them out again (any proxies then lapse). If the type allows remote participation, switch it on with **Allow remote participation for this meeting**; members entitled to vote then tap **Take part online** in the member area. If **Online voting on the phone allowed** is switched on for the type, you create a vote for resolution and election items, open or secret, for elections with one or more candidates.

**Start vote** opens it, **End vote** closes it and shows the result, **Transfer to the minutes** records it as a resolution or election. Members present and entitled to vote can vote, with one extra vote for each proxy. In a secret ballot no person is recorded on the ballot; in an open vote, **Who voted how** shows after the end who voted how. Remote participation and voting need a basis in the constitution (section 32 (2) German Civil Code).

## Minutes

After the meeting choose **Mark as held**. The agenda is then fixed and the minutes appear in its place. For each agenda item write down what was discussed. Use **Add resolution** to record a resolution with its text and result, and **Add election** to record an election with the office and the person elected. Enter the vote as yes, no and abstentions or tick **unanimous**. The minutes save themselves shortly after each entry, as soon as every resolution has a text and every election the office and the person elected.

## Approval

Under **Approval of the minutes** the chair and the minute taker confirm the minutes with **Confirm as chair** and **Confirm as minute taker**. Both must first be entered in the meeting details. **Preview as PDF** shows the minutes as a draft beforehand. Any change to the minutes or the attendance cancels the confirmations. With the second confirmation the minutes are approved: the resolutions receive a consecutive number per year (such as 2027/03), and the PDF is stored with a checksum and can no longer be changed. If document storage is switched on, HUBIplan files the PDF in the folder “Minutes”, which only the board sees at first. **Minutes as PDF** downloads the approved minutes.

## Resolution book

The **Resolution book** tab lists all resolutions and elections from approved minutes with number, date and result. Search by text, office or number and filter by year, type of meeting, resolution or election and implementation status. With editing rights you set the status to open, implemented or repealed. If the tasks module is switched on and you may create tasks, **Create as task** turns an open resolution into a task for you so its implementation is not forgotten. **List as Excel** downloads the filtered list.

## Taking elections into office

For an accepted election whose elected person was picked from the member list, **Take into office** opens the **Assign role** dialog in the club. The role named like the office is preselected, the term starts on the day of the meeting, and if you wish the predecessor's term ends the day before. The election then counts as implemented. You need the right to manage roles. Offices of units are still filled under Members › Offices.

## Member area

Members entitled to vote see meetings they are invited to there, with the agenda. They see approved minutes only if the meeting type makes them available to everyone entitled to vote; board minutes stay with the roles that have read access.

## Motions

For each type, **Types and notice periods** sets until how many days before the meeting members can submit motions; an empty field switches motions off. Invited members entitled to vote submit their motions in the member area. They appear in the meeting under **Motions**. **Add to agenda** turns a motion into a new agenda item; **Decline** gives the member a reason. This works while the meeting is in preparation or invited. If the invitation has already been sent, inform the members about the changed agenda.
en.seiten/webseite-aufbau.md:
---
key: page.website_structure
titel: Website › Menu and pages
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/aufbau]
stichworte:
  [
    menu,
    section,
    order,
    chronicle,
    member list,
    memorial,
    heading,
    search,
    instrument,
    link,
    button,
    home page,
  ]
---

Here you decide which sections the website has, such as events, sub-units, chronicle or contact, what they are called in the menu and in which order they appear.

## Unpublished changes

When there is a draft, the bar “Unpublished changes” with **Publish** and **Discard** is shown at the very top. It stays visible below the top bar while you scroll.

## Members

The heading “Members” has one list per member type, for example “Active” and “Passive”. You switch each list on separately and give it a name with the pencil. The lists show today’s members by surname, with the year they joined and, if you like, their main instrument (settings under “People”). Only members who consented appear: in the member record on the “Photo & website” tab under “Publication on the website”, item “Member list”.

Anyone who objected to publishing their name is still left out. “In memoriam” shows members whose reason for leaving is “death”, with the year of death, but only if the board has approved each of them in their member record under “In memoriam”; a text page with the address `in-gedenken` appears above it as an introduction.

## Custom headings

“Add heading” creates a menu item without its own page, for example “Band”. Drag sections onto it and they become its sub-items. Without sub-items the heading does not appear. If you leave the name empty, it is removed when saved.

## External links

“Add external link” creates a menu item that leads to another website, for example your federation. Use the pencil to enter the name and the address (with https://). The link opens in a new window and can be moved or made a sub-item like any other item. If you leave the name empty, it is removed when saved.

## Button

Under “Highlight a menu item as a button” you choose one main item that appears in the menu as a coloured button, such as “Contact” or a link “Become a member”. There is at most one button; headings and items with sub-items are not possible.

## Menu items in the footer

If the menu bar gets too full, “Menu items in the footer” lets you set for each main item whether it appears “in the menu”, “footer only” or “menu and footer”. In the footer it appears next to the legal notice and privacy policy, for example “Contact”. The page stays reachable and switched on. Headings and items with sub-items are not possible. “Home” and the search are set under Website › Fine-tuning, in the header and menu settings.

## Draft

Order, names, links, button and footer place of the menu go into the draft, like design and home page. The preview under Website › Design and colours shows the new menu; it becomes public with **Publish**. The check boxes that switch a section on or off, however, apply immediately.

## Home page

You put together the home page sections under Website › Home page, with the preview next to them.

## Repertoire and press

“Repertoire” shows the pieces from the sheet music library that are ticked “In the repertoire on the website”. “Press” shows the press clippings from Website › Documents.

## Bookings

“Bookings” shows facilities and material whose booking calendar is not set to “do not show” under “On the website”, as a week view with a calendar subscription. Depending on the setting it shows only “Booked” or, for public bookings, also the purpose; names never appear.

## Search

With the “Search” section a magnifying glass appears in the menu. It searches everything the website shows publicly: the greeting and sections of the home page (including tiles, buttons and questions), text pages with their sections, the chronicle, units, area introductions, albums, documents and events. Drafts and people are not searched. Part of a word is enough, and case and accents do not matter: “flag” finds “Flag bearers”.

## People

“Show titles before names” puts the title from the member record before the name (e.g. “Dr. Max Muster”) for the board, lists and results as well as for the authorised representatives in the legal notice (if the role is linked to the member record); when off, names appear without a title. “Show main instrument below the name” takes the main instrument from Music › Musicians. “Show postal address for the board” only applies to people with the consent “Postal address” in their member record.

## Sub-units

Under “Units on the website” you choose “all”, “selected” (with a check box per sub-unit) or “none”. Anyone allowed to edit the unit drags the sub-units in this list by their handle into the order in which they appear on the website; nested sub-units are sorted within their level. The order is saved immediately and is the same as under the sub-units menu item with “Change order”.

## Events

If there are sub-units, a check box adds their public events to the website calendar; if there are parent units with events (e.g. the umbrella association), a second one adds their events that are shared downwards. If there are neither, the “Events” block is not shown.
en.seiten/webseite-beitraege.md:

key: page.website_social
titel: Website › Social media
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/beitraege]
siehe: [guide.mcp_tasks]
stichworte: [Instagram, Facebook, post, social media]
---

Here you connect Instagram or Facebook and show selected posts on the website. HUBIplan stores the posts so the website works without third-party services.

Drafts for posts: if an AI assistant has prepared a post, it appears here with text and images. **Copy text** puts the text on the clipboard; clicking an image opens it for saving. You post in your own Instagram or Facebook account, then **Mark as done**. HUBIplan never publishes drafts itself.

At the top you manage the club’s social media channels, i.e. the profile links shown in the website header and in letter templates. They used to be under Settings › Organisation.

**Fetch now** schedules a background fetch. Repeated requests are coalesced; manual and periodic fetches of the same channel never run concurrently. Reload later to see the results. The web process does not wait for Meta or image downloads.
en.seiten/webseite-bilder.md:
---
key: page.website_images
titel: Website › Images
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/bilder]
stichworte: [image, photo, gallery, consent, author, creator, image credits, clipboard]
---

You upload and crop images for the website here. Instead of a file you can also use a copied image, such as a screenshot or an image from the browser: just press Ctrl+V, here or in the image picker. JPEG (including iPhone photos), PNG and WebP up to 15 MB are allowed; save HEIC images from an iPhone as JPEG first.

## In detail

Mind the rights: for photos you need the photographer's permission and, for recognisable people, their consent. Each image needs a short alternative text. Under “Creator” enter who took or provided the photo (for free images with the licence, e.g. “Max Mustermann, CC BY 4.0”). The website credits them as “Photo: …” below the image, in the enlarged view and collected in the legal notice under “Image credits”, even when captions are switched off.

Website images have a storage limit per unit (default 2 GB), set by the platform. Once it is reached, no new images can be uploaded until images no longer used are deleted.

---

Every website needs a privacy notice. Here you set where it comes from.

Under **Privacy notice** you choose **own text** or **link to own page**; then enter the **Address of the privacy notice**. For your own text, **Create text draft** writes a draft that matches the areas switched on for the website. **Recreate draft** replaces the existing text; save your own additions first.

The draft is a template and not legal advice. Read it through and add whatever is different for you.

routen: [/webseite/dokumente]
siehe: [guide.document_upload, guide.website_page]
stichworte: [documents, press, press clippings, newspaper article, PDF]
---

Here you upload files for the website, as PDF or image (JPEG, PNG, WebP). Each file belongs to a section:

- Press: press clippings, for example newspaper articles with source and date. They appear in the “Press” section, newest first.
- Documents: further files. They appear in the “Documents” section next to the statutes, fee regulations and founding deed.

You switch both sections on under “Menu and pages”. Images are rewritten when uploaded, which removes camera and location data. PDFs stay unchanged and get a preview image of the first page. With “Show on the website” you take a file off the website temporarily without deleting it.

Newspaper articles are protected by copyright. Only show them if the newspaper has agreed.

Search engines and “Images for AI assistants” are under Website › Overview.
en.seiten/webseite-fassungen.md:
---
key: page.website_versions
titel: Website › Versions
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/fassungen]
stichworte:
  [versions, earlier versions, texts, text pages, log, restore, design as a file, export, import]
---

Under **Versions** you find everything that concerns the whole design.

Under **Earlier versions of the design** you find the last five published designs (design, colour assignment, fine-tuning, area display, header images, home page and menu). **Restore** turns one of them into a draft; it only goes live with **Publish**. If nothing has been published yet, a notice appears here.

Under **Texts and text pages** you find the most recently published texts (greeting, text pages, texts of sub-units) with time and person. Each text has its own versions: **Open** takes you to the text under **Content**, where you restore an earlier version. If you only published text pages, you find the change here and not under the design.

## In detail

The website settings, images, design packages and the unit's colours and logo have no versions. They take effect immediately; what was changed is shown in the **Log**.

Under **Design as a file**, **Save design** saves the design, colour assignment, **Fine-tuning** and **Area display** as a small file. For another unit or on another server, **Load design** loads it into the draft again; it is checked like a change made by hand. If the design does not exist there, the other values still apply. Coat of arms, texts, images and the home page are not included; the colours follow the palette of the unit that loads the file. Unlike a design package the file contains no CSS; anyone who manages the website may load it.
en.seiten/webseite-feinabstimmung.md:
---
key: page.website_style
titel: Website › Fine-tuning
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/feinabstimmung]
stichworte:
  [
    fine-tuning,
    style controls,
    presets,
    font,
    corners,
    width,
    header,
    header image,
    banner,
    menu,
    title image,
    darken,
    tint,
    sub-pages,
    tables,
    date,
    footer,
    dark,
    contrast,
    dignitaries,
    placeholder,
    person cards,
    honours,
    honorary members,
    form of address,
    chronicle,
    eras,
    podium,
    ranking,
    lists,
    two columns,
    areas,
    display,
    monthly calendar,
    masonry,
    show,
    undo,
  ]
---

Under **Fine-tuning** you adjust the chosen design without any programming. Each control has fixed steps, for example corners “square”, “slight” or “round”; fonts are chosen from a list; yes/no questions are switches. Where it helps, a small icon above the word shows what the step looks like. Without your own choice the website shows what the design provides; that step is marked with a dot, and switches say “as the design”. If a design lies between the steps (for example the corners), there is no dot. All changes go into the draft first, and the preview on the right shows the effect.

## How the page is organised

On the left is the bar with the areas of the website, from top to bottom: **Basic style**, **Font**, **Readability**, **Header and menu**, **Title image and home page**, **Subpages**, **Website areas** and **Footer**. A click shows the controls of that area on the right, grouped into small sections (for the header and menu, for example, “Header”, “Menu” and “On phones”). The number next to an area tells you how many controls are changed there. On a phone you first see the list of areas; “‹ All areas” takes you back.

Each section shows the most important controls first. Less common ones are under “More settings” and are named there; changed controls always stay visible. The switch **Show all controls** expands everything and remembers this on the device. A small “i” next to the name opens an explanation.

Whatever does not apply right now stays greyed out and says why, for example “Choose “Darken” first.” for the tint, or “Search is switched off.” with a link to Menu and pages; “Go there” jumps to the control it depends on. Dependent controls are indented below that control. Whatever a design sets itself (such as the position of the coat of arms in the sidebar design) is listed in one line at the bottom of the section with the link **Change design**. Changed controls have a coloured edge on the left.

## Quick start, search and reset

Under **Quick start**, **Presets** set several controls at once: **Calm** (plain, lots of white space), **Festive** (serifs, script font, title image in club colour), **Modern** (round corners, shadows, menu as buttons) and **Easy to read** (Atkinson Hyperlegible font, large text, high contrast, striped tables). Afterwards every control can still be changed one by one.

The search field searches all areas, including the further settings, for example by “crest” or “phone”; each hit names its area and section. **Changed only** lists all changed controls: a click jumps to the control, “×” resets it. “↺” next to a control resets it, “↺ … changed” the section, **Reset area** the whole area and **Reset all** under Quick start all controls. A second click on the chosen field also resets the control.

**Undo** and **Redo** above the controls take back the last steps or bring them back, also after a preset or a reset (up to 50 steps, together with design and colours). Outside text fields this also works with Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z. The history starts again when you reload the page, publish or discard.

## Preview and pointing

After a change the preview jumps to the matching spot and briefly highlights it: header and menu at the top, the footer at the bottom, the page title on a sub-page (the legal notice), the date on the events page. For **Menu on phones** it switches to the phone view.

With **Show** above the preview it also works the other way round: move the mouse over the website, and the part below gets a frame and a label with its area. A click opens the matching controls; links do not lead away while doing so. A second click on **Show** switches it off.

## Font

- **Font**: “System”, “Modern” with Open Sans and Roboto, “Festive” with Open Sans and serif headings, “**Clear**” with Source Sans 3, “**Elegant**” with Source Sans 3 and headings in Crimson Pro or “**Easy to read**” with Atkinson Hyperlegible, whose letters are especially easy to tell apart.
- **Heading font**: “same as text”, “Modern”, “Festive”, “Clear”, “Elegant”, “**Blackletter**” or “**Bold**” with the narrow, heavy Oswald. Blackletter only suits headings and is never used for body text.
- Headings plain, with a line, **short line** (a short stroke in the decorative colour below the heading) or in colour, plus their alignment and the **Heading size** (“normal” or “larger”).
- **Page title size**: “small”, “medium”, “normal” or “larger”. It only applies to the heading at the top of the page and takes precedence over the heading size; “small” or “medium” fits if the title would otherwise look larger than the club name in the header.
- Line spacing and a script font for the greeting.

The fonts are stored on the website itself (free licences); nothing is loaded from other servers.

**Own font stack** takes a house font from a style guide that is not free, such as “Lucida Sans, Lucida Grande, Segoe UI, Arial”: up to six font names separated by commas. The website does not deliver a font file for it; the font only appears where it is installed on the device, otherwise the next one in the list and finally a sans-serif fallback (or a serif one if you write “serif” last).

On phones and under Linux the fallback usually appears. The free fonts above are not affected. The own font stack takes precedence over the font and also applies to headings unless a separate **Heading font** is chosen there; **Own font stack for headings** gives them their own list. Only letters, digits, spaces and hyphens are allowed.

## Readability

**Font size** up to “very large”, **Increased contrast** (darker text, stronger lines), **Dark mode** › “follow device” (the website turns dark when the visitor's phone or computer is set to dark; header, menu and footer keep their club colours, design packages with their own CSS stay light), **Striped tables** (every second row shaded, in the surface colour or lightly tinted), the **“Back to top” button on long pages** and **Fade in while scrolling** (“subtle”: sections and cards appear gently while scrolling; visitors who chose “reduce motion” on their device never see it).

## Basic style

Page, cards and buttons, images: width, background, spacing, corners (“square” also applies to photos and initials of people, the social media icons, the chronicle with its photos, cards and jump links, and the fields of the contact form), **Colour of light sections** (under title image and home page: home page sections with a light background “tinted” in the club colour, “warm” or “grey”), cards (border, shadow, flat or **white with stripe**: white cards with a fine edge, events with a club-colour stripe on the left, subunit tiles on top), images, **Image format in tiles** (3:2, 4:3 or square for home page tiles, gallery albums and posts), frames around images and buttons (“filled”, “outlined” or **Label**: capitals, slightly spaced).

On coloured sections, buttons and decorative lines always use the text colour of the section so they stand out.

## Header and menu

With **Background** › **Header image** you choose an image from the image library that appears at the top of the website instead of the coat of arms and club name, for example a banner with lettering. It should contain the club name and be wide, about 1200 × 300 pixels. Without a header image, or with the background “white” or “coloured”, the coat of arms and name stay. **Height** sets how tall the header image can get: “low”, “medium”, “normal” or “high”.

On a phone a wide header image quickly becomes too small next to the menu button; below the header image you can therefore choose an optional **Header image for phones**, which the website shows below 600 pixels wide. You can also choose several header images (and several header images for phones), up to ten: the website then shows one of them on each visit, on every page. Also here: **Crest** with its position, **Club name**, **Line below the header** and **Pin to the top**. The coat of arms and the club name cannot both be hidden.

In the menu section: **Menu style** (bar, buttons, text), **Active item**, **Lettering** (“normal” or in capitals), **Menu font size**, **Menu on phones** (“collapsible” behind the “Menu” button or as a **swipeable bar**), **“Home” in the menu** (off: on larger screens the coat of arms, name or header image lead to the home page, the phone menu keeps “Home”) and **Position of the search** (“in the menu”, “top right” in the header or “in the footer”). To hide the search completely, switch off the “Search” block under Website › Menu and pages.

## Title image and home page

**Height** of the title image, **Darken** (“slight” or “strong”) with **Tint** (“black”, “club colour” or “second colour”): a semi-transparent colour over the image makes text on it easier to read and tints the image in the club colours. **Image crop** sets whether the top, middle or bottom stays visible when the image is cropped.

**Name on the title image** with **Position of the name** (“top”, “centred” or “band at the bottom”), **Advance** of the carousel (“only by hand”, “slowly”, “normal” or “random”: the home page then shows a different image from the carousel on each visit, which stays fixed like a single title image; the same applies to the image in the heading band of the other pages) and **Separate sections** (“no”, “with a line” or “alternately tinted”; in the “Stage” design this switches the coloured bands off).

If the image carousel is set to full width under Website › Home, the title image reaches from edge to edge. **Width** › “edge to edge” puts the cover photo right below the header without border or gap, at a limited height, with a gradient in the dark club colour at the bottom; the title lines and overline from the “Image carousel” block sit on it on the left. Several title lines change calmly with the images; pausing the carousel also pauses the line.

**Carousel buttons** (pause, back, next and counter) are “always visible” or only appear “on mouse-over” on the image or with the keyboard; on phones and tablets they always stay visible. Without your own choice they are always shown on the stage, otherwise on mouse-over. “In content width” shows the same stage only as wide as the content column, so more of the photo stays visible on wide screens; the **Stage width** is “like the content”, “a little wider” or “wide”, and the **Area beside the stage** then shows the page background or the dark club colour. On phones it looks like “edge to edge”.

## Subpages

Under **Subpages**: **Page title** “plain”, as a **coloured band** or **with title image** (the home page image behind the heading, darkened as set there), the **Band of sub-units** on their pages (in the “club colour” like the other bands, in the “box colour” of the colour role “Date field”, “light” in the tone of the light sections with a fine line, or “plain with line” on the page background; light and plain show the name in the dark club colour so the band does not look like a second page header; it only applies when the heading is shown as a band).

## Website areas

Under **Website areas** you find the controls for each area: for events the **Events view** (“list by month” or “monthly calendar”; on a phone only the days with events appear), the **Date** as a tile, strip or **Cards** (the upcoming events on the home page and sub-unit pages as cards side by side with a large date, the next one in the club colour) and **Date next to it**: only the weekday, short (“Sat 14/11/2026”) or long (“Saturday 14 November 2026”).

The **Notice board view** is cards with photo or a compact list, the **Sub-units view** large or small tiles or a list, the **Gallery view** tiles or masonry with pictures at their own height; a sketch shows each option. You write an introduction at the top of an area under Website › Texts. If an area is switched off, it says so there with a link to Menu and pages.

## Individual pages

There are also controls for individual pages; without your own choice every page stays as it was:

- **Title holders** “Band and cards”: the current title holders appear large in a band in the dark club colour directly below the page title, with the photo on the left and, on the right, the dignity as a top line with a short line in the second colour, the name in large type and the term of office. Below, the last eight predecessors appear as cards (two side by side on a phone) and a button “All … entries” expands the full list. Without a photo the band stays, with text only.
- **People without a photo** “no placeholder”: the board, honours and contacts of sub-units no longer show an initial letter when there is no photo; the name moves to the left. Photos stay.
- **Person cards** “Office as a label”: the office in small capitals above the name, the name in large type in the heading font, “Write a message” as an underlined text link and a top edge in the club colour; several people in one office are listed one below the other, honorary members in a three-column grid.
- **Honours** “one card per person”: all honoured people appear in one shared grid with three columns (one on a phone) like the board, without subheadings. At the top of each card the honour appears in small type, below it the name in large type. If someone was given their own title with the award (field **Title**, e.g. “Ehrenhauptmann” for the honour “Ehrenmitglied”), the card shows this title. You enter the title in the member record next to the honour.

## Salutation, chronicle and lists

- The **Salutation** (formal “Sie” or informal “du” for the contact form and the events page) has been under Website › Overview › **Salutation** since 16 November 2026, because it concerns the tone of the texts rather than the design. Like the design, it only applies after **Publish**.
- **Chronicle eras** “as a band”: each era edge to edge in the dark club colour, with the period in large type in the second colour, the title and the text of the era; the timeline continues below. The jump links at the top become underlined links, and the years use the heading font. “as a slim band” shows the same band much lower: the period (in the second colour) and the title on one line, the text of the era small below; on phones the title moves below the period.
- **Result rankings** “Places 1 to 3 as cards”: above each ranking the first three places appear as cards with a large place number (place 1 in the club colour), name, sub-unit and result with its unit, such as “48 Ringe”. In a tie everyone sharing a place gets a card; the table below starts at place 4 and is left out when there are no further places.
- **Long lists** “in two columns”: long, narrow tables such as the list of all kings, the winners of a challenge trophy or the winners of a competition over the years appear side by side in two columns on a computer screen, so the page is only half as long. You read the left column from top to bottom first, then the right one. This only applies to tables with no more than two columns and at least 20 rows, and only from about 800 pixels wide; on a phone and in narrow windows it stays a single column. Screen readers still read one table in the right order.

Labels, the numbers of places 2 and 3 and the box next to the contact form use the colour you chose for the date field among the design colours.

## Footer

Colour, alignment, **Layout** (“simple” or “with crest and name”: the crest on the left, next to it the club name with founding year and town and the note on the umbrella association, on the right the links stacked and social media, below a fine line “© year · data from HUBIplan”; stacked on phones), with the crest layout the switches **Club name next to the crest** and **Founding year and town** (switch off if the crest or the header already shows the name; without the name the note on the umbrella association sits centred next to the crest, and the crest gives the name to screen readers) and **Line above the footer** (none, ornament line, second colour or club colour).
en.seiten/webseite-galerie.md:
---
key: page.website_gallery
titel: Website › Gallery
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/galerie]
stichworte: [gallery, photo album, album, sub-album, photos, cover image, sorting]
---

In the gallery you create photo albums for the website. An album can have sub-albums, for example “2024” with “Summer party” and “Annual trip”; it does not go any deeper.

Create an album: enter a title and choose “New album”. The address on the website (e.g. /galerie/schuetzenfest-2024/) is made from the title and can be changed. With a date the website shows the year and can sort the albums by it. For a sub-album, choose the parent album under “Belongs to album”.

## In detail

Photos: “Upload photos” takes many photos at once; you can also drag them onto the page. The photos are also added to the image library. Cropping is off while uploading to keep it quick; you can crop single photos later with “Edit image”. “Choose from the image library” adds existing images to the album. “Remove from album” does not delete the image.

Sorting: by default the gallery sorts images by date taken and albums by date (newest first). Choose “custom order” to sort by dragging. The cover is the chosen image, otherwise the first one.

Visibility: an album appears on the website only with “Show on the website”; a sub-album only if its parent album is shown as well. The “Gallery” section must also be switched on under “Menu and pages”. Only show photos of recognisable people with their consent.
en.seiten/webseite-gestaltung.md:
---
key: page.website_design
titel: Website › Design and colours
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/gestaltung]
stichworte: [design, colours, gradient, logo, draft, preview, publish, design package, icon]
---

Under **Design and colours** you choose the look, colours and logo of the website. The colours usually come from the unit's appearance and can be adjusted here. Design has its own items in the sidebar: **Design and colours**, **Fine-tuning**, **Areas** and **Versions**; you put together the home page under Website › Home.

## Assign colours

When assigning colours you choose a palette colour, white or dark for each place of the design (header, menu, decorative lines, footer, colour bands, date box). The header, footer, colour bands and decorative lines can also get a gradient from the appearance settings instead of a colour; the menu, buttons and date box stay single-coloured, and rounded edges show the first colour of the gradient.

Below, under **Text, surfaces and background**, you set the colour of body text, secondary text, surfaces (cards, table rows) and the page background. “Default” takes the colour ticked under **Used for** in Settings › Appearance, otherwise the design stays as it is; table rows then alternate with the surface colour; a chosen page background takes precedence over the “Background” control of the fine-tuning. If text on surfaces or background becomes hard to read (below 4.5 : 1), a notice appears.

## Draft and publishing

Changes to design, colours, fine-tuning, header image, areas and home page are a draft first: visitors keep seeing the previous version. At the top of each of these pages you then see “Unpublished changes”. **Publish** makes the draft public, **Discard** undoes all changes. On a wide screen, a preview on the right shows the real website with the draft; it reloads after every change. At the top you choose **Phone**, **Tablet** or **Desktop**, **Reload** reconnects the preview, **In a new window** opens it full size. On narrow screens the **Preview** button opens the website in a new window. Anyone you gave a preview link can see the draft as well.

## Browser icon

In the browser tab and on the phone home screen the website shows the unit's own icon, otherwise its coat of arms (square, with a transparent border). You set both under Settings › Appearance. Without an icon or coat of arms the website shows no icon of its own. Browsers often keep an old icon for a while; reloading the page helps.

## Share a design

Under **Share design** you save a design as a ZIP file with **Save as package**. The package contains the styling, the layout of header, footer and home page and the colour defaults, but no coat of arms, texts or images.

Whoever manages the website can import a package under **Load design from package**, for example to keep the previous look when moving from WordPress. With a new **Short name** and **Name** it becomes an own design. **Check** lets HUBIplan check the package: no JavaScript, no content from other addresses, no imported HTML/Django templates, only permitted CSS rules. **Import** releases the design for this website.

It applies to your unit only, other clubs do not see it, and the short name only has to be unique within your unit. A unit can import up to ten designs of its own, each package at most 2 MB. Under **Imported designs** you see your designs and the installation designs released for you, marked “this unit only” or “whole installation”.

Platform administrators import a package for the whole installation (or, with **for this unit only**, like a club) and switch the release on and off for each website. Under **Designs of units** they see all designs that units imported themselves and can block them with **blocked**; a website with a blocked design then shows Classic. Importing, deleting and blocking are recorded in the unit's change log.

Design packages use maintained built-in layouts with custom CSS and colours. Imported HTML/Django templates are rejected. Legacy packages with such templates are quarantined and display Classic until replaced by a package without templates. Layout markup follows maintained components rather than freezing historic HTML.
en.seiten/webseite-inhalte.md:
---
key: page.website_texts
titel: Website › Texts
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/inhalte]
stichworte: [text, page, home page, blocks, sections, banner, tiles, chronicle, timeline, chapter]
---

Here you write the website texts and put together the blocks of the home page. Changes are saved as you type; the latest versions of each text are kept.

## Text pages from sections

Under **Page sections** you build a text page from sections, like the home page. The existing text with the image at the top is the fixed section “Page text”; without further sections the page stays as before. **Add section** adds, for example, a **Banner**, a **Button bar**, **Tiles**, a **Quote**, **Frequently asked questions**, **Directions** or a **Document to download** above or below it; drag them by the handle into order. **Edit** opens content, background and width, **Apply** saves the section to the draft.

For the “Page text”, **Content width** sets the text at reading width along the content edge, **Text width** as a centred column and **Full width** without a limit; the page title always sits at the content edge. The website preview (Website › Design and colours, or a preview link) also shows the draft of texts and their sections. Everything becomes visible with **Publish**; earlier versions bring back their sections too. A **Cover image** is a narrow image at the very top above the heading; each page has at most one, and it always appears at the top, wherever it is in the list.

## Event pages

An event page is a text page about a public event. You create it at the event under “For this event” › **Website** › **Create**. At the top of the page, date, place, directions, programme, prices, places left, cancellation rule, terms of participation and the registration button appear by themselves, all taken from the event. Here you only write the text and sections below, such as the invitation, sponsors or pictures from last year. The menu item disappears on the day after the end; with **Remove from the website after the event has ended** the page disappears too.

## Sub-unit pages from sections

The text of a sub-unit (platoon, department, band, team) also has **Page sections**. Besides the “Page text” (image, text and picture carousel), it lists the fixed blocks “Contact”, “Own homepage”, “Title holders”, “Upcoming events”, “News (posts)” and “Follow us”. Drag them into a different order or hide them with the tick box. Before and after them you can add your own sections, such as **Text with image**, **Images**, a **Quote**, **Frequently asked questions**, **Opening and training hours**, a **Video as a link** or the **Title holders of a unit**. Without changes the page looks as before.

## Picture slot without a picture

If the photo is not there yet, leave the picture empty in **Text with image** or **Images** and write a **Note for the picture slot (optional)**, e.g. “Rehearsal scene, landscape”. The preview then shows a placeholder with this note. The empty picture slot does not appear on the published page.

## Area introductions

**Introduction for an area** lets you write a short text, with an image if you like, that appears at the top of the board, events, sub-units or gallery, as on the memorial page. The **Contact** introduction appears as a box to the right of the contact form (below it on a phone): the title as its heading, then the text; if the last paragraph holds nothing but a link, for example to your “Join in” page, it becomes a button. Without this introduction the contact page stays in one column. Each area has one introduction; it appears once you choose **Publish**.

## Image captions

For each text, **Show image captions on the website** decides whether the website shows the caption below the image at the top and in the image carousel. Without the tick (the default) the images appear without a caption; the description for screen readers stays.

## Chronicle as a timeline

The “Chronik” text has a short introduction at the top and the timeline below it (box **Timeline**). Each event has a year or a period (e.g. 1939 to 1948), a heading, at most 400 characters of text and, if you like, up to six pictures, such as posters from several years. On the website they appear small side by side; in the large view you can page through them.

Under “Picture position” you choose for each event whether the pictures appear on the left, on the right or large below the text; automatic alternates the side from entry to entry. On a phone they always appear below the text. Chapters (marked **Chapter**) such as “Founding years 1920–1938” are subheadings: below them the website shows all events from their year until the next chapter begins. **Add from Excel** brings a list with the columns Jahr (year), Überschrift (heading) and optionally bis (until), Text and Art (type, “Kapitel” for a chapter) into the draft.

With **Newest entries at the top** the website shows the timeline backwards, from the present to the founding; chapters still stay above their events and the jump links follow. Without the tick the order stays from old to new. The timeline is published together with the chronicle. The timeline belongs to the “Chronicle” module. When it is switched on, you maintain the introduction and timeline only under its own menu item **Chronicle**, even without rights on the website; here the chronicle then only shows the address, “show in menu” and delete.

en.seiten/webseite-startseite.md:
---
key: page.website_home_content
titel: Website › Home page
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/startseite]
stichworte:
  [
    home page,
    sections,
    content,
    change text,
    tiles,
    quote,
    contact persons,
    frequently asked questions,
    partners,
    sponsors,
    directions,
    video,
    divider,
    draft,
    publish,
  ]
---

Everyone edits the home page in one place: whoever manages the website puts it together here and changes the content; people who may only “Edit content” change the content of the existing sections. The **Preview** on the right shows the website with the draft.

Under **Home page** you build the home page from sections and see every change straight away in the preview. The fixed sections (such as welcome text, upcoming events, title holders) exist once each; you switch them on and off.

## Available sections

**Add section** adds your own sections, which you can use as often as you like:

- **Text**
- **Text with image** (the image left, right, above or below the text)
- **Banner**
- **Button bar**
- **Tiles**
- **Featured event** (with “N days to go”, disappears after the event)
- **Album preview**
- **Quote**
- **Contact persons** (only roles shown on the website, and people who have given their consent, as on the board page)
- **Frequently asked questions** (questions with answers to expand)
- **Partners and sponsors** (logos with a link; **Take over from business partners** fetches name and link of the business partners who have consented)
- **Directions** (address of a saved place with “Plan route”)
- **Events of one category** (the next public events of one category)
- **Document to download** (a published file from Website › Documents as a button)
- **Video as a link** (preview image linking to the video at the provider; the website embeds nothing)
- **Excerpt from the chronicle** (the latest timeline entries with a link to the chronicle)
- **Facts at a glance** (two to six numbers with a short text)
- **Divider** (line or space)

## More sections

- **Countdown** (counts down days, hours, minutes and seconds to the start of a public event or to a date and time of your choice; under **Afterwards** you choose whether the section then disappears or shows a text of your own, such as “The festival has started!”)
- **Become a member** (an invitation with a button to the “Become a member” page; only appears when the online application is switched on)
- **Call for donations** (text, bank details, payment reference, optionally a target with a progress bar and a link to a donation page)
- **Opening and training hours** (days with times and a note)
- **Two columns** (two blocks of text side by side, one below the other on phones)
- **Table** (one to six columns with a header row)
- **Timeline** (your own milestones with a time, independent of the chronicle)
- **Programme** (programme items with day and time; consecutive entries with the same day appear under one heading)
- **Notice box** (info, caution or success, permanent)
- **Expandable sections** (headings with text to expand)
- **Images** (one to eight images of your own with captions, enlarged on click; a single image spans the whole width, with **Full width** from edge to edge)
- **Download list** (up to ten published files from Website › Documents)
- **Title holders of a unit**
- **Results of a competition** (winners and standings of a chosen, published competition)
- **Gallery overview** (the first albums of the gallery)
- **Latest posts** (from Instagram and Facebook)
- **Members' area and app** (button to sign in, optionally with a QR code and a link to the app)
- **Figures from HUBIplan** (number of members, years since founding and number of units, always up to date and only as totals)

## Order and editing

Events and chronicle only appear when their area is switched on. Drag the sections by the handle into the order you want. **Edit** opens a section's content and appearance, **Apply** saves it to the draft, **Delete** removes one of your own sections.

## How long something is shown

For “Current results”, **Results of a competition**, **Gallery overview** and **Latest posts**, **How long to show** sets how long something counts as current: **Always** or 3 to 365 days after the competition, the date of the album or the post. Running and provisional competitions stay; albums without a date are then left out. If nothing is current any more, the section disappears by itself.

## Background, width and column

For each section you choose the **Background** (**None**, **Light**, a palette colour or a gradient, each with a matching text colour) and the **Section width** (**Text width**, **Content width** or **Full width**). In the “Newspaper” design, **Column** sets whether a section is in the **Main column** or the **Side column**. With a background you can add a **Watermark** behind it: the **Crest** or an **Image** from the image library, large, very faint and cropped on the right, for example a plain white heraldic animal on a transparent background; the text then stays on the left at reading width.

For the “Image carousel” block you enter **Title lines on the cover photo (optional)** (one per line, at most six) and an **Overline (optional)**. They appear when **Width** is set to “in content width” or “edge to edge” under Fine-tuning › Title image and home page; several title lines change with the carousel images. In the “Newspaper” design, **Column** sets whether a section is in the **Main column** or the **Side column**.

Buttons and tiles lead to a page of the website, the contact form, the page of a **Sub-unit** (such as a platoon), an event or, as an **External link**, to a new window. A link to an address on your own website opens in the same window. With **Button text (optional)** a tile with a target gets a button at the bottom, such as “Get in touch”; the title is then no longer a link. The buttons in a row line up at the same height and stay easy to read on a coloured background.

## Buttons and tiles

Buttons and tiles lead to a page of the website, the contact form, the page of a **Sub-unit** (such as a platoon), an event or, as an **External link**, to a new window. A link to an address on your own website opens in the same window. With **Button text (optional)** a tile with a target gets a button at the bottom, such as “Get in touch”; the title is then no longer a link. The buttons in a row line up at the same height and stay easy to read on a coloured background.

## Permissions, draft and publishing

With the “Edit content” permission you change the content of the custom sections, for example heading and text, the image or the buttons. Which sections exist, their order and how they look (background, width, column) is decided by whoever manages the website.

**Edit** opens a section, **Apply** saves the change to the draft. Visitors keep seeing the previous version until you choose **Publish**.

If the draft also changes the design, for example a different design, only the website managers can publish it. Your content changes stay in the draft and go online with it.
en.seiten/webseite.md:
---
key: page.website
titel: Website › Overview
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite]
siehe: [guide.website_design, guide.website_publish]
stichworte: [website, homepage, publish, language, search engines, AI assistants]
---

The overview shows the status of your club website and what is still missing before publishing, such as the legal notice or privacy notice. The website only reads what you release here; names and photos only appear with consent.

Under **Notice bar** a short notice appears at the top of every page, for example “Fair 22–25 Aug: programme”. With **Target** it leads to a page of the website, to an event or to an outside address. **Show from** and **Show until** set the period (both days included); afterwards the bar disappears by itself. Without dates it applies right away and without end; without **Notice bar text** there is none. The notice bar goes online immediately, not with the design draft.

## In detail

To make it stand out, choose the **Style** (accent colour, attention in a signal colour, festive with a pattern or plain in the header colour), the **Place** (above the header, below the header or floating at the bottom as a box visitors can close) and an **Icon**. With a target a button appears; its **Button label** is up to you, empty means “Learn more”. **Countdown to** shows “5 days to go”, “tomorrow” or “today”; if the target is an event and no date is set, the bar uses the event’s day.

Below **Status** come the basic settings: **Website language** (German or, where enabled, English for the fixed texts of the website), **Search engines** (whether search engines may index the website) and **Images for AI assistants**.

Images for AI assistants: under “Allowed servers” you enter host names from which a connected AI assistant may fetch images by address, such as `cloud.example.org` for the club’s Nextcloud. HUBIplan downloads the image itself, only via https and only JPG, PNG or WebP, and checks it like any upload. If the field stays empty, images only arrive via an upload link that the assistant offers in the chat.

The details help when creating a competition: target selection first shows the targets that suit your lanes. For competitions at other facilities the full catalogue remains available.

en.seiten/wettbewerbe-reihen.md:
---
key: page.competitions_series
titel: Competitions › Series
modul: competitions
rechte: [competitions.manage, competitions.results]

en.seiten/wettbewerbe-titel.md:
---
key: page.competitions_titles
titel: Competitions › Titles and winners
modul: competitions
rechte: [competitions.manage, competitions.results]

---

Titles and dignities such as “king” or “club champion” are set up here and awarded from a competition. The holders then appear in the chronicle. Kings and other honours of past years are added under Members › Title holders, where all honours are kept in one place.
en.seiten/wettbewerbe-urkunden.md:
---
key: page.competitions_certificates
titel: Competitions › Certificate templates
modul: competitions
rechte: [competitions.manage, competitions.results]

---

A certificate template defines the text, background, coat of arms and signatures of the certificates. They are printed in the competition under “Evaluation” for all placed participants at once.
en.seiten/wettbewerbe.md:
---
key: page.competitions
titel: Competitions
modul: competitions
rechte: [competitions.manage, competitions.results]
routen: [/wettbewerbe, /wettbewerbe/statistik]
stichworte: [shooting, bird shooting, ranking, shoot-off, result]
---

Here you set up your own shooting competitions with individual and team scoring, record results and decide ties in a shoot-off. Bird shooting with prizes and external competitions where you only enter your places also belong here. Provisional results only become fixed when marked final. If the shooting sports module is not switched on, the page speaks neutrally of participants, scores, tie-break and on-site entry instead of marksmen, shots, shoot-off and range mode; the procedures are the same.

## Stand mode and camera

Stand mode stores private data for the verified account or complete stand credential, for at most twelve hours and never beyond the credential's expiry. Without reception, the same stand remains available in the same browser tab. An explicit server access denial ends offline access. Signing out or switching accounts removes this browser's stand cache. Send outstanding entries before signing out; signing out asks before discarding them. Revoked or expired access also removes unsent entries. The old cache without account binding is removed on first opening this version; a notice appears if it contained unsent entries. Browser storage does not replace a backup.

In the live camera, the dashed circle shows where the outermost ring of the target should be; if the target has a black aiming area, a solid circle also shows where the black should be. On the card with five target faces (four corners and centre), the camera looks for all five and draws the circles around the ones it finds; it takes the picture once all five are straight, steady and fully in view. It does not need fixed card dimensions for this. This works the same in the browser and in the app.

## Setup

**Set up** separates **Basic data**, **Shooting conditions**, **Rankings** and **Output & sharing**. A target is selected by its image once per shooting round. Individual and centre-distance rankings can share the same recorded hits; unit rankings derive from an individual ranking. Facilities configured under [Competitions › Setup](/wettbewerbe/einrichtung) filter the target catalogue without removing existing selections. Targets with hit pattern, photo evaluation and bird shooting belong to the “Shooting sports” module; without it you enter results as values.

Under **Basic data** › **Event in the calendar** you link the competition to an event. The competition then takes the event's date, and empty place and description fields as well. If the event is moved later, the competition moves with it; competitions that are already final keep their date. If the dates still differ, a notice offers **Use the event's date**. If the event has binding registration, **Add registered people as starters** adds everyone registered: your own members as members, everyone else as a guest with their club; “adult” follows from the date of birth. Anyone already on the starter list is not added twice.

Changes to conditions or calculations require confirmation when results exist. Calculated results are recalculated, while manual totals remain and must be reviewed. After conditions change, stand mode requires the current setup and discards old offline entries. Finalising and reopening are available under **Evaluation** → **Competition and finalisation**.

## Names on the website

Members under 18 and members without a date of birth appear by name only with the consent “Competition results under 18”. Guests have no date of birth: tick “of age” when recording a new guest, otherwise the website shows “without name”. You can add this later under **Evaluation** in the section **Guests on the website**, also for closed competitions; prize winners entered by name only (for example after a starter was removed) are listed there too, and **Mark all as of age** handles a whole competition at once.

Under **Set up** → **Output & sharing** → **Publicly visible**, **prize places with names** publishes individual places up to the number of **prize places** configured for each scoring. Two prize places show places 1 and 2; five prize places show places 1 to 5. This also applies to the results block on the home page and to external competitions.

The results page shows the latest published competition directly; older competitions can be opened through links. Zero prize places show no individual places. Tied prize places are shown in full; existing consent and objections still apply. Unit and team rankings also show only their prize places, likewise with **only the scoring of subunits and teams**. All places appear only with **full ranking**.

## Address on the website

Results appear under a readable address made from title and year, such as `/ergebnisse/vereinsmeisterschaft-2027/`. You can choose it yourself under **Address on the website**; left empty, it follows the title again. Earlier addresses redirect.

## Personal results for connected clubs

Under **Evaluation** → **Result approval for connected clubs**, administrators with both
competition and peering management rights may explicitly assign otherwise unassigned
guest starters to an active downstream connection. Changes are audited and also
possible after completion; scores and places stay unchanged. An empty selection
revokes the local assignment. A starter already assigned to a unit uses that stable
assignment. Club names alone never authorize personal result sharing. The connection
must also allow the own-starters packet. Changes propagate on the next peering sync;
already received copies cannot reliably be recalled remotely.

## Lists and live tables

Name lists use a fixed alphabetical order: accented letters are placed with their base letter. Identical names keep their relative order when paging through the list.

On wide screens the live tables of the scorings (for example individual and unit ranking) appear side by side, on narrow screens one below the other. Live tables show an error and **Reload** even when the first request fails. Previously loaded rankings remain visible with a notice identifying the earlier state until updating succeeds.

## Statistics

Open **Competitions** › **Statistics** for participation, achievements and performance across
all members. Select a member for their personal statistics. The same view is available in
the member file under **Competitions**. Your own entries and results are under My area › Competitions.

Filter by year, competition type and scoring conditions. Average rings, rings per counted
shot and best results refer to the same recorded conditions. Different conditions have
separate averages; select a row to see the corresponding progress. Averages include the
number of valid results. The overall view also shows the equally weighted average of
personal member averages.

Only final results count. Missing values are not zero. Each person counts once per
competition. **Participations** counts all scored starts including guests and states how many
of them were guests; **Participating members** counts members only. Non-competing entries and
absent starters do not count as participations; **Participations** shows how many were not
counted. This is why the number of starters in the competition list can be higher. Wins and podium finishes count per individual standing. Team achievements
are not counted as personal wins. Chart values are also available as a table. Expand
**All starts and awards** to see ongoing competitions as well.

de.name: Wer braucht noch ein Konto mit Rolle?
de.text: Zugriff auf Mitgliederdaten soll nur haben, wer ihn für sein Amt braucht (Art. 5 Abs. 1 lit. f, Art. 32 DSGVO). Geh die Liste nach jeder Wahl durch und beende Rollen von Personen, die kein Amt mehr haben. Ohne Rolle bleibt einem Konto nur der eigene Mitgliederbereich.

de.name: aktiv / passiv
de.text: Kennzeichen einer Mitgliedsart: aktive Mitglieder nehmen voll am Vereinsleben teil, passive unterstützen vor allem mit ihrem Beitrag. Was das für Rechte und Beitrag bedeutet, regelt die Satzung.
de.example: Beispiel: 112 aktive und 38 passive Mitglieder: Der Dachverband berechnet seinen Beitrag für beide Gruppen getrennt.

de.name: Vorschuss
de.text: Geld, das der Verein vor einem Kauf auszahlt. Nach dem Kauf wird mit den Belegen abgerechnet, und der Rest geht zurück an die Kasse.
de.example: Beispiel: 300,00 € Vorschuss für den Einkauf zum Fest, Belege über 268,40 €: 31,60 € gehen zurück an die Kasse.

de.name: Anzahlungsrechnung
de.text: Rechnung über einen Teil des Entgelts vor der Leistung; die Umsatzsteuer entsteht schon mit der Zahlung (§ 13 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 Buchstabe a Satz 4 UStG). Die Schlussrechnung zieht die Anzahlungen mit ihrer Steuer ab (§ 14 Abs. 5 UStG).
de.example: Beispiel: Für das Sommerfest zahlt die Brauerei 1.190 € an; die Schlussrechnung über 4.760 € zieht sie ab, offen bleiben 3.570 €.

de.name: Altersstufen oder eigene Mitgliedsart?
de.text: Altersstufen setzen den Beitrag automatisch nach dem Alter zu Beginn des Geschäftsjahrs, ohne dass du die Mitgliedsart wechseln musst. Eine eigene Mitgliedsart wie „Jugend“ ist besser, wenn sich mit dem Alter auch Rechte oder die Meldung ändern. Unterschiedliche Beiträge brauchen eine Grundlage in Satzung oder Beitragsordnung (§ 58 Nr. 2 BGB).

de.name: Tagesordnung
de.text: Liste der Punkte, über die die Versammlung berät und beschließt. Ein Beschluss ist nur gültig, wenn sein Gegenstand schon in der Einladung bezeichnet war (§ 32 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: TOP 7 „Beitragserhöhung“ steht in der Einladung; über eine Satzungsänderung, die dort fehlt, kann die Versammlung nicht gültig beschließen.

de.name: Welche Einwilligungen abfragen?
de.text: Was für die Mitgliedschaft nötig ist, etwa Anschrift und Bankverbindung, verarbeitet der Verein ohne Einwilligung, weil er es für die Mitgliedschaft braucht (Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. b DSGVO). Einwilligungen gehören nur zu Freiwilligem wie Fotos oder dem Geburtstag auf der Webseite, jede einzeln und ohne Nachteil bei einem Nein (Art. 7 DSGVO). Sie lassen sich jederzeit widerrufen, also biete nur an, was der Verein nach einem Widerruf auch wieder abstellen kann.

de.name: Wer entscheidet über die Aufnahme?
de.text: Wer über die Aufnahme entscheidet, regelt die Satzung; meist ist es der Vorstand (§ 58 Nr. 1 BGB). Halte den Beschluss fest, etwa im Protokoll der Vorstandssitzung, bevor du aufnimmst. Mit der Aufnahme beginnen Mitgliedschaft und Beitragspflicht zum eingetragenen Datum.

de.name: Beitragsordnung bestätigen lassen?
de.text: Beiträge schuldet ein Mitglied nur, wenn die Satzung oder eine Beitragsordnung auf ihrer Grundlage sie regelt (§ 58 Nr. 2 BGB). Mit der Bestätigung im Antrag ist festgehalten, welche Fassung das neue Mitglied kannte. Das hilft, wenn später jemand Höhe oder Einzug des Beitrags bestreitet.

de.name: Minderjährige online beantragen lassen?
de.text: Ein Beitritt bringt die Pflicht zum Beitrag und braucht deshalb die Zustimmung der Eltern (§ 107 BGB); im Antrag bestätigt das mindestens eine erziehungsberechtigte Person. Willigt ein Kind unter 16 Jahren online ein, etwa in Fotos auf der Webseite, zählt ebenfalls die Zustimmung der Eltern (Art. 8 DSGVO). Ohne den Schalter nimmt das Formular keine Anträge von Minderjährigen an.

de.name: Arrangement
de.text: Eigene Fassung eines Stücks, etwa für eine andere Besetzung; rechtlich eine Bearbeitung. Solange das Original geschützt ist, darf sie nur mit Zustimmung des Urhebers veröffentlicht oder aufgeführt werden (§ 23 Abs. 1 UrhG), und sie ist selbst wie ein eigenes Werk geschützt (§ 3 UrhG).
de.example: Beispiel: Der Dirigent setzt einen Schlager von 1985 für 25 Bläser; vor dem Konzert holt der Verein die Zustimmung des Verlags ein.

de.name: Welche Ausgaben als Künstlerhonorar kennzeichnen?
de.text: Abgabepflichtig sind Honorare an selbständige Künstler und Publizisten, etwa Kapelle, DJ, Fotograf oder Grafiker, auch wenn sie selbst nicht in der Künstlersozialkasse sind (§ 25 KSVG). Nicht dazu gehören Zahlungen an eine GmbH, gesondert ausgewiesene Umsatzsteuer und steuerfreie Reisekosten (§ 25 Abs. 2 KSVG). Beauftragt der Verein Künstler nur für eigene Feste oder Werbung, beginnt die Abgabepflicht erst über 1.000 € Honorar im Kalenderjahr; bei höchstens drei Veranstaltungen im Jahr bleiben deren Honorare frei (§ 24 Abs. 2 KSVG).

de.name: Künstlersozialabgabe
de.text: Abgabe an die Künstlersozialkasse auf Honorare an selbständige Künstler und Publizisten (§§ 24, 25 KSVG). Die Summe eines Jahres meldet der Verein bis 31. März des Folgejahres (§ 27 KSVG).
de.example: Beispiel: 2.400 € für die Band beim Sommerfest; bei einem Abgabesatz von 5 % wären das 120,00 €.

de.name: Vermögensverwaltung
de.text: Einnahmen aus dem Vermögen des Vereins, etwa Zinsen oder langfristige Vermietung, ohne eigenen Geschäftsbetrieb. Bei gemeinnützigen Vereinen bleibt sie steuerfrei (§ 14 Satz 3 AO, § 5 Abs. 1 Nr. 9 KStG).
de.example: Beispiel: 1.200,00 € Pacht im Jahr für die verpachtete Vereinsgaststätte.

de.name: Sofort abschreiben, Sammelposten oder über die Nutzungsdauer?
de.text: Bis 800 € netto darf ein Gegenstand im Jahr der Anschaffung voll abgeschrieben werden (§ 6 Abs. 2 EStG), von 250 bis 1.000 € wahlweise als Sammelposten über 5 Jahre (§ 6 Abs. 2a EStG). Teurere Anlagen verteilen sich linear über die Nutzungsdauer laut AfA-Tabelle (§ 7 Abs. 1 EStG). Steuerlich zählt das nur im wirtschaftlichen Geschäftsbetrieb, und die Wahl für den Sammelposten gilt dann für alle Anschaffungen des Jahres.

de.name: Welche Empfehlung zur Entlastung?
de.text: „Entlastung empfohlen“ passt, wenn die Prüfung nichts Wesentliches ergab, „mit Anmerkungen“ bei Mängeln, die das Ergebnis nicht in Frage stellen. „Nicht empfohlen“ ist richtig bei ungeklärten Differenzen oder fehlenden Belegen; die Versammlung entscheidet trotzdem selbst. Die Prüfer berichten nur, Grundlage ist die Rechenschaftspflicht des Vorstands (§ 27 Abs. 3, § 666 BGB).

de.name: Warum der Kontenabgleich?
de.text: Nur wenn der Bestand laut Kassenbuch mit Kontoauszug und gezählter Barkasse übereinstimmt, ist die Buchführung vollständig und richtig (GoBD). Eine Differenz heißt: Es fehlt eine Buchung oder ein Betrag ist falsch erfasst. Klärt jede Differenz und schreibt die Ursache in die Anmerkung.

de.name: Warum Stichproben und welche?
de.text: Kassenprüfer müssen nicht jeden Beleg sehen, aber nachvollziehen können, dass jede Buchung belegt und richtig ist (GoBD, Nachprüfbarkeit). Die größten Ausgaben tragen das größte Risiko; zufällig gezogene Buchungen verhindern, dass nur ausgesuchte Belege geprüft werden. Bei Auffälligkeiten zieht weitere Stichproben, bis das Bild klar ist.

de.name: Kassenprüfer
de.text: Von der Mitgliederversammlung gewählte Mitglieder, die die Kasse prüfen und darüber berichten; ihre Aufgaben bestimmt die Satzung. Sie gehören nicht zum Vorstand, den sie prüfen.
de.example: Beispiel: zwei Kassenprüfer prüfen 312 Buchungen stichprobenartig und empfehlen die Entlastung.

de.name: B2B – Firmenlastschrift
de.text: SEPA-Lastschrift nur für Zahler, die keine Verbraucher sind, ohne Rückgaberecht nach der Belastung (EPC B2B Rulebook). Der Zahler muss das Mandat vorher seiner Bank bestätigen.
de.example: Beispiel: Die Sparkasse als Fördermitglied zahlt 250 € Jahresbeitrag per B2B; ohne Bestätigung bei ihrer Bank wird der Einzug abgewiesen.

de.name: Basislastschrift oder Firmenlastschrift?
de.text: Die Firmenlastschrift (B2B) gibt es nur für Zahler, die keine Verbraucher sind, etwa Firmen oder Vereine als Mitglied. Der Zahler kann eine autorisierte Belastung nicht zurückgeben, muss das Mandat aber vorher seiner Bank melden, sonst wird der Einzug abgewiesen (EPC B2B Rulebook). Nimm B2B für Organisationen mit eigener Buchhaltung, sonst die Basislastschrift mit 8 Wochen Widerspruchsfrist.

de.name: Saldo
de.text: Differenz von Einnahmen und Ausgaben, etwa je Kategorie. Positiv heißt: mehr eingenommen als ausgegeben.
de.example: Beispiel: Kategorie Sommerfest: Einnahmen 3.100,00 €, Ausgaben 2.700,00 €, Saldo 400,00 €.

de.name: pain.008 – Datei für die Bank
de.text: Die XML-Datei mit allen Lastschriften eines Laufs, die du im Online-Banking hochlädst. Ihr Format legt das SEPA-Regelwerk fest; die Bank zieht danach die Beträge ein (EPC016-06).
de.example: Beispiel: eine Datei mit 104 Lastschriften über 7.488,00 €: einmal hochladen statt 104 Einzelaufträge.

de.name: Jährlich oder öfter abrechnen?
de.text: Jährlich abrechnen spart Arbeit, Porto und Bankgebühren je Lastschrift. Halb- oder vierteljährlich verteilt hohe Beiträge auf kleinere Beträge, vervielfacht aber Läufe und Mahnungen. Was gilt, legen Satzung oder Beitragsordnung fest (§ 58 Nr. 2 BGB).

de.name: § 26 BGB – Vorstand nach § 26 BGB
de.text: Die Personen, die den Verein gerichtlich und außergerichtlich vertreten; wer dazugehört, bestimmt die Satzung. Sie stehen im Vereinsregister (§§ 26, 64 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: Laut Satzung vertreten 2 von 3 Vorstandsmitgliedern gemeinsam; die 7 Beisitzer des erweiterten Vorstands nicht.

de.name: Was gehört zu einem Vorstandswechsel?
de.text: Jede Änderung des Vorstands muss der Vorstand zur Eintragung ins Vereinsregister anmelden (§ 67 Abs. 1 BGB). Beende zugleich die Amtszeit des Vorgängers, damit seine Zugriffsrechte enden (Art. 32 DSGVO). Denk auch an Bankvollmacht, Impressum und Schlüssel.

de.name: Vorstand mit Pauschale vergüten?
de.text: Ohne Regel in der Satzung arbeitet der Vorstand unentgeltlich und bekommt nur seine Auslagen ersetzt (§ 27 Abs. 3 BGB). Eine Vergütung ohne Grundlage in der Satzung kann die Gemeinnützigkeit gefährden, weil Mittel satzungswidrig fließen (§ 55 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 AO). Kreuze das nur an, wenn die Satzung eine Vergütung des Vorstands ausdrücklich erlaubt.

de.name: Buchwert
de.text: Anschaffungskosten abzüglich aller bisherigen Abschreibungen (§ 7 Abs. 1 EStG). Er sagt, mit welchem Wert ein Gegenstand noch im Verzeichnis steht, nicht, was er beim Verkauf brächte.
de.example: Beispiel: Kühlanhänger für 6.000 €, nach 3 Jahren mit je 600 € Abschreibung: Buchwert 4.200 €.

de.name: Warum nur noch Storno statt Ändern oder Löschen?
de.text: Der ursprüngliche Inhalt einer Buchung muss feststellbar bleiben (§ 146 Abs. 4 AO), deshalb ist sie nach Ablauf des Folgemonats festgeschrieben (GoBD) und nur am Tag der Erfassung löschbar. Danach korrigierst du mit einem Storno: Eine Gegenbuchung hebt die falsche Buchung auf, beide bleiben sichtbar, und die richtige legst du neu an. Das ist umständlicher, macht aber jede Korrektur für Kassenprüfer und Finanzamt nachvollziehbar.

de.name: Haushaltsplan
de.text: Plan der erwarteten Einnahmen und Ausgaben für ein Geschäftsjahr, meist je Bereich oder Kategorie. Pflicht ist er nur, wenn die Satzung ihn vorsieht; beschließt ihn die Versammlung, richtet sich der Vorstand danach wie nach einer Weisung (§ 27 Abs. 3, § 665 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: Plan 4.000 € für das Sommerfest, Ist im Oktober 4.600 €; die 600 € Abweichung erklärt der Kassierer in der Versammlung.

de.name: CAMT.053 – Elektronischer Kontoauszug
de.text: Kontoauszug als Datei im Format camt.053 nach ISO 20022, den fast jedes Online-Banking anbietet; anders als eine CSV-Datei enthält er eindeutige Angaben wie IBAN, Verwendungszweck und Endsaldo.
de.example: Beispiel: Auszug Oktober mit 37 Umsätzen und Endsaldo 4.812,55 € als XML-Datei.

de.name: Welche Kündigungsfrist eintragen?
