Mit dem Link kommt die Webseite ohne Einwilligungsabfrage aus, dafür läuft das Video beim Anbieter und nicht auf der Vereinsseite.

de.name: Ehrenamtspauschale
de.text: Steuerfrei bis 960 € im Jahr (ab 2026) für nebenberufliche Tätigkeit im gemeinnützigen Bereich, etwa als Kassierer oder Platzwart (§ 3 Nr. 26a EStG). Für dieselbe Tätigkeit gibt es sie nicht zusätzlich zum Übungsleiterfreibetrag.
de.example: Beispiel: Der Platzwart erhält 80 € im Monat, also 960 € im Jahr; mehr wäre steuerpflichtig.

de.name: Wozu ein Alternativtext?
de.text: Screenreader lesen ihn blinden Besuchern vor, und er erscheint, wenn ein Bild nicht lädt (WCAG 2.2, Kriterium 1.1.1). Beschreib in einem Satz, was zu sehen ist und was davon wichtig ist. Reiner Schmuck wie ein Muster braucht keinen Text.

de.name: Was zeigt die Webseite ohne Einwilligung?
de.text: Namen von Mitgliedern auf einer öffentlichen Seite brauchen eine Rechtsgrundlage, meist ihre Einwilligung (Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. a DSGVO). „Auslassen“ ist am sichersten, ein Platzhalter hält dafür Listen wie die Königsliste vollständig. Einwilligungen und Widersprüche pflegst du in der Mitgliederakte unter „Veröffentlichung“.

de.name: Sollen Suchmaschinen die Webseite aufnehmen?
de.text: Mit Aufnahme finden Interessierte den Verein über Suchmaschinen, ohne sie bleibt die Seite nur über die Adresse erreichbar. Dafür tauchen dann auch Namen auf der Seite in Suchergebnissen auf (Art. 5 Abs. 1 lit. c DSGVO). Schalte es ein, sobald Impressum, Datenschutz und Namensform stimmen.

de.name: Wie viel vom Namen zeigt die Webseite?
de.text: Der volle Name macht Vorstand und Würdenträger eindeutig erkennbar, „Vorname N.“ schützt mehr, weil Suchmaschinen weniger finden (Art. 5 Abs. 1 lit. c DSGVO). Für Funktionen mit Außenwirkung wie den Vorstand ist der volle Name üblich. Bei Chronik und Würden reicht oft die kurze Form.

de.name: Welche Fotos dürfen auf die Webseite?
de.text: Bilder von erkennbaren Personen brauchen deren Einwilligung (§ 22 KUG, Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. a DSGVO). Ausnahmen gelten etwa für Bilder von Versammlungen und Umzügen, auf denen die Menge im Vordergrund steht (§ 23 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 KUG). Im Zweifel nimm Gruppenbilder von öffentlichen Auftritten und frag bei Nahaufnahmen nach.

de.name: Warum holt HUBIplan die Beiträge selbst ab?
de.text: Ein eingebetteter Instagram- oder Facebook-Beitrag schickt beim Seitenaufruf Daten an Meta; dafür bräuchte die Seite eine Einwilligung (§ 25 TDDDG), und der Verein wäre mitverantwortlich (EuGH, C-40/17). HUBIplan holt die Beiträge deshalb alle 30 Minuten selbst ab und zeigt sie ohne Verbindung zu Meta. Der Preis: Neue Beiträge erscheinen mit etwas Verzögerung, und jede Einheit braucht eine eigene Meta-App.

en.name: Who still needs an account with a role?
en.text: Only those who need it for their office should have access to member data (Art. 5(1)(f), Art. 32 GDPR). Go through the list after every election and end the roles of people who no longer hold office. Without a role, an account only keeps its own member area.

en.name: active / passive (aktiv / passiv)
en.text: Property of a membership type: active members take full part in club life, passive members mainly support with their fee. What this means for rights and fee is governed by the constitution.
en.example: Example: 112 active and 38 passive members: the umbrella association calculates its fee separately for both groups.

en.name: Advance
en.text: Money the club pays out before a purchase. After the purchase it is settled with the receipts, and the remainder goes back to the treasury.
en.example: Example: €300.00 advance for shopping for the festival, receipts for €268.40: €31.60 go back to the treasury.

en.name: Advance payment invoice (Anzahlungsrechnung)
en.text: Invoice for part of the price before the service; VAT already arises on payment (§ 13(1) no. 1(a) sentence 4 UStG). The final invoice deducts the advance payments with their VAT (§ 14(5) UStG).
en.example: Example: the brewery pays €1,190 in advance for the summer party; the final invoice for €4,760 deducts it, leaving €3,570 open.

en.name: Age bands or a separate membership type?
en.text: Age bands set the fee automatically by age at the start of the financial year, without you having to change the membership type. A separate membership type such as “Youth” is better if rights or reporting also change with age. Different fees need a basis in the constitution or fee regulations (§ 58 no. 2 BGB).

en.name: Agenda
en.text: List of the items the meeting discusses and decides on. A resolution is only valid if its subject was already named in the invitation (§ 32(1) sentence 2 BGB).
en.example: Example: item 7 “fee increase” is in the invitation; the meeting cannot validly decide on an amendment to the constitution that is missing there.

en.name: Which consents should you ask for?
en.text: What membership requires, such as address and bank details, the club processes without consent because it needs it for the membership (Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. b GDPR). Consents belong only to voluntary things such as photos or the birthday on the website, each one separately and with no disadvantage for a no (Art. 7 GDPR). They can be withdrawn at any time, so only offer what the club can switch off again after a withdrawal.

en.name: Who decides on admission?
en.text: The constitution governs who decides on admission; usually it is the board (§ 58 no. 1 BGB). Record the decision, for example in the minutes of the board meeting, before you admit. With admission, membership and the duty to pay fees begin on the date entered.

en.name: Have applicants confirm the fee rules?
en.text: A member owes fees only if the statutes, or fee rules based on them, provide for them (§ 58 Nr. 2 BGB). The confirmation in the application records which version the new member knew. This helps if someone later disputes the amount or the collection of a fee.

en.name: Let minors apply online?
en.text: Joining creates the duty to pay fees and therefore needs the parents' consent (§ 107 BGB); in the application at least one person with parental responsibility confirms it. If a child under 16 consents online, for example to photos on the website, the parents' consent is needed as well (Art. 8 GDPR). Without this switch the form does not accept applications from minors.

en.name: Arrangement
en.text: A version of a piece of your own, for example for a different line-up; legally an adaptation. As long as the original is protected, it may only be published or performed with the author’s consent (§ 23(1) UrhG), and it is itself protected like a work of its own (§ 3 UrhG).
en.example: Example: The conductor arranges a 1985 pop song for 25 wind players; before the concert the club obtains the publisher’s consent.

en.name: Which expenses to mark as artist fees?
en.text: The levy applies to fees paid to self-employed artists and journalists, such as a band, DJ, photographer or graphic designer, even if they are not insured with the artists’ social insurance fund themselves (§ 25 KSVG). Payments to a limited company, separately shown VAT and tax-free travel expenses do not count (§ 25(2) KSVG). If the club engages artists only for its own festivals or advertising, the levy only becomes due above €1,000 in fees per calendar year; with no more than three events a year, the fees for those events stay exempt (§ 24(2) KSVG).
en.section: Finance → Taxes → Artists' social security levy

en.name: Artists’ social levy (Künstlersozialabgabe)
en.text: Levy paid to the artists’ social insurance fund on fees to self-employed artists and journalists (§§ 24, 25 KSVG). The club reports a year’s total by 31 March of the following year (§ 27 KSVG).
en.example: Example: €2,400 for the band at the summer party; at a levy rate of 5 % that would be €120.00.

en.name: Asset management (Vermögensverwaltung)
en.text: Income from the club's assets, such as interest or long-term letting, without its own business operation. For non-profit clubs it remains tax-free (§ 14 sentence 3 AO, § 5(1) no. 9 KStG).
en.example: Example: €1,200.00 a year rent for the leased club restaurant.

en.name: Write off at once, pool or spread over useful life?
en.text: Up to €800 net an item may be written off in full in the year of purchase (§ 6(2) EStG); from €250 to €1,000 it may instead go into a pool written off over 5 years (§ 6(2a) EStG). More expensive assets are spread evenly over their useful life according to the depreciation tables (§ 7(1) EStG). For tax this only matters in the commercial operation, and choosing the pool then applies to all purchases of that year.

en.name: Which recommendation on discharge?
en.text: “Discharge recommended” fits if the audit found nothing significant, “with remarks” if there were flaws that do not call the result into question. “Not recommended” is right for unexplained differences or missing receipts; the meeting still decides for itself. The auditors only report; the basis is the board’s duty to account (§ 27(3), § 666 BGB).
en.section: Finance → cash audit → checks and result

en.name: Why reconcile the accounts?
en.text: Only if the balance in the cash book matches the bank statement and the counted cash are the books complete and correct (GoBD). A difference means a booking is missing or an amount was entered wrongly. Clear up every difference and note the cause.

en.name: Why samples, and which ones?
en.text: Auditors do not have to see every receipt, but must be able to confirm that each booking is documented and correct (GoBD, verifiability). The largest expenses carry the greatest risk; randomly drawn bookings prevent only hand-picked receipts being checked. If something looks wrong, draw more samples until the picture is clear.

en.name: Cash auditors (Kassenprüfer)
en.text: Members elected by the general meeting who audit the treasury and report on it; the constitution sets their tasks. They are not part of the board they audit.
en.example: Example: two cash auditors check 312 entries by sampling and recommend discharge.

en.name: B2B – Business direct debit (Firmenlastschrift)
en.text: SEPA direct debit only for payers who are not consumers, with no right to a refund after the debit (EPC B2B Rulebook). The payer must confirm the mandate with their bank beforehand.
en.example: Example: the savings bank as a supporting member pays its €250 annual fee by B2B; without confirmation at its bank the collection is rejected.

en.name: Core direct debit or business direct debit?
en.text: The business direct debit (B2B) is only available for payers who are not consumers, such as companies or clubs as members. The payer cannot reverse an authorised debit, but must register the mandate with their bank beforehand, otherwise the collection is rejected (EPC B2B Rulebook). Use B2B for organisations with their own accounts department, otherwise the core direct debit with its 8-week refund period.

en.name: Balance (Saldo)
en.text: Difference between income and expenses, for example per category. Positive means: more taken in than spent.
en.example: Example: category summer party: income €3,100.00, expenses €2,700.00, balance €400.00.

en.name: pain.008 – File for the bank (SEPA XML)
en.text: The XML file with all direct debits of a run, which you upload in online banking. Its format is set by the SEPA rulebook; the bank then collects the amounts (EPC016-06).
en.example: Example: one file with 104 direct debits totalling €7,488.00: upload once instead of 104 separate orders.

en.name: Bill annually or more often?
en.text: Annual billing saves work, postage and bank charges per direct debit. Half-yearly or quarterly billing splits high fees into smaller amounts but multiplies runs and reminders. The constitution or fee regulations decide (§ 58 no. 2 BGB).

en.name: § 26 BGB – Board under § 26 BGB (Vorstand nach § 26 BGB)
en.text: The persons who represent the club in and out of court; the constitution determines who belongs. They are entered in the register of associations (§§ 26, 64 BGB).
en.example: Example: according to the constitution, 2 of 3 board members represent jointly; the 7 assessors of the extended board do not.

en.name: What does a change of board involve?
en.text: The board must register every change of the board with the register of associations (§ 67(1) BGB). At the same time end the predecessor’s term so that their access rights end (Art. 32 GDPR). Also think of bank authority, legal notice and keys.
en.section: Roles → terms of office → new term

en.name: Pay the board an allowance?
en.text: Without a rule in the constitution the board works unpaid and only has its expenses refunded (§ 27(3) BGB). Paying the board without a basis in the constitution can put charitable status at risk, because funds are used against the constitution (§ 55(1) no. 1 AO). Only tick this if the constitution expressly allows paying the board.

en.name: Book value (Buchwert)
en.text: Purchase cost less all depreciation so far (§ 7(1) EStG). It states the value at which an item still stands in the register, not what it would fetch if sold.
en.example: Example: refrigerated trailer for €6,000, after 3 years of €600 depreciation each: book value €4,200.

en.name: Why only cancellation instead of changing or deleting?
en.text: The original content of an entry must remain ascertainable (§ 146(4) AO), so it is locked once the following month has passed (GoBD) and can only be deleted on the day it was recorded. After that you correct with a cancellation: a reversing entry cancels the wrong one, both remain visible, and you create the correct one anew. This is more laborious but makes every correction traceable for cash auditors and the tax office.

en.name: Budget
en.text: Plan of the expected income and expenses for a financial year, usually by area or category. It is required only if the statutes provide for it; if the meeting adopts it, the board follows it like an instruction (§ 27 Abs. 3, § 665 BGB).
en.example: Example: plan 4,000 € for the summer party, actual 4,600 € in October; the treasurer explains the 600 € difference at the meeting.

en.name: CAMT.053 – Electronic bank statement (elektronischer Kontoauszug)
en.text: Bank statement as a file in camt.053 format under ISO 20022, offered by almost every online banking system; unlike a CSV file it contains unambiguous details such as IBAN, reference and closing balance.
en.example: Example: October statement with 37 transactions and closing balance €4,812.55 as an XML file.

en.name: Which notice period should you enter?
en.text: Enter exactly the period and date from the statutes; HUBIplan calculates the earliest exit date from them. Every member may leave, and the statutes may bind leaving to a notice period of at most two years (§ 39 BGB). If your statutes say nothing, choose no notice period.

en.name: What do the cash auditors check?
en.text: The law does not provide for cash auditors; the constitution sets their tasks. They usually check whether every entry has a document, whether balances match bank statements and the cash box, and whether expenses are covered by decisions. Their report helps the general meeting decide on discharging the board, which owes an account (§ 27(3), §§ 666, 259 BGB).

en.name: Why count the cash box regularly, and with two people?
en.text: The cash box must be verifiable at any time: counted money and cash book should match (§ 146(1) AO). A count record with denominations proves the balance and makes a difference with its reason traceable; a second person protects the treasurer from suspicion but means one more appointment. Count at least at the end of each month and year, and whenever the cash box is handed over.

en.name: Cash count (Kassensturz)
en.text: Counting the cash and comparing it with the balance in the cash book. The cash box must be verifiable like this at any time (§ 146(1) AO).
en.example: Example: counted €412.30, cash book €415.00: the difference of €2.70 is booked with a reason.

en.name: Receipt (Quittung)
en.text: Written confirmation that money was received; whoever receives money must issue it on request (§ 368 BGB). For the treasury it is also the document for the entry.
en.example: Example: a member pays a €40 fee in cash at the summer party and gets receipt Q-2026-0012.

en.name: Treasurer's report (Kassenbericht)
en.text: Statement of opening and closing balance per account as well as income and expenses by category for a financial year. With it the board accounts to the general meeting (§ 27(3), §§ 666, 259 BGB).
en.example: Example: treasurer's report 2026 on four pages, signed by both cash auditors, is presented to the annual general meeting.

en.name: Chained log (verkettetes Protokoll)
en.text: Every entry in the change log contains a checksum of its predecessor; if one is changed or deleted, the chain no longer fits. This keeps it provable that changes were not suppressed (§ 146(4) AO, GoBD).
en.example: Example: entry no. 1205 refers to the checksum of no. 1204; if no. 1204 is missing, the daily check reports “no. 1204 to 1204 missing”.

en.name: Challenge cup
en.text: Cup that passes to the new winner after each competition. Whether someone may keep it after several wins is governed by the call for entries.
en.example: Example: whoever wins the cup 3 times in a row may keep it; Paul won it in 2025 and 2026.

en.name: Show title holders on the website?
en.text: Names and photos of former kings are personal data; for living people publication needs a legal basis, most safely consent (Art. 6(1) GDPR). For the deceased, relatives decide on photos for another ten years (§ 22 KUG). When in doubt, ask before you tick the box.

en.name: Combine letters per household?
en.text: One letter per household saves postage and paper when several members live at one address. For the invitation to the meeting, however, every member should demonstrably be invited, because errors in convening make resolutions open to challenge (§ 32(1) BGB). So combine greetings and information, and when in doubt send formal invitations individually unless the constitution allows otherwise.

en.name: Is an email enough as an invitation?
en.text: The constitution sets the form in which the general meeting is convened (§ 58 no. 4 BGB). An email is only enough if the constitution allows text form or email (§ 126b BGB); if it requires a letter, the invitation goes by post. The agenda belongs in the invitation, otherwise resolutions can be challenged (§ 32(1) BGB).

en.name: Official notice or information?
en.text: What belongs to membership, such as the invitation to the meeting or a note on the fee, the club may send to every member (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR). Advertising by email, by contrast, needs express consent (§ 7(2) no. 2 UWG), which is why members can unsubscribe from information. When in doubt choose “Information”: the message then reaches slightly fewer members, but nobody who no longer wants it.

en.name: Closing balance (Endbestand)
en.text: Money in an account at the end of the period: opening balance plus income minus expenses, plus or minus transfers. It must match the bank statement.
en.example: Example: €4,250.00 + €9,800.00 − €8,900.00 = €5,150.00: the bank statement for 31 December shows the same amount.

en.name: Lock a closed year instead of changing it?
en.text: After closing, the year is locked so that the audited treasurer's report stands and later changes remain visible (§ 146(4) AO). This protects against silent corrections but costs flexibility: you then correct errors with a reversing entry in the current year. Only close once the cash auditors have finished.

en.name: Which collection date to choose?
en.text: The collection date must be a bank working day and fall after the pre-notification period (EPC016-06). An early date brings the money in sooner; a date shortly after the start of the month often finds accounts in funds and can save returned debits. Do not collect before the invoices are due.

en.name: Collective invoice (Sammelrechnung)
en.text: One invoice to a sub-unit that pays its members' fees collectively instead of each member individually. The sub-unit then collects the fees itself (§ 58 no. 2 BGB).
en.example: Example: collective invoice Jägerzug: 18 members, €1,296.00: the unit transfers one amount for everyone.

en.name: wGB – Commercial operation (wirtschaftlicher Geschäftsbetrieb)
en.text: An independent, ongoing activity by which the club earns income and that goes beyond asset management (§ 14 AO). Corporation and trade tax are only due when this income including VAT exceeds €50,000 a year (§ 64(3) AO).
en.example: Example: drinks sales at the summer party, €14,000.00: taxable area, but below the threshold.

en.name: Elimination and fixed order?
en.text: If whoever has won a prize drops out, more shooters get a prize. In fixed order, prize after prize is shot, and HUBIplan offers the next one right after each hit. Which rule applies is in the club's shooting rules.

en.name: Scored shots (gewertete Schüsse)
en.text: The shots whose rings count towards the score; the others are sighting or dropped shots. How many count is set by the club's shooting rules or the DSB sport regulations.
en.example: Example: 5 shots, 3 of them scored: whoever shoots 9, 10, 8, 10, 7 has 29 rings with the best three, if the rules count the best.

en.name: Decimal scoring (Zehntelwertung)
en.text: Every shot counts with one decimal place, the closer to the centre the higher, on the air rifle at most 10.9 (DSB sport regulations). This makes ties much rarer than with whole rings.
en.example: Example: a hit 0.8 mm from the centre of the DSB air rifle target counts 10.6, one 3 mm off 9.8.

en.name: What does closing for good mean?
en.text: After that entries are locked, and only final results are intended for the website and honours. Open shoot-offs block the closing, because places would otherwise remain unresolved. Published results must be factually correct (Art. 5(1)(d) GDPR); “Reopen” remains for corrections.

en.name: final (endgültig)
en.text: Status after closing: entries are locked, the results stand. Only final results are intended for the website and honours.
en.example: Example: after the 2nd shoot-off the shooting master closes the competition; after that no score can be changed.

en.name: Guest (Gast)
en.text: Participant who is not a member; HUBIplan only stores name and club for them (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR). Whether guests may shoot for prizes is set by the call for entries.
en.example: Example: “Gerd Gast, SV Nachbarort” shoots 26 rings; for the unit ranking he can be assigned to a sub-unit.

en.name: Hole in hole (Loch in Loch)
en.text: Several shots are so close that their holes merge; then the outline does not reliably show where each hole is. Every shot is still scored by its hole edge (DSB sport regulations), which is why photo recognition says “please check”.
en.example: Example: 5 shots in one bullseye give a single, jagged hole about the size of 2 separate holes.

en.name: Inner ten (Innenzehner)
en.text: A particularly good ten: on the DSB air rifle target it is one that shoots away the white ten dot completely (DSB sport regulations). More inner tens often decide a tie.
en.example: Example: a hit 0.8 mm from the centre is an inner ten, one 2.3 mm off only a ten.

en.name: Lot number (Losnummer)
en.text: Number from the hat that sets the order of shooters in the bird shoot. Latecomers draw a number still free; the procedure is governed by the shooting rules.
en.example: Example: whoever draws lot 7 shoots after number 6 and before number 8.

en.name: What is “lots in the hat” for?
en.text: Without this, “Draw number” only draws up to the number of shooters so far, and a latecomer usually gets the next number. With the number of lots in the hat, HUBIplan draws as if from a real hat; if you prefer to draw for everyone at once, use “Draw all without number”. How the order is decided is governed by the shooting rules.

en.name: Hors concours (außer Konkurrenz)
en.text: The shooter takes part and appears in the list but gets no place and no prize. Common for range officers or guests from neighbouring clubs (§ 25 BGB, shooting rules).
en.example: Example: the range officer shoots 30 rings hors concours; 1st place goes to the best with 28.

en.name: Organiser (Ausrichter)
en.text: Club or association that holds and scores an external competition. It sets rules and prizes.
en.example: Example: at the district shoot 2027 the district association is the organiser; you only enter your places, for example 3rd place with 287 rings.

en.name: Own or external competition?
en.text: In your own competition you record shooters and scores yourself, and HUBIplan calculates places, unit ranking and shoot-offs. In an external one you only enter what the organiser has announced: place and score of your own participants. How scoring works there is governed by the organiser's shooting rules.

en.name: Why is the photo only a suggestion?
en.text: With several holes inside each other, on a dark background or close to a ring line, recognition can be wrong; what counts is the evaluation of the target under the DSB sport regulations or the club's shooting rules. That is why the photo only places the hits in the tap view, and only “Save” takes them over. The photo itself is only evaluated and never stored, so no image linked to the shooter is created (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR).
en.section: Range mode → Photo of the target

en.name: Collect bullseye crops?
en.text: Real, confirmed targets are the only way to check how good photo recognition really is; without them it is only measured on artificial photos. Only the crop of the bullseye with the hit positions is stored, without name, competition or time, so without reference to a person (Art. 4 no. 1 GDPR). Switch it on if the club uses recognition often; switching off and deleting everything is possible at any time.

en.name: Total and photo differ, which applies?
en.text: The total entered is what is saved; the photo is only a second opinion that makes typing errors and miscounted rings stand out. If they differ, look at the target again; if in doubt, the supervisor or scorer decides under the DSB sport regulations or the club's shooting rules. “View hits” shows where recognition sees the holes.
en.section: Range mode → Enter total only → Photo of the target

en.name: Prize piece (Pfand)
en.text: Part of the bird for whose shooting down there is a prize, such as head, wing or tail. Whoever brings it down has won the prize piece; prize pieces and prizes are set by the shooting rules.
en.example: Example: Paul brings down the left wing with shot 54 and receives the wing medal.

en.name: Prize place (Preisplatz)
en.text: Place for which there is a prize according to the call for entries, for example the first three. Only here does a tie need a shoot-off (§ 661 BGB).
en.example: Example: with 3 prize places, a tie for 3rd place must be shot off, one for 4th place not.

en.name: What are prize places for?
en.text: Only on prize places does a tie decide a prize, so HUBIplan only requires a shoot-off there; below them, tied entries share the place. How many places get a prize is in the call for entries. A publicly announced prize is a public promise of reward by which the club is bound (§§ 657, 661 BGB).

en.name: When is the shooting finished?
en.text: HUBIplan does not detect the end itself, because only the range officer knows about latecomers, absentees and shoot-offs. “Finish shooting” marks the results as provisional; additions and shoot-offs remain possible. Only hand out provisional lists with this note so that nobody takes them as final.
en.section: Competition → Results → Competition and completion; range mode → Finish

en.name: provisional (vorläufig)
en.text: Status after “Finish shooting”: results are in, additions and shoot-offs are still possible. Lists carry the note “provisional” so that nobody takes them as final.
en.example: Example: in the evening the provisional list is put up; a shoot-off the next morning still changes 3rd place.

en.name: What happens when resetting?
en.text: Resetting deletes all recorded scores, shoot-offs, shots and fallen prizes; rules, prizes, range access and event remain. Tablets that still have old entries stored without reception discard them at the next sync. Whether a round is repeated is governed by the shooting rules; resetting cannot be undone.

en.name: Round (Runde)
en.text: One pass through all lot numbers; after that the next round starts again at the lowest number. Absentees and those eliminated are skipped (shooting rules, § 25 BGB).
en.example: Example: with 40 shooters the second round starts with the 41st shot.

en.name: Shoot-off (Stechen)
en.text: Additional shooting in case of a tie on a prize place, with its own rules for number of shots and scoring. If it is tied again afterwards, another shoot-off follows; the rules are in the shooting rules or the DSB sport regulations.
en.example: Example: Anna and Paul both have 28 rings for 1st place; in a 1-shot shoot-off Anna scores 9, Paul 8, Anna comes first.

en.name: Why the shoot-off rules only when creating it?
en.text: Whether 1 or 3 shots are fired in a shoot-off is often decided by the range officer. HUBIplan suggests the rule from “Setup”; changing it is possible until the first score is entered, otherwise the conditions would change in the middle of the shoot-off. For association competitions the DSB sport regulations govern the shoot-off, in the club its own shooting rules.
en.section: Competition → Evaluation or range mode → Create shoot-off

en.name: What are number of shots and maximum per shot for?
en.text: With scored shots and a maximum, HUBIplan rejects impossible values when recording, for example 31 with 3 scored shots of at most 10. That way typing errors at the range are noticed before they shift places. The numbers are in the club's shooting rules or the DSB sport regulations.
en.section: Competition → Setup → Shooting conditions and rankings

en.name: Shots for the prize piece (Schüsse für das Pfand)
en.text: Shots since the previously fallen prize piece up to the one that brought down this prize piece. For the first prize piece all shots since the start count; what prizes exist for is governed by the shooting rules.
en.example: Example: the head falls with shot 30, the tail with shot 75: for the tail it took 45 shots.

en.name: Bullseye (Spiegel)
en.text: The black circle in the middle of the target that is aimed at; a card has one or more bullseyes (DSB sport regulations). Photo recognition first looks for the bullseye and then aligns the image.
en.example: Example: the bullseye of the DSB air rifle target measures 30.5 mm and reaches from the 4 ring to the ten.

en.name: Why range access instead of signing in?
en.text: A borrowed tablet gets its own key that can only record this competition and expires at the end of the competition day. That way nobody enters their password on someone else's device, and the tablet only sees name and sub-unit (Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 32 GDPR). If a device is lost, end the access immediately.
en.section: Competition → Record → Other device via QR code

en.name: Range access (Standzugang)
en.text: Access via QR code for a device without signing in, only for this competition and until the end of the competition day (Art. 32 GDPR).
en.example: Example: the borrowed tablet “Range 2” scans the code and can record until 23:59.

en.name: Range mode (Standmodus)
en.text: Full-screen view for a tablet or phone at the range, with large search and input; it keeps working without reception. It only shows what is needed for recording (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR) and sends as soon as there is a connection again.
en.example: Example: at the range the supervisor types “Mül”, chooses Jürgen Müller and enters 27.

en.name: What are target and scoring type for?
en.text: If HUBIplan knows the target, it calculates ring, tenths, inner ten and distance from each hit according to the DSB sport regulations: if the edge of the hole touches the ring line, the higher ring counts. Without recorded hits everything stays as before: you enter the total, and a shoot-off decides ties. The results are internal to the club, not official.
en.section: Competition → Setup → Shooting conditions and rankings

en.name: Why do only the best shooters of a unit count?
en.text: With “sum of the best 5”, a large unit does not win merely by having more shooters, and weak results drag no one down. A unit with fewer than 5 shooters is therefore not ranked, otherwise it would be at a disadvantage against full units. The DSB sport regulations also rank teams with a fixed number of shooters.
en.section: Competition → Setup → Rankings → Ranking of sub-units

en.name: Distance value (Teiler)
en.text: Distance of the centre of the hole from the centre of the target in hundredths of a millimetre; smaller is better (DSB sport regulations, with a factor for some targets). In a Teiler shoot the best single shot wins.
en.example: Example: a hole whose centre is 0.8 mm from the centre of the target has the Teiler 80; Teiler 80 beats Teiler 120.

en.name: Tie (Gleichstand)
en.text: Two or more shooters have the same score. They share the place; on prize places a shoot-off decides (club shooting rules, DSB sport regulations).
en.example: Example: two scores of 27 rings give 2nd place twice; the next shooter is fourth.

en.name: Which rules for ties?
en.text: With rules based on the hits, HUBIplan decides a tie without a shoot-off, for example under the DSB sport regulations first by the series from the back, then by more tens and more inner tens. This saves time at the range but requires hits to be recorded for everyone tied; otherwise it stays with the shoot-off. Take the order from the club's shooting rules or the call for entries; if nothing is stated there, the shoot-off remains the usual solution.
en.section: Competition → Setup → Rankings → Ties and shoot-offs

en.name: Ranking of sub-units (Wertung der Untereinheiten)
en.text: Ranking of units or departments from the individual results of their shooters, for example as the sum of the best 5 (unit ranking). Units with too few shooters remain unranked, as with teams under the DSB sport regulations.
en.example: Example: unit 1 with 28, 27, 25, 24, 22 and 20 rings has 126 rings with “best 5”.

en.name: Results on the website?
en.text: Showing names with results usually relies on the club's legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR); members can object (Art. 21 GDPR), and for minors ask the parents. For photos of the winners §§ 22 and 23 KUG also apply. “After closing” only shows checked results, “live” also interim standings.

en.name: Consent (Einwilligung)
en.text: A person's voluntary, informed agreement to a specific processing of their data, e.g. for a photo. It can be withdrawn at any time (Art. 6(1)(a), Art. 7 GDPR).
en.example: Example: consent given on 12 March, withdrawn on 2 May: from 2 May the photo no longer appears.

en.name: Set a reminder before the notice period?
en.text: If a contract renews automatically, the last day of the notice period counts, not the end of the contract; whoever misses it is often bound for another year. Notice period and renewal are set in the contract; the law sets limits mainly for standard business terms (§ 309 Nr. 9 BGB). Set the reminder so that there is still time for a board decision before the period runs out.

en.name: Term of protection
en.text: Copyright expires 70 years after the author’s death (§ 64 UrhG). After that the work is free, but a more recent adaptation may still be protected (§ 3 UrhG).
en.example: Example: A composer died in 1950; his march has been free since 1 January 2021, an arrangement from 2010 has not.

en.name: Creditor ID (Gläubiger-ID)
en.text: The creditor identifier marks the club as a submitter of direct debits; in Germany the Bundesbank issues it on application. Together with the mandate reference it makes every mandate unique (Bundesbank, EPC016-06).
en.example: Example: DE98ZZZ09999999999: “DE” stands for Germany, “ZZZ” is a fixed placeholder.

en.name: Which details belong in a custom field?
en.text: Collect only what the club needs for its purpose, such as the clothing size for club clothing or the instrument (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR). Details on health, religion or political opinion are specially protected and do not belong in a custom field (Art. 9 GDPR). Every field also means work, because it has to be kept up to date and handed over when someone requests their data.

en.name: Cut-off date (Stichtag)
en.text: The day for which a figure is counted or calculated, such as members, age or account balance. Whoever is a member on that day counts.
en.example: Example: cut-off date 1 January 2026, 150 members: whoever joins on 2 January only counts at the next cut-off date.

en.name: Data provision on media (Datenträgerüberlassung)
en.text: In an audit the tax office may demand the accounts as machine-readable files (§ 147(6) AO). The data export provides all tables, documents and a description (index.xml) for this.
en.example: Example: for the 2025 audit the treasurer downloads “Kasse-2025-Export.zip” and gives the file to the auditor on a USB stick.

en.name: Why does every category need a DATEV account?
en.text: The tax adviser books according to a chart of accounts (SKR 42 or SKR 49). Every income and expense needs a ledger account there, otherwise it ends up in a suspense account and must be rebooked by hand (GoBD). Agree the accounts with the tax adviser beforehand, then the export works every year without rework.

en.name: Direct debit run
en.text: One pass in which HUBIplan bundles due invoices with a mandate into a file for the bank. The bank collects all amounts on the same day.
en.example: Example: run of 2 March with 142 direct debits totalling €8,520.00, collection on 9 March.

en.name: How long to keep data after leaving?
en.text: Personal data must not be stored longer than necessary (Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17(1)(a) GDPR). A short period protects former members, a longer one allows queries, rejoining and honours; invoices and entries stay longer anyway because of tax retention (§ 147 AO). Base the period on possible queries, for example the three-year limitation period (§ 195 BGB).

en.name: Deletion period (Löschfrist)
en.text: Time after leaving after which HUBIplan reduces a member's data to a minimum. Personal data may only be stored as long as necessary for the purpose (Art. 5(1)(e) GDPR).
en.example: Example: left on 31 December 2025, period 24 months: from January 2028 only name, date of birth and periods remain.

en.name: AfA – Depreciation (Abschreibung)
en.text: Spreading the purchase cost of an item over the years it is used (§ 7(1) EStG). For tax it only matters in the commercial operation.
en.example: Example: a refrigerated trailer for €6,000 with a useful life of 10 years: €600 depreciation per year.

en.name: Discharge (Entlastung)
en.text: By granting discharge the general meeting approves the board’s conduct for a period and waives claims for damages it knew of or could have known of with careful checking. It rests on the board’s duty to account (§ 27(3), § 666 BGB).
en.example: Example: the meeting on 14 March 2027 grants the board discharge for 2026 with 48 yes and 0 no; the 4 board members do not vote.

en.name: Who should see the documents in a folder?
en.text: The more widely a folder is visible, the more easily members find the constitution and minutes. At the same time the risk grows that personal data goes too far (Art. 5(1)(c) and (f) GDPR). General items such as the constitution can be widely visible; minutes with names, contracts and lists, if in doubt, only for the board.

en.name: What may be deleted for good?
en.text: Accounting vouchers must be kept for eight years, books and annual accounts for ten years and business letters for six years (§ 147(1) and (3) AO). The club needs minutes and the constitution permanently, even though the law sets no period for them. After 30 days in the bin a document is gone for good; restore it before then if the period is still running.

en.name: Who may issue donation receipts?
en.text: Any tax-privileged corporation with its own notice, including an unregistered association (§ 10b(1) sentence 2 no. 2 EStG, § 5(1) no. 9 and § 1(1) no. 5 KStG). What matters is the tax office's notice, not the entry in the register of associations. Dependent sub-units such as units or departments usually have no notice of their own; the club confirms their donations.

en.name: Also confirm membership fees?
en.text: If the club mainly promotes sport, local heritage, customs or leisure culture, membership fees are not deductible as donations (§ 10b(1) sentence 8 EStG); this usually applies to shooters's, sports and carnival clubs. A receipt for them would be incorrect, and the club is liable for the lost tax (§ 10b(4) EStG). Only switch it on if the notice names other purposes, such as youth welfare or monument protection.

en.name: What must be documented for a donation in kind?
en.text: The value of the item is confirmed: for used items the market value (gemeiner Wert), for items from a business the withdrawal value (§ 10b(3) sentences 2 and 3 EStG). Describe the item precisely and keep documents on its value, such as a purchase receipt or expert opinion; without them the amount cannot be upheld in an audit. HUBIplan always issues donations in kind individually, never in a collective receipt.

en.name: Who is liable for an incorrect receipt?
en.text: Whoever issues an incorrect receipt intentionally or through gross negligence is liable for the lost tax, a flat 30% of the confirmed amount (§ 10b(4) EStG). The club keeps a duplicate of every receipt (§ 50(7) EStDV); HUBIplan stores the PDF for this. You correct errors by cancelling and issuing anew, not by changing.

en.name: How long does the tax office's notice last?
en.text: The club may only issue donation receipts as long as the exemption notice is at most 5 years old or the determination under § 60a AO at most 3 calendar years old (§ 63(5) AO). After that HUBIplan issues nothing until the new notice is entered. File the tax return in good time so that no donor has to wait for their receipt.

en.name: Donation receipt (Zuwendungsbestätigung)
en.text: Certificate from the club for a donation or a deductible fee, following the official template; only with it can the donor deduct the amount from tax (§ 10b(1) EStG, § 50(1) EStDV). Colloquially called Spendenquittung.
en.example: Example: Ms Muster donates 3 × €50 during the year: in January she receives a collective receipt for €150.

en.name: When is waiving expenses a donation?
en.text: Only if a claim to reimbursement existed beforehand by contract or constitution and the person then waives it. The claim must not already have been granted on condition of the waiver (§ 10b(3) sentences 5 and 6 EStG). Travel costs under a club travel expense rule are typical; without one, the waiver is not a deductible donation.

en.name: Confirm individually or once at year end?
en.text: The collective receipt combines all monetary donations of a donor in a calendar year and saves work and postage; the individual receipt comes immediately; both follow the official template (§ 50(1) EStDV). Up to €300 the bank statement together with a document from the club is often enough for the donor (§ 50(4) sentence 1 no. 2 EStDV). Common practice: large donations individually at once, everything else collectively in January.

en.name: Do we need a data protection officer?
en.text: It is mandatory if as a rule at least 20 people are constantly engaged in the automated processing of personal data (§ 38(1) BDSG) or the core activity requires it (Art. 37 GDPR). In small clubs this is rarely the case. Appointed voluntarily, a contact person still helps but takes time and expertise.

en.name: due (fällig)
en.text: From the due date the club may demand payment; it results from invoice date and payment term. If the member then does not pay despite a reminder, they are in default (§§ 271, 286(1) BGB).
en.example: Example: invoice dated 1 March, payment term 14 days, so due on 15 March.

en.name: How long should the payment term be?
en.text: The payment term is the period from the invoice date to the due date. A member is only safely in default after a reminder sent once the amount is due (§ 286(1) BGB). A short term brings the money in sooner but means more reminders; a long term the opposite.

en.name: Reminder level (Mahnstufe)
en.text: Step in the reminder process reached a certain number of days after the due date, with its own text and possibly a charge. With the first reminder after the due date the member is in default (§ 286(1) BGB).
en.example: Example: payment reminder after 14 days without charge, 1st reminder after 28 days with €2.50 postage.

en.name: How many reminder levels and what charge?
en.text: More levels give late payers more opportunity but take time and delay expulsion or a court payment order. Charges beyond actual costs such as postage need a basis in the constitution or fee regulations (§§ 280(2), 286, 58 no. 2 BGB). Start with a friendly reminder without a charge and add levels if a lot is still open afterwards.

en.name: Reminder by email or letter?
en.text: By email the reminder is quick and free; by letter, receipt is easier to prove. A reminder only takes effect once it is received (§ 130(1), § 286(1) BGB). Email is usually enough for a first reminder; before expulsion or a court payment order a letter is safer.

en.name: E-invoice (E-Rechnung)
en.text: Invoice in a structured data format (XRechnung or ZUGFeRD) that a program can read; a PDF alone is not an e-invoice (§ 14(1) UStG). Since 2025 every business must be able to receive them, including a club with a commercial operation.
en.example: Example: the brewery sends invoice RE-2026-0815 for €1,190.00 as an XML file; HUBIplan reads amount and date and keeps the file as a document.

en.name: Why start and end of service?
en.text: Every invoice must state when the goods or services were supplied (§ 14(4) sentence 1 no. 6 UStG). For longer services such as a season’s rent the period states exactly that; for a single day start and end are the same. Without it the recipient cannot deduct input VAT.

en.name: Which details to pass on per person?
en.text: Every ticked detail goes to the organiser and to everyone who handles the entry there. Only tick what is needed for start, scoring or classification, for example year of birth instead of date of birth (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR). The name is always part of the entry.
en.section: Entries → call for entries → details per person

en.name: Why work out the festival's day's takings backwards?
en.text: Without a cash register, not every sale is recorded individually; the takings result from closing balance minus float plus expenses paid in cash and withdrawals (open till, § 146(1) AO). This is simple but requires a complete count record at the end, because without it the takings cannot be proven. An electronic till would be more precise but needs a certified security device (§ 146a AO).
en.section: Finance → cash count → festival cash report

en.name: Event public or members only?
en.text: Public events reach guests and the press and can be subscribed to as a calendar. Internal events protect place, time and participants, for example for board meetings or youth gatherings (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR). Make public what should be known anyway, and keep everything else internal.

en.name: Exemption limit
en.text: If income from commercial operations including VAT stays at or below €50,000 a year, no corporation or trade tax is due on it (§ 64(3) AO). If it is higher, the whole profit is taxable, not just the part above the limit.
en.example: Example: €48,300 income from festivals and advertising is below the limit; at €50,400 the whole profit would be taxable.

en.name: Exemption notice (Freistellungsbescheid)
en.text: Notice from the tax office that the club is exempt from corporation tax because of its non-profit status, usually as an annex to the corporation tax notice (§ 5(1) no. 9 KStG). It comes after the tax return, usually every three years.
en.example: Example: notice of 14 March 2024 for the years 2021 to 2023: receipts are possible until 14 March 2029.

en.name: Expense
en.text: Money someone has advanced for the club and gets back against a receipt. Anyone acting on behalf of the club can claim reimbursement of the necessary expenses (§ 670 BGB).
en.example: Example: Anna buys drinks for the summer party for €42.80, uploads the till receipt and gets the amount transferred.

en.name: Donation by waiver of expenses (Aufwandsspende)
en.text: Someone waives reimbursement of expenses that the club owes them; the waiver then counts as a monetary donation (§ 10b(3) sentences 5 and 6 EStG).
en.example: Example: 120 km trip to the association conference at €0.30 under the travel expense rule, so €36, and the treasurer confirms €36 as a donation.

en.name: Why should the invoice be made out to the club?
en.text: The club can only deduct input VAT from invoices made out to it (§ 15(1) UStG). Up to €250 a till receipt without the buyer’s name is enough (§ 33 UStDV). This only matters if the club pays VAT; still, always have larger invoices made out to the club.

en.name: Reimburse travel costs at a flat rate per kilometre?
en.text: Anyone driving on behalf of the club can claim reimbursement of their expenses (§ 670 BGB); a flat rate per kilometre saves fuel receipts. Up to €0.30 per kilometre is usual, the highest rate of the Federal Travel Expenses Act (§ 5(2) BRKG). Set the rate and occasions in a board resolution or travel expense rules so that everyone is treated equally.

en.name: What to do if the receipt is missing?
en.text: No entry without a voucher (GoBD). If it is missing, for example because a till receipt was lost, a self-issued voucher replaces it, stating date, amount, recipient, occasion and why the voucher is missing. It should remain the exception, and no input VAT can be deducted from it (§ 15(1) UStG).

en.name: Why can you not approve your own expense?
en.text: Anyone acting for the club may not conclude a transaction with themselves unless permitted (§ 181 BGB). That is why another person approves your own expense. The club sets an exception for small amounts in the settings; a second person then reviews afterwards.

en.name: From what amount two approvals?
en.text: From this amount two people approve, the four-eyes principle. It protects the treasury from errors and the treasurer from suspicion, but takes time. The law names no amount; the board only has to be able to account for its actions at any time (§ 27(3), § 666 BGB).

en.name: Include an external calendar?
en.text: Events from an external calendar appear unchecked in the club’s calendar. This saves double upkeep, for example for the umbrella association’s events. If you also show them on the website, they count outwardly as the club’s own information, for which it is responsible (§ 7(1) DDG).

en.name: Family fee
en.text: A joint, usually reduced fee for several members of one household. It only applies if the constitution or the fee rules provide for it (§ 58 no. 2 BGB).
en.example: Example: 2 adults and 2 children together pay €120 instead of 4 × €40 = €160 individually.

en.name: Verbandsnr. – Association number (Verbandsnummer)
en.text: Number under which the umbrella association lists a member, so that reports and honours are assigned unambiguously. It is part of the data that goes to the umbrella association (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR).
en.example: Example: association no. 1920-0457: the same member, even if they change unit.

en.name: Accept clear proofs automatically?
en.text: Only proofs that HUBIplan classifies as clear are accepted automatically; all others and every rejection are still checked by a person. This saves work with many proofs, but nobody looks at the clear ones any more. After the decision HUBIplan deletes the file and keeps only the note (Art. 5(1)(c) and (e) GDPR).
en.section: Fee rates → reduction with proof → accept automatically

en.name: When does a reduction with proof make sense?
en.text: A reduction, for example for pupils, students or pensioners, needs a basis in the constitution or fee regulations (§ 58 no. 2 BGB). The proof makes sure the rule applies equally to everyone. If it is missing by the deadline, HUBIplan bills the regular fee.

en.name: Fee run (Beitragslauf)
en.text: Creates the fee invoices for a period all at once, according to each member's fee rules. The basis is the obligation to pay fees under the constitution or fee regulations (§ 58 no. 2 BGB).
en.example: Example: fee run 2026 with 142 invoices totalling €9,360.00: one click instead of 142 separate invoices.

en.name: Calendar year or different financial year?
en.text: The calendar year suits tax, because corporation tax is assessed by calendar year (§ 7(3) KStG). A different financial year suits clubs whose year follows a season or festival, but may require additional statements for the tax office. What the constitution says is decisive.

en.name: Financial year (Geschäftsjahr)
en.text: The period for which the club accounts and presents a treasurer's report, usually the calendar year. The constitution can set a different year.
en.example: Example: financial year 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026: the summer party in June falls at the end of the same year.

en.name: Four-eyes principle
en.text: A second person checks and approves before money flows. This way errors are noticed, and nobody decides on a payment alone.
en.example: Example: expense of €620.00: treasurer and 1st chairperson approve one after the other.

en.name: How to handle the export file?
en.text: The file contains all personal data, treasury and invoices of the unit and leaves the protection of HUBIplan when downloaded. Only pass it on encrypted and only to people who need it for their task (Art. 32 GDPR). Delete copies as soon as the purpose is fulfilled (Art. 5(1)(e) GDPR).

en.name: GEMA – Society for musical performing and mechanical reproduction rights
en.text: Collecting society that manages the rights in public performances for composers, lyricists and publishers and collects a fee for them (§ 2 VGG, § 15(2) UrhG).
en.example: Example: For the spring concert with 12 pieces the club registers the event beforehand and submits the set list afterwards.

en.name: QR code on the invoice?
en.text: The QR code contains recipient, IBAN, amount and reference, so members scan it with their banking app instead of typing (EPC069-12). That avoids typos and wrong references; not every banking app reads it. It is worthwhile as soon as members pay by transfer rather than direct debit.

en.name: Grace period
en.text: Additional days after the deadline in which a proof still counts as on time. Only after that does HUBIplan bill the regular fee.
en.example: Example: deadline 31 January, 14 days’ grace: a proof dated 10 February still counts.

en.name: Should volunteers see the other names?
en.text: Anyone who can see who else is on duty can coordinate or share lifts. At the same time the club passes names on to other members, which should be limited to what is necessary (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR). Switch it on if coordination within the shift matters, otherwise leave it off.

en.name: Who pays, and who gives the mandate?
en.text: The fee may also be paid by someone other than the member, such as a parent for the children (§ 267(1) BGB). The direct debit mandate, however, must be given by the account holder themselves, otherwise they can return the collection as unauthorised for another 13 months (EPC SEPA Direct Debit Core Rulebook). So enter as payer the person who owns the account.

en.name: IBAN / BIC – Account number and bank code (IBAN/BIC)
en.text: The IBAN is the international account number, 22 characters in Germany; the BIC identifies the bank and is no longer needed for payments within the SEPA area. A check digit in the IBAN catches most typing errors (EPC016-06).
en.example: Example: DE02 1203 0000 0000 2020 51: “DE” for Germany, “02” is the check digit.

en.name: Non-profit sphere (ideeller Bereich)
en.text: The actual club work for the statutory purpose, financed mainly by fees and donations. For non-profit clubs this area is tax-free (§ 52 AO, § 5(1) no. 9 KStG).
en.example: Example: membership fees €9,360.00 and donations €800.00 belong to the non-profit sphere.

en.name: Why name the author on the picture?
en.text: Whoever took a photo may decide whether and how their name appears on the picture (§ 13 UrhG). Without the credit there is a risk of a warning letter and damages, even if the club was allowed to use the picture. Enter the name with the picture straight away; the website shows it on the picture and in the legal notice.

en.name: Which columns to import?
en.text: Old lists often contain more than the club needs today, such as occupation or place of birth. Only import columns that serve a purpose of the club (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR). What is missing can be added later; what is superfluous you would have to delete again later.

en.name: Legal notice (Impressum)
en.text: Mandatory information about the provider of a website: name, address, authorised representatives, contact and, if registered, register and number (§ 5 DDG). It must be easy to reach from every page.
en.example: Example: an “Impressum” link in the footer of every page, no more than 2 clicks away.

en.name: Why approve an incoming invoice on the merits?
en.text: Whoever ordered or received the service confirms that it was delivered as invoiced; only then does the treasurer pay. Two people check what one would otherwise decide alone, and errors or duplicate invoices are caught earlier (GoBD, internal control system). In small clubs where one person does everything, the chair can give the approval.

en.name: Input VAT
en.text: VAT the club itself pays on purchases. If it pays VAT, it may deduct this from invoices for its business (§ 15(1) UStG).
en.example: Example: drinks for the festival €1,190.00 gross: €190.00 input VAT reduce the VAT the club pays to the tax office.

en.name: Which invoice date for the fee run?
en.text: The payment term runs from the invoice date; at its end the amount is due (§ 271 BGB). A date shortly before sending is right; a backdated one shortens the members' term, a late one delays the money coming in.

en.name: Routing ID (Leitweg-ID)
en.text: Identifier that routes an e-invoice to the right office of a public authority; invoices to federal authorities must contain it (§ 5(1) ERechV). The authority states it with the order or the grant notice.
en.example: Example: the town gives routing ID 05162000-0001-12 for the hall rental; it goes in the “buyer reference” field.

en.name: Register details on the letterhead?
en.text: For clubs, the register court and register number are voluntary on letters; they do show, however, that the club is registered. On invoices, by contrast, the full name and address as well as the tax number or VAT identification number are mandatory (§ 14(4) nos. 1 and 2 UStG). With the box ticked, the details from the legal notice appear on every letter, so they are missing nowhere.

en.name: Lending (Ausleihe)
en.text: Handing over an item for use free of charge, legally a loan for use (§ 598 BGB). The borrower returns it on time and is liable for damage, but not for normal wear (§§ 602, 604 BGB).
en.example: Example: the Jäger unit borrows 20 beer table sets from 3 to 5 July; 2 come back with a broken leg, which is noted on return.

en.name: SEPA mandate (SEPA-Mandat)
en.text: The payer's permission for the club to collect amounts from their account, and at the same time the instruction to their bank to honour the direct debit (EPC016-06). Without a valid mandate the club may not collect (§ 675j(1) BGB).
en.example: Example: 104 of 142 members have granted a mandate: their fee arrives without a transfer.

en.name: Expired mandate (Mandat verfallen)
en.text: A mandate expires if no direct debit has been collected on it for 36 months. After that a new mandate is needed (EPC016-06).
en.example: Example: last collection in May 2023, then expired in May 2026: the member must sign again for the next fee.

en.name: Mandate reference (Mandatsreferenz)
en.text: Unique identifier of a mandate at the club, up to 35 characters. It appears on every direct debit and pre-notification so that the payer can match it (EPC016-06).
en.example: Example: mandate reference M-0042: on the bank statement the member recognises which mandate the collection belongs to.

en.name: Store material with a member?
en.text: What belongs to the club remains club property, even if it is kept at a member’s home. Whoever keeps it for the club must hand it over, at the latest when the office or task ends (§ 667 BGB, for the board via § 27(3) BGB). Enter the location so that after a change it is clear where the things are.

en.name: What does a connected AI assistant see?
en.text: A connected assistant may never do more than you: it reads the unit’s website and edits it, texts only as drafts. What it reads is processed by its provider, including names and pictures in the texts. Clarify beforehand whether the club may do this, and name the provider in the privacy notice (Art. 13(1)(e), Art. 28 GDPR).

en.name: Which notice period and form for the invitation?
en.text: The constitution sets the form and notice period of the invitation (§ 58 no. 4 BGB); enter exactly those values here. Every matter to be decided must already be named in the invitation, otherwise the resolution is invalid (§ 32(1) sentence 2 BGB). An invitation sent too late makes every resolution of the meeting open to challenge.

en.name: Who approves the minutes?
en.text: The constitution sets how resolutions are recorded and who signs the minutes (§ 58 no. 4 BGB), usually the chair and the minute-taker. The register court requires a copy after a board election or a change to the constitution (§§ 67, 71 BGB). Once approved, the minutes can no longer be changed, so check them together beforehand.

en.name: Motions from members before the meeting?
en.text: The meeting can only safely decide on a motion that was announced with the invitation (§ 32(1) sentence 2 BGB). A deadline for motions gives the board time to announce motions it has received but rules out spontaneous ones. Take the deadline from the constitution; if it says nothing, the board decides.

en.name: Allow remote participation?
en.text: Whoever convenes the meeting may allow members to take part and vote electronically, as long as there is also a venue (hybrid meeting, § 32 Abs. 2 BGB). A purely virtual meeting, by contrast, needs a resolution of the members or a rule in the statutes. The invitation must say how members exercise their rights remotely, for example checking in and voting in the app.
en.section: Meeting → Check in with the app and online voting

en.name: Allow voting by proxy?
en.text: By law the right to vote is personal and cannot be handed to anyone else (§ 38 sentence 2 BGB). The constitution may allow proxies (§ 40 BGB); this helps members who cannot attend but risks a few people collecting many votes. Only switch it on if the constitution provides for proxies.

en.name: Minimum attendance for a quorum?
en.text: The law sets no minimum: a properly convened meeting can pass resolutions however many attend (§ 32 BGB). A minimum protects against decisions by small groups but can paralyse the meeting if too few turn up. Only enter a value if the constitution requires one (§ 40 BGB).

en.name: Vote by secret ballot?
en.text: A secret ballot protects against pressure and is common for elections and sensitive personnel matters. In return, nobody can check afterwards who voted how, not even in a dispute about the result. It is required only if the statutes, election rules or a resolution of the meeting demand it (§§ 32, 40 BGB).

en.name: Membership type (Mitgliedsart)
en.text: Group of members with the same rules, such as “active”, “passive” or “youth”. It determines the fee, reporting to the umbrella association and whether the time counts towards length of membership (§ 58 no. 2 BGB).
en.example: Example: “Passive” with an annual fee of €36.00 instead of €72.00 for “Active”: whoever no longer takes an active part pays half.

en.name: When is a membership type “active”?
en.text: Active members are counted separately, for example for the association fee per active member and in the development figures; passive members often pay less and take less part in club life. A fine-grained division helps with reporting and fees but takes upkeep if members change often. Follow the constitution or fee regulations, which set out which groups exist and what they pay (§ 58 no. 2 BGB).

en.name: Which periods count towards length of membership?
en.text: If a type counts towards duration, its periods feed into anniversaries and honours. In favour: loyalty is also recognised as a passive member; against: if the honours regulations only count active years. Adopt the rule from the constitution or honours regulations so that honours are calculated the same for everyone.

en.name: Which members to report to the umbrella association?
en.text: The club passes reported members with their data to the umbrella association, which then calculates its fees. Every transfer needs a legal basis and should be limited to what is necessary (Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 6(1) GDPR). Report the types that the umbrella association's constitution requires, and no more.

en.name: Length of membership (Mitgliedsdauer)
en.text: Total of the periods in which someone was a member, without gaps between leaving and rejoining. Only membership types marked “counts towards duration” count.
en.example: Example: 1998 to 2010 and again from 2014 gives 24 years in total in 2026; the 25-year anniversary follows in 2027.

en.name: When to reset two-factor sign-in?
en.text: Resetting helps when someone has lost their phone, but removes the account’s second protection until the person sets it up again. Only reset if you are sure who is asking, for example after calling back on the known number. Protecting access appropriately is the club’s duty (Art. 32 GDPR).

en.name: Mileage rate
en.text: Fixed amount per kilometre driven instead of individual fuel and parking receipts. The club sets the rate; up to €0.30 is usual (§ 5(2) BRKG).
en.example: Example: 84 km to the district meeting and back × €0.30 = €25.20.

en.name: What applies to payments to musicians?
en.text: Part-time artistic work for a non-profit club is tax-free up to €3,300 a year (§ 3 no. 26 EStG). The limit applies per person across all clients; so have it confirmed that it has not been used up elsewhere. Fees to self-employed musicians can also trigger the artists’ social levy (§ 24(2) KSVG).

en.name: Statement of assets (Vermögensübersicht)
en.text: List of accounts, fixed assets, receivables and liabilities at the end of the year. It is part of the board’s accounting to the general meeting (§ 27(3), § 666 BGB).
en.example: Example: €8,000 accounts + €4,200 assets + €300 unpaid fees − €1,190 unpaid invoices = €11,310.

en.name: Deactivate Nextcloud accounts automatically?
en.text: When a role or membership ends, access to the Nextcloud should end too, otherwise a former board member keeps reading minutes and lists (Art. 32 GDPR). Automatically this happens without your doing, but needs a service account in the Nextcloud. Without the switch you have to block accounts there by hand.

en.name: Which obligations should you enter?
en.text: Typical ones are the tax return, which the tax office usually requests from non-profit clubs every three years (§ 149 AO), and registering a new board with the register court (§ 67 BGB). Add deadlines from contracts, insurance and grants that are in no law. A reminder with a responsible person ensures that a deadline is not forgotten even after a change of board.

en.name: When does a term of office end?
en.text: How long a board office lasts is not set by law but by the constitution (§ 27(1), § 58 no. 3 BGB). Enter the end if the constitution names a fixed term; when it ends, the rights of the role lapse. Whether the board stays in office until the next election is likewise governed only by the constitution.

en.name: Open till (offene Ladenkasse)
en.text: Cash box without a cash register, for example at the drinks stand; the day's takings are worked back at the end from the counted balance (§ 146(1) AO). This requires a count record.
en.example: Example: closing balance €1,850.00, float €200.00, ice cream paid in cash €50.00: day's takings €1,700.00.

en.name: Opening balance with cut-off date?
en.text: The opening balance is the account balance on the cut-off date from which you book in HUBIplan, usually the start of the financial year. Take it from the bank statement or the last treasurer's report; an estimated value is quicker but carries through every later report as a difference. The board's duty to account requires a complete statement of income and expenses (§ 259(1) BGB).

en.name: Opening balance (Anfangsbestand)
en.text: Money in an account or the cash box at the start of the period, usually the previous year's closing balance. It is the starting point of every cash calculation.
en.example: Example: opening balance €4,250.00 on 1 January: this much was in the current account before the year began.

en.name: Objection (Widerspruch)
en.text: A member can unsubscribe from information emails such as circulars; HUBIplan then no longer sends them by email. An objection to advertising by email is possible at any time (Art. 21(2) and (3) GDPR).
en.example: Example: 6 of 120 members have unsubscribed: the circular goes to 114 addresses.

en.name: open (offen)
en.text: The part of an invoice not yet paid: invoice amount minus all recorded payments. The member still owes this remainder (§ 362(1) BGB).
en.example: Example: invoice €72.00, paid €36.00, open €36.00: half is still missing.

en.name: overdue (überfällig)
en.text: An invoice whose due date has passed and on which something is still open. Whether the member is already in default also depends on a reminder or a note on the invoice (§ 286 BGB).
en.example: Example: 9 of 142 invoices overdue, together €648.00: time for the reminder.

en.name: What belongs in a written mandate?
en.text: A mandate states, among other things, payer, IBAN, creditor ID, mandate reference, date and signature (EPC016-06). Keep the original as long as you collect on it and queries are possible afterwards; HUBIplan stores mandates from the member area itself. Without proof, the club must refund a disputed direct debit up to 13 months later (§§ 675u, 676b(2) BGB).
en.section: Direct debit → mandates → record written mandate

en.name: May the club show the logo?
en.text: Someone else’s logo can be protected as a trade mark or as a work (§ 14 MarkenG, § 15 UrhG). Show it only with the partner’s consent and in the version they give you. Ideally record the consent in the agreement with the partner.
en.section: Website → home page → “Partners and sponsors” section

en.name: Store private individuals as business partners?
en.text: The club may store a private individual’s data as far as it needs them for a contract with or an enquiry from that person (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR). Name, address and one way of contact are usually enough. Once the business is done and no retention period is running, delete the entry (Art. 17(1)(a) GDPR).

en.name: Passkey
en.text: Sign-in with a key pair instead of a password; the secret part stays on your own device. It cannot be guessed or captured on fake pages and is thus a state-of-the-art safeguard (Art. 32(1) GDPR).
en.example: Example: The treasurer signs in with her fingerprint on the phone; she no longer has to remember a 12-character password.

en.name: Payer
en.text: Person or body that pays a member’s fee and receives the invoice. This can be the member themselves, a parent, the household or an employer.
en.example: Example: the mother pays for 2 children: both fees are on her invoice and are collected from her account.

en.name: Payment reference
en.text: Text the payer adds to a transfer. If it contains the invoice number, the incoming payment is easy to match to the right invoice.
en.example: Example: “RE 2026-0041 fee Muster”: the €60.00 belong to invoice 2026-0041.

en.name: Report by name or only numbers?
en.text: Numbers are enough for fees and statistics; the association needs reports by name, for example for honours or eligibility to compete. Names may only be passed on if the constitution or membership of the association provides for it (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) and no more than necessary (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR). Also name the association as a recipient in the privacy notice.

en.name: Why record the programme?
en.text: Anyone performing protected music in public needs prior consent, which is usually granted by GEMA (§ 19(2) UrhG, § 42(1) VGG). After the event it generally requires a list of the works played (§ 42(2) VGG). With the programme recorded at the performance, this set list already exists.

en.name: Personal data shared or per unit?
en.text: Maintained jointly, an address changes everywhere at once, so data stays correct (Art. 5(1)(d) GDPR). In return several units see and change the same data, which requires clear agreements on responsibility (Art. 26 GDPR). Separate copies per unit separate responsibility but lead to diverging versions.

en.name: Photos only with consent?
en.text: A photo makes recognition on the ID card easier but shows a person recognisably. For this the club usually needs their consent; it is voluntary and can be withdrawn at any time, after which the photo must go (§ 22 KUG, Art. 6(1)(a), Art. 7(3) GDPR). The ID card also works without a photo, so only ask if it really helps.

en.name: How many days of pre-notification?
en.text: Before each collection you announce amount and date, under the SEPA rulebook 14 calendar days in advance unless otherwise agreed (EPC016-06). A shorter period speeds up the run but only applies if it is stated in the mandate or the fee terms. Without such an agreement, use 14 days.

en.name: Pre-notification (Vorabankündigung)
en.text: Notice to the payer of the amount and date of a collection, 14 calendar days in advance unless otherwise agreed (EPC016-06). It can also be on the invoice or apply once for several identical collections.
en.example: Example: collection on 15 March, notice by 1 March at the latest: the member can make sure the account is in funds.

en.name: Pro rata fee when joining during the period?
en.text: Pro rata means: whoever joins or leaves during the period only pays for the started parts, as chosen months, quarters or half-years. Per month seems fairest but gives odd amounts; quarters and half-years give round amounts. If the constitution or fee regulations say nothing, the board should decide on a rule and apply it equally to all (§ 58 no. 2 BGB).

en.name: Create events and series?
en.text: If you assign bookings to an event, you see its result and can compare it over the years in a series. This shows which festival pays for itself and provides figures for the limit in the commercial operation (§ 64(3) AO). It is worth the effort for festivals with many bookings; for small occasions the category is enough.

en.name: Special-purpose operation (Zweckbetrieb)
en.text: A business operation that directly fulfils the statutory purpose and cannot be achieved otherwise. It remains tax-privileged like the non-profit sphere (§§ 64(1), 65 AO).
en.example: Example: entry fees for the club competition, €650.00: the event itself serves the club's purpose.

en.name: Record only that it was inspected?
en.text: For the extended certificate of good conduct, the club may only record that it inspected it, the date of the certificate and whether there is a relevant conviction (§ 72a Abs. 5 SGB VIII). The certificate itself is not copied or uploaded, and the data must be deleted at the latest six months after the activity ends. An expiry date is only worthwhile for certificates that really expire, such as first aid (Art. 5 Abs. 1 lit. c GDPR).

en.name: Document (Beleg)
en.text: Evidence for an entry, e.g. invoice, receipt or bank statement. Accounting documents must be kept for eight years (§ 147(1) no. 4, (3) AO).
en.example: Example: entry 2026-0117 “Festival drinks” €412.30 with the scanned invoice from the drinks supplier.

en.name: Show VAT on the receipt?
en.text: Only if the payment belongs to a VAT-liable area and the club is not a small business (§ 19 UStG). Whoever shows tax without being entitled to owes it to the tax office anyway (§ 14c(2) UStG). Up to €250 a small-amount invoice with the tax rate instead of the tax amount is enough (§ 33 UStDV).

en.name: A document for every entry?
en.text: Without a document an entry cannot be proven at the cash audit or to the tax office; the principle is “no entry without a document” (GoBD). Accounting documents must be kept for eight years (§ 147(1) no. 4, (3) AO). Uploading the document straight away with the entry takes a moment but saves searching before the closing.

en.name: Register court and register number (Registergericht, Registernummer)
en.text: A registered association is entered in the register of associations at the local court, under a number with “VR”. Both belong in the legal notice (§ 21 BGB, § 5(1) no. 4 DDG).
en.example: Example: Amtsgericht Neuss, VR 1234.

en.name: Rejoining
en.text: Someone was a member before and joins again. The earlier period stays in the file and counts towards the membership duration, the gap in between does not.
en.example: Example: member from 1998 to 2010, rejoined in 2014: in 2026 that makes 24 years in total.

en.name: Why does reopening a closing need a reason?
en.text: A closed year is the basis for the cash audit and discharge; if it is reopened, it must remain visible what applied before (§ 146(4) AO, GoBD). That is why the old state is kept with reason, person and time, and when closing again you see the differences. Only reopen a closing for real errors, such as a forgotten document, and inform the cash auditors.

en.name: Reserve (Rücklage)
en.text: Part of the funds that the club sets aside for a purpose without moving money (§ 62 AO). It is then no longer freely available.
en.example: Example: €3,000.00 of €8,000.00 in the accounts are tied up as “Reserve refrigerated trailer”; €5,000.00 is freely available.

en.name: When does the club need a reserve?
en.text: A tax-privileged club must in principle use its funds by the end of the year after next; clubs with income of up to €100,000 a year are exempt from this (§ 55(1) no. 5 AO). Whoever saves for a project, such as a larger purchase or an anniversary festival, creates a reserve for it (§ 62(1) AO). Reserves make saving traceable but tie up money and need a decision with a purpose.

en.name: Responsible for the content (Verantwortlich für den Inhalt)
en.text: Person who takes responsibility for journalistic and editorial content such as reports and news, with name and address (§ 18(2) MStV). Usually the chair or the press officer.
en.example: Example: “Responsible under § 18(2) MStV: Erika Muster, Hauptstraße 1, 41468 Neuss”.

en.name: Result (Ergebnis)
en.text: All income minus all expenses of a period or event, without transfers. A negative result means the club paid in from reserves or balances.
en.example: Example: result 2026: +€900.00: the club took in €900.00 more than it spent during the year.

en.name: When may old treasury data go?
